News.title: Moment cocaine-fuelled thug ‘celebrates’ knocking innocent party-goer unconscious after unprovoked brawl outside club
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment a thug “celebrated” knocking an innocent party-goer unconscious after an unprovoked brawl on a night out.

Jayden Swift, 19, was captured grappling with the man in Barnsley, South Yorkshire, after a night of drinking and taking drugs.



The victim had come to the aid of another man who Swift had initially punched 20 times and left unconscious just moments before.

Footage showed the pair exchanging blows on the pavement before moving on to a main road in the city centre.



Swift then caught the innocent man with a brutal punch to the back of his head – causing him to collapse to the floor.

The thug then unleashes a savage kick to the man’s head while he is on the ground, knocking him unconscious.

He was filmed kicking the man’s head again before celebrating over his victim’s limp body by putting his arms in the air.

The yob continues to taunt him by standing over him and pointing as his own nose streams with blood.



Before attempting to leave the scene, Swift landed one more vicious kick to the man’s head.

Sheffield Crown Court heard the brawl erupted aftr Swift had a brief conversation with the first victim before launching into the “unprovoked, senseless and serious” attack.

The victim in that attack suffered injuries to his head, and above his eye and temple along with a blackened eye.

Swift’s second victim was left with bruising to his left eye and scalp, along with grazing to the left side of his head.

The thug pleaded guilty to two counts of attempting to cause grievous bodily harm with intent, in relation to the incident on January 11, 2026.



He was jailed for four years and one month and granted a 10-year restraining order protecting both men.

News.title: Afghan nationals including 17-year-old boy jailed for raping girl, 17, in depraved attack before 3 fled UK in lorry
News.content:
BEHIND BARS Afghan nationals including 17-year-old boy jailed for raping girl, 17, in depraved attack before 3 fled UK in lorry







Next

FOUR Afghan nationals including a 17-year-old boy have been jailed for raping a teen girl after plying her with vodka.

Mehrab Safi, 21, Awal Ahmadzai and Salman Habibkheil, both 19, and the schoolboy – then aged 16 – attacked the girl in Bristol.



Safi, Ahmadzai and Habibkheil fled the UK three days later in the back of a lorry but were discovered by the French authorities in Calais.

The fiends have now been jailed after being convicted of a string of sex offences.



Safi, who was found guilty of one count of human trafficking and two charges of rape, was jailed for 15 years.

Habibkheil was convicted of one count of human trafficking and one charge of rape, while Ahmadzai was found guilty of one charge of rape and one of assault by penetration.



They were both sentenced to nine years in a youth detention centre.

The 17-year-old boy, who cannot legally be named, was convicted of one charge of rape and jailed for two years and seven months in a youth detention centre.

In a victim impact statement, the girl said the attack had left her “traumatised”.

She added: “If I ever leave the house, it is only with my best friend or mum. I would not be able to go out by myself, even the thought of that makes me panic.



“Generally my brain keeps blocking out the trauma that happened to me, but when I am feeling low emotionally it all comes back and makes me feel even worse.

“Sometimes I would dream about what happened, which I was not expecting – and I do not like those dreams at all.”

Jurors heard the girl had been out with a friend Christmas shopping when they got talking to Safi, who they had not met before.



He later asked her to add him on social media platform Snapchat before requesting nude photographs of her on November 28.

Two days later, Safi arranged for a taxi to take her from her home in Somerset to Bristol in the early hours.

She was initially dropped off in an industrial area of the city, where Safi was waiting with Habibkheil, before they got into another taxi which took them to a house in the St Werburghs area.

Once there, she was provided with cigarettes and vodka before being raped by Safi and his co-defendants, Bristol Crown Court heard.

Ed Hetherington, prosecuting, said: “The prosecution say that they sexually abused a young girl who Mr Safi had met and began grooming only days before the rapes took place.



“On November 30 last year, Mr Safi and Mr Habibkheil arranged for her to be brought by taxi to meet them in Bristol in the early hours of a Sunday morning.

“Once she arrived, she was taken to a home in St Werburghs and she was very quickly expected to have sex with Mr Safi.

“She didn’t want to, not yet, but it happened anyway.”

The court was told after she was raped by Safi, the other three defendants “took it in turns to get her alone in a bedroom or in a bed and to have sex with her against her wishes”.

Mr Hetherington said she was “plied with alcohol and cigarettes to secure her compliance”.



He added: “She was alone.

“She was isolated in an unfamiliar city miles from home, in the dead of night, with a house full of men she didn’t know.

“We say she was raped and she was abused repeatedly over a period of several hours.”

Jurors were told the sex attack ended when the girl’s mother contacted police.

Officers traced the girl to the house and arrested the 17-year-old defendant when he answered the door.



The three older co-accused fled the house as the police arrived and travelled to both Birmingham and London.

Mr Hetherington said: “You might have heard reports from time to time about people concealing themselves in the back of a lorry and crossing the Channel.

“In a deeply unusual turn of events, the defendants Safi, Habibkheil and Ahmadzai, chose to use this mode of transportation to leave the UK rather than enter.

“Unfortunately for them, they were discovered by the French police in Calais.”

They were then returned to the UK and immediately arrested by the police on suspicion of rape.



Mobile phone footage recovered from Safi’s phone showed the three defendants in the back of the lorry with Habibkheil making hand gestures to the camera and laughing, and Ahmadzai having a lie down.

Detective Chief Inspector Matt Cable of Avon and Somerset Police, speaking after the case, said: “These four people exploited a vulnerable young girl purely for the purposes of their own sexual gratification.

“They are dangerous individuals who pose a significant threat to young women and girls and gave not a single thought to the welfare of the victim.”

Sally Helliwell, of the Crown Prosecution Service, said: “The young victim in this case was targeted, groomed, and then lured to an unfamiliar city, miles from home in the dead of night.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Isolated and alone, she was plied with alcohol and then raped and abused over several hours by four different people. It was clear throughout that she did not consent.



“Thankfully, the three men who fled in such a cowardly manner were swiftly returned to the UK to face justice.”

News.title: Billionaire & his wife killed in fireball chopper crash ‘had heads eaten by animals’ after bodies left at site for hours
News.content:
FAMILY’S AGONY Billionaire & his wife killed in fireball chopper crash ‘had heads eaten by animals’ after bodies left at site for hours







Next

THE heads of a billionaire and his wife are feared to have been eaten by animals after they died in a horror fireball plane crash.

Wicknell Chivayo and his partner Lucy Muteke were killed inside the doomed aircraft that plunged to the ground in Zimbabwe just 40 minutes after take-off.



In a grim turn of events, the couple will be buried without their heads after animals scavenged their remains, which had been left at the scene overnight, according to a lawyer.

Family spokesman, Herbert Chivayo, said their headless bodies were “beyond recognition”.



He said: “The bodies were burnt until the fire died on its own, so you can imagine what the status is like.”

Former Zimbabwean opposition politician and lawyer Fadzayi Mahere has criticised the country’s emergency response and questioned whether enough was done to recover missing body parts.

She alleged the helicopter crashed at about 5pm but that the victims’ bodies remained at the scene until around 8am the following morning.

Fadzayi wrote: “When we say fix the nation’s emergency services, this is what we mean.



“The helicopter crash happened at around 5pm. The deceased persons’ bodies were left outside to be ravaged by the elements and stolen by wild animals and ‘wild animals’ until around 8am, the next day.

“Why are they now surprised that crucial body parts, including the heads of the deceased persons, are missing?”

She added: “Every person who has passed away in a tragedy deserves dignity.



“To be buried with such an important body part must be grueling for those who remain. Was there an active search to recover them?”

The couple are due to be buried side by side at Glen Forest Cemetery in Harare on Thursday.

The cause of the crash remains under investigation but it is understood it went down following a massive blaze.

All six people on board died.

Wicknell had become one of Zimbabwe’s best-known businessmen and was known for highly publicised gifts to football clubs, churches, musicians, journalists and social media influencers.



He and Lucy had reportedly been returning to Harare after visiting the construction site of a new rural mansion when the helicopter went down..

Billionaire Wicknell had built his huge fortune through several business ventures including energy and infrastructure projects in Zimbabwe.

His popularity saw him regularly hand out expensive gifts, including cars, to celebrities to help boost his online fame.

His business dealings and political links had previously attracted controversy across Africa.

Among his biggest business ventures was a £128m solar power project in Gwanda awarded to his company Intratrek Zimbabwe by the state-owned Zimbabwe Power Company.



Wicknell had always denied wrongdoing over allegations linked to his business dealings.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Kenya’s President William Ruto paid tribute to Wicknell as a “dear friend”.

He said: “I will remember him for his friendship, his energy and his deep conviction in the possibilities of our continent.”

News.title: Bin lorry smashes into house & three cars in trail of destruction as ‘drug driver’, 44, is arrested
News.content:
CRASH CARNAGE Bin lorry smashes into house & three cars in trail of destruction as ‘drug driver’, 44, is arrested







Next

A BIN lorry has smashed into three cars and before ploughing into a house as a man was rushed to hospital.

An alleged drug driver, 44, was arrested at the scene in Cleveleys, Lancashire, on Friday.



Firefighters freed a man from one of the vehicles while police sealed off the surrounding area.

It is understood the rubbish lorry first collided with a moving car before hitting two parked vehicles and smashing into the house.



A grey Mercedes and red Seat were among three cars damaged in the smash, with both left so badly wrecked they had to be lifted onto recovery trucks.

Cops said the bin wagon’s driver, a 44-year-old man from Blackpool, was arrested on suspicion of drug driving.

Lancashire Fire and Rescue Service Station Manager Kevin Warwick said: “Fire service operations took place and we extricated one male casualty who’s currently being assessed at Blackpool Victoria Hospital.

“One of the vehicles involved was a bin wagon which unfortunately impacted a domestic property. Operations are ongoing to assess the stability of that property moving forward.”

News.title: Is Putin edging Nato into all-out war? Tyrant’s new tactic to push alliance to brink with drone blitz on Black Sea ships
News.content:
Next

VLADIMIR Putin is testing Nato’s red lines with a calculated campaign designed to push the alliance towards breaking point, an expert has warned.

It comes after drones blasted two merchant ships off Bulgaria just a day after another vessel sank near Romania in a suspected Russia attack.



Two crew members were severely injured as one ship sank within minutes and another erupted in flames.

Several sailors remain missing in the Black Sea.



Crucially, the drones struck inside Nato member Bulgaria’s Exclusive Economic Zone – bringing the attack alarmingly close to the alliance’s doorstep.

It is not yet clear who launched the drones.



Now experts are warning Russia has been deliberately probing Nato to discover exactly how far it can go before the alliance hits back.

British military veteran and intelligence expert Justin Crump told The Sun: “They’re steadily testing NATO and NATO member countries’ boundaries around their response to a lot of incidents that fall sub a threshold of what would almost certainly trigger an Article 4 or an Article 5 response.”

He said Moscow’s tactics were no accident, but part of a gradual ratcheting up of pressure against the West.

Justin added: “This is carefully calibrated by Russia. And actually what you see is a creeping progression of the sorts of actions they do to test the alliance.



“What Russia is trying to do is work out where those thresholds really are.

“How can they increase the cost to Europe of supporting Ukraine?

“How can they increase public pressure over the war in Ukraine in Russia’s favour without triggering a clear Article 4 or Article 5 response?”



Article 4 allows Nato members to demand consultations when they believe their security is threatened.

Article 5 is the alliance’s collective defence principle under which an armed attack against one member is considered an attack against them all.

The expert warned the Kremlin was effectively trying to operate in the dangerous space beneath those thresholds.

He said: “They’re constantly threading that line. And as they become more bold, of course, the risk gradually increases.”

The danger, he warned, is that Russia eventually pushes too far.



Justin said: “The risk is that they miscalculate and they do something potentially in the Baltics that is strong enough that it really does invite a reaction, demand a reaction from nations that Russia may not have expected.”

The stark warning came after the Alfa Watan was struck around 80 miles off the Bulgarian coast and immediately sank.

A second vessel, the Able, was seriously damaged after another strike sparked a huge fire on board, forcing all 18 crew members to abandon ship.

Rescue teams managed to pull them from the water, with several injured sailors treated aboard the Bulgarian ferry Dioscuria.

Two crew members suffered severe injuries, including burns, and were flown to hospital.



Eleven of those rescued are Turkish and seven are Indian, according to Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev.

Distress signals were sent out at around 4am local time – and by 9am one vessel had disappeared from Border Police radar.

Rescuers raced towards the sunken ship but found only life jackets floating in the water, with none of its missing crew recovered so far.



Radev condemned the strikes as a “flagrant attack on maritime law”.

He said: “Such an attack within Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone is absolutely unacceptable.

“Two merchant vessels were attacked by sea and air drones.”

Bulgaria has called an emergency meeting of defence ministers and officials following the strikes.

The Alfa Watan had been carrying wheat to the Romanian port of Sulina, according to ship-tracking website VesselFinder and official statements.



The Able was flying under the flag of Palau, although it remains unclear where it was heading or what cargo it was carrying.

Rumen Nikolov, director of the Maritime Rescue Coordination Center, told Bulgarian public radio: “The crew of one ship is missing, while the sailors from the second vessel have been rescued.”

The strikes are the first attacks on vessels recorded inside Bulgaria’s Exclusive Economic Zone.

Justin said Romania and Bulgaria could be particularly attractive targets for Russian pressure because of their geography and Moscow’s historic understanding of the region.

He said: “There is an argument that Romania and Bulgaria, elements of society, they’re much more laissez-faire towards Russia.



“They’re not particularly in favour of Ukraine necessarily. They’re easier targets for Russia.”

He added: “It’s not surprising to see these things on that southern flank.”

Justin said the pressure was part of a much wider Russian playbook stretching beyond conventional military force.



“All of it is effectively hybrid warfare,” he said.

“Some of it more diplomatic, some of it more economic, some of it more military.”

The Black Sea strikes also expose a major headache for Nato – detecting and destroying cheap drones before they can reach hugely valuable civilian ships.

The expert added that the said European defences had not been designed for the explosion in cheap, slow-moving weapons now transforming warfare.

“We have been a bit negligent about our tracking of threats in our airspace,” he said.



“Slow drones are therefore often excluded from what a radar would automatically see.”

He added: “We just haven’t really got a very joined up air defence system over Europe because we didn’t need it.”

That leaves merchant vessels particularly exposed when drones skim towards them at low altitude.

Crump said: “No one’s quite found the right formula yet fully to defend against smaller drones.

“They’re coming in slow, they’re coming in low, they’re attacking vessels that haven’t got the sensor systems to deal with it.”



And arming civilian vessels presents its own problems, leaving commercial shipping caught in a dangerous gap between civilian and military protection.

Crump warned: “Until merchant ships can become armed vessels you’re always going to have a gap in how they can defend themselves and, as in many other conflicts, they therefore make easy targets.”

The latest chaos came just a day after a Turkish-owned cargo ship was left sinking and ablaze off Romania, killing two people.

The vessel had been carrying grain from Ukraine to Italy when it was hit in a drone attack.

Romanian officials did not confirm who was responsible, but Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky blamed the Kremlin.



Since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, drones have repeatedly breached the airspace of European countries, while the Black Sea has become an increasingly dangerous arena for commercial shipping.

For Justin, fears the possibility that repeated provocations could slowly become accepted as normal.

“They’ve got away with a lot of operations over a long period of time in our nations without eliciting significant reactions,” he said.

And he warned Nato faces an increasingly perilous balancing act as Moscow searches for the point at which the alliance will finally refuse to back down.

Justin said: “The more you shove, the more chance there is that something you think NATO will let go or nations will let go becomes the issue that we just don’t let go.”



He added: “They’re doing it for a reason, they’ll keep doing it without doubt.

“They’ll keep pushing what they’re doing and their hope is eventually they’ve created a new normal where we accept what they’re doing.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But every new test carries the risk that one strike, incursion or miscalculation finally crosses the line Moscow has spent years trying to locate.

Justin warned: “We are going into a pretty dangerous period and not really very prepared for it.”

News.title: I defended 400 death row lags and saw gashed arms, dud drugs & poison from backroom UK lab…Christa Pike mess is no shock
News.content:
Next

LYING in an unconscious state, breathing only thanks to a ventilator machine and with “swollen, burned and blistered arms”, Satanic killer Christa Pike is barely clinging to life.

The 50-year-old survived two botched attempts to execute her by lethal injection last Wednesday, in Tennessee, leaving the world including President Donald Trump to question: “How does that happen? It should be easy to do.”





Murderer Pike was sentenced to death for butchering 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in 1995. But instead of the ‘lethal’ injection sending her to sleep before her brain was starved of oxygen, resulting in her death, Pike survived.

In a disturbing two-hour ordeal, viewers in the gallery observed mixed reactions from the killer ranging from “a joyous laugh and chuckle” and a “loud snore like an old man sleeping” to crying, whimpering and “a significant gasp for air”.

By 8.53pm, unconscious but still alive, Pike was ushered to hospital where she was intubated, put on a ventilator and had doctors battle to save her life – potentially so that she can be put to death again.

In the past 50 years, the US has executed around 1,700 people – including 29 this year – via methods ranging from the gas chamber to electric chair and lethal injection – which leads to the question: what went wrong?

Cambridge-born human rights lawyer Clive Stafford Smith, 67, specialises in the death penalty, and has watched six of his clients being put to death – two of whom died by injected poison.

He told The Sun that the fatal drugs are often “sub-optimal, either out of date or don’t work” and that qualified doctors are barred from taking part so executioners administering them have no medical training. As a last resort, some even slice open the condemned prisoner’s arms to stick the IV drip inside.





The exact reasons for the failing in Pike’s case are yet to be fully discovered. Tennessee governor Bill Lee has ordered an independent review and halted executions until the end of the year.

Clive suspects the IV line, which delivers the fatal dose of pentobarbital, “slipped out at least twice”, which in part is due to it being incorrectly inserted into her veins.

It’s known that one needle became bent at a 90-degree angle and had to be yanked during the two-plus hour execution. Pike also was hit with a double dose of poison.

At one point, Pike herself remarked “a vein in my arm feels like it’s about to burst open” and a minute later complained: “One spot is really throbbing.”

Pike’s former lawyer James Crowson remarked “I can’t say I’m surprised” that the execution was botched, noting that her “compromised veins” were an issue known about by the State.

He continued: “[It] was going to be a difficult and perhaps cruel procedure for her because it was going to put her at risk for exactly what happened.”

Clive tells us it is “pretty obvious when an execution has been botched” and claims “it’s pretty frequent” for three main reasons – the first, being the executioner.

He explains: “Doctors, nurses and medical professionals are barred from taking part in executions by the Hippocratic oath.”

This is an ethical vow they take after completing medical training which bars them from causing intentional harm, injury or suffering. They are then duty-bound to do all they can to keep someone in their care alive.

This means that death penalty executioners have to volunteer – although they are paid. Previously an electrician who operated the electric chair told Clive he received $300 (£250) a time. But in states where lethal injection is used many are inexperienced and low paid prison staff.



Clive adds: “Veins are hard to get at the best of times, let alone with someone who had very thin and worn veins, caused by drug use, like Christa.

“The people they use are not qualified to do this, not really trained, they don’t have experience and don’t really know what they are doing.

“They would have a hard time getting someone to practise finding veins on, so I suspect they are trained on mannequins, which isn’t real life.

“In one execution, they were prodding this guy with a needle for over an hour and ended up having to cut open his arm and put the IV line in there, it was barbaric.”

In the case of Thomas Creech, who survived a lethal injection in 2024, he was repeatedly stabbed 10 times with a needle before it was called off.

He later said: “The worst ones were when they got down to my ankles. I was thinking the whole time that this is really it. I’m dead. This is my day to die.”

Clive suspects the only qualification most lethal injection executioners have is “volunteering to do it”, which is “a really bad qualification”.

He claims details of the training of lethal injection executioners is “kept very secret and hidden behind secrecy laws” by individuals States because it “makes them look worse”.



Another issue, Clive alleges, is that “not very good, sub-optimal drugs” are used for the killing – sometimes they are incorrectly mixed, other times they are “out of date or don’t work”.

It is because US states have struggled to obtain the poison used to perform lethal injections since pharmaceutical firm Hospira stopped producing them back in 2011.

Clive adds: “Before that, Hospira used to sell them for 90 cents a vial. Making money off executions led to very bad publicity so they stopped making the original drugs.

“Hospira didn’t want the bad publicity from their drugs being used to kill people so they had to shop around the world, sometimes in dubious places.

“They tried all sorts of places, India, China, and compounding agencies, who are not manufacturers but can create the drugs out of the constituent parts.

“Bizarrely, there was also one opportunistic guy, who became a one-man pharmacy and operated from the back of a driving school in Acton, West London.

“None of these places are regulated. The states try to avoid all oversight for the drugs and when there is no oversight, making mistakes is inevitable.”

The British poison seller Clive referred to was Mehdi Alavi, who aged 50 in 2011, was found to be operating from the back room of E L Gone Driving School back in 2011.

It’s alleged his firm, Dream Pharma, produced the drug sodium thiopental which was then shipped to five US states. The charity Reprieve UK found the firm’s exports to California alone contained enough doses to be used in 85 executions.

Clive claims all of these labs are unregulated, so could be using out of date chemicals or mixing the deadly doses incorrectly – too much or too little could lead to agonising pain.



Back in the 2000s, there was a three drug protocol – first the condemned was injected with a sedative, followed by a paralytic and then a poison to kill them.

Clive adds: “The truth is the poison they used was extremely painful and so the paralytic used simply to prevent witnesses from seeing someone thrashing around in agony.

“Now pentobarbital does the job of all three and ends up poisoning you in the sense that it stops you from taking in oxygen until you are ultimately suffocated.

“We don’t understand if, when the person is asleep, they feel pain but at least they are not thrashing around because they are unconscious.”

Interestingly, Clive suspects Pike may not face the death penalty again due to there being “a moderate chance” that she is “brain damaged” to the point where she cannot legally face a third lethal injection.

He tells us: “There is a moderate chance that the poor woman will be brain damaged by what she went through.

“If she regains consciousness and is brain damaged to the point that she’s not competent then they won’t be able to try to kill her for a third time.

“If that’s the case, they will have to keep her in prison or a mental hospital for the rest of her life.”

Under Ford v Wainwright, a 1986 Supreme Court ruling, those considered insane or “mentally incompetent” cannot be executed.

The full details of Pike’s botched executions are yet to emerge – but few will forget her highly violent crimes, which fueled “Satanic panic” across the US.



In January 1995, the 18-year-old alongside her boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp, 17, and pal Shadolla Peterson, 18, carried out a “lengthy beating and torture” that resulted in death.

They stabbed Colleen Slemmer, 19, more than 100 times with a box cutter knife, carved a pentagram into her chest and Pike took a section of her caved-in skull as a grizzly souvenir.

It’s claimed that Pike instigated her kidnap from a university campus and attacked her fearing Colleen was trying to steal her partner. She was found dead and naked from the waist up.

Pike was sentenced to death the following year and has remained in solitary confinement on death row for 27 years in a cell the size of a car parking space.

While Pike has insisted there is “no excuse for what I did”, she had a highly troubled past. Clive describes her as “the victim of dozens of death penalty offences” herself.

Neurology Professor Dr Jonathan Pincus described an “almost unbearably abusive background” stemming from her birth and early years.

Pike was born with partial brain damage due to her mum drinking alcohol during pregnancy and from infancy onwards suffered seizures.

“She was molested by at least three people by the time she was three years old, then she was raped at 11 and violently raped again at 17 years old,” Clive says.



Her ex boyfriend Shipp regularly beat and kicked her, threatened her with a razor blade and allegedly cheated on her multiple times – including with future victim Colleen.

Clinical psychologist Dr Bethany Brand believed Pike had suffered “extraordinarily severe extreme trauma” and “more severe adverse events than 99 per cent of the US population.”

Many of them would argue, alongside her lawyers, that Pike – who was diagnosed with bipolar disorder post-conviction – was never fit to stand trial in the first place let alone now.

Currently unconscious, Pike’s fate very much still hangs in the balance and if she miraculously recovers from her deathly predicament, the State may very well try to kill her yet again.

News.title: Moment plane packed with tourists makes emergency landing after hitting ZEBRA during take-off as smoke billows from wing
News.content:
Next

THIS is the terrifying moment a packed tourist plane skids across the runway during an emergency landing after hitting a zebra.

The pilot was forced to divert during take-off after it was discovered that the plane’s gears had been damaged when it fatally struck the animal.



Dramatic footage shows smoke billowing from the wing as the plane’s underside skids across the runway in Tanzania.

The plane eventually screeched to a halt at the airport in Kilimanjaro, in the north of the country.



Emergency responders raced to the scene of the astonishing crash.

Miraculously all 26 passengers and four crew were able to safely disembark the plane.



No injuries were reported.

The plane struck and killed the zebra as it took off at an airport in the Serengeti National Park, a hotspot for tourists on safari.



The runway at Kilimanjaro International Airport – which is about 270 miles (430km) northwest from where the plane took off – was closed following the emergency landing.

The Serengeti National Park is home to between 200,000 and 300,000 zebras, as well as lions, elephants and leopards.

The animals are the most common species seen on safari in the nature reserve.

Zebras, and other species seen in the national park including wildebeests, take part in the great migration, the largest continuous animal movement on earth.

The plane had been on course for Zanzibar, on Tanzania’s coast, when it was forced to make the emergency landing on Sunday.



Tanzania’s civil aviation authority has launched an investigation into the incident.

Collisions between planes and wild animals have been known to occur in Africa, especially at remote airports.

In 2020, a commercial aircraft hit a wildebeest while landing at airstrip at a nature reserve in Kenya.

A plane was forced to make an emergency landing when it hit a warthog in Zimbabwe in 2009.

In another animal-related aviation accident, a penguin caused a helicopter to crash in South Africa when it burst out of a cardboard box on a passenger’s lap and knocked the controls.

News.title: We’ll cut Labour’s ‘Jobs Tax’ in half for young Brits to get them into work, Kemi vows – as she reveals new rescue plan
News.content:
Next

KEMI Badenoch will slash Labour’s “Jobs Tax” in half for young people to help get them into work.

The Tory leader will unleash a rescue plan for people aged 21 to 24 years-old allowing them to get one foot on the career ladder.



Youth unemployment has soared to its highest level since 2014 with more than one million young people not earning or learning.

The starting cost for the move will be £3.2 billion but this will drop by nearly a billion pounds after fewer pay-outs on benefits and higher tax revenues.



Ms Badenoch told the BBC: “Young people have a much worse problem than everybody else. I’ve talked about the unemployment that’s skyrocketing.

“We’ve got to fix that. There’s a graduate recruitment crisis, and if young people don’t get a job early, that impacts their lifetime earnings.”



Lifetime earnings for a young person drop by £52,000 but it goes up to £293,000 for those who are out of work or education between 18 and 24.

The intervention to help young people comes as she addresses the party faithful in Birmingham tomorrow for the second time as leader.

She has vowed to halve the employers National Insurance on young people from 15 per cent to 7.5 per cent in the first stage of their rescue effort for young people.

The party say there are 60,000 more young people labelled as NEETs – not in education, employment or training – than when Labour came to power in July 2024.



The move to slash national insurance will cost £2.3 billion with the part saying its fully funded.

Labour imposed a national insurance raid at their first Budget which hit business for an eye-watering £25 billion.

All earnings for young people earning more than £50,270 will face the standard rate with the cut helping those starting in the work place.

The move will allow businesses to hold on to more of their cash amounting to £1,545 on average for every young worker.

The move would save bosses £1,484 for youngsters on the National Living Wage and £1,875 for the age cohort earning more than £30,0000.



The announcement comes as Andy Burnham awaits a review into youth inactivity written by Labour grandee Alan Milburn to land on his desk.

His recommendations are set to include mandatory work experience placements starting in primary school to give kids a taste of work.

The ex-Health Secretary will also call for hundreds of thousands of youngsters with mild anxiety, depression and ADHD to be given immediate support.

He sees this as stopping people becoming “trapped in the benefits system” instead of languishing for months or years without a diagnosis.

Shadow Chancellor Andrew Griffith added: “Labour are destroying the future of our young people.



“Their Jobs Tax, employment red tape and minimum wage hikes have seen an explosion in the cost of employing a young worker. We will fix that.”

John Foster, from the CBI, said: “Businesses want to give young people their first step on the jobs ladder — but right now it is simply too expensive to hire.

“The Conservatives are right to focus on cutting those costs, because if you want more jobs you have to give firms a reason to create them.

“But the bigger prize would be lowering the point at which employers start paying National Insurance, cutting the cost of entry-level jobs across the board and giving businesses more confidence to take a chance on young people.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But a Labour party spokesman said: “This is yet more fantasy economics from the Tories.



“Kemi Badenoch pretends to be on the side of young people but her party allowed nearly one million of the next generation to be locked out of work or training.



“It’s no surprise her Shadow Chancellor wants another unfunded tax cut given he co-wrote Liz Truss’ mini-Budget that crashed the economy. The Tories can never be trusted with Britain’s public finances or the life chances of young people again.”

News.title: Tanzania safari plane carrying 30 faces emergency after striking and killing zebra
News.content:
Tanzania safari plane carrying 30 faces emergency after striking and killing zebra

A Sindbard Air Embraer EMB-120ER flying from the Serengeti to Zanzibar diverted to Kilimanjaro International Airport after a zebra strike caused landing gear problems.

Plane makes emergency landing with 30 people onboard

A safari plane carrying 30 people was forced to make an emergency landing after striking and killing a zebra during take-off in Tanzania.

‌



‌



The Sindbard Air aircraft was carrying 26 passengers and four crew from Seronera to Zanzibar when it hit the animal on the runway in the Serengeti National Park at around 11.30am local time on Sunday, according to Aviation Herald.

‌



The aircraft was a 1990-built Embraer EMB-120ER Brasilia, registered 5H-HLL, Aviation Safety Network records show. The crew diverted towards Kilimanjaro International Airport after the collision but were unable to lower the aircraft’s main landing gear.

‌



The Embraer EMB-120 was eventually forced to land with its main gear up on runway 09 at Kilimanjaro. Dramatic footage showed smoke coming from the aircraft as its underside scraped along the runway during the landing.

View 2 Images A zebra was struck and killed by the safari plane during take-off in Tanzania. (Image: Youtube)

Emergency crews rushed to the plane after it came to a stop, with all 26 passengers and four crew members able to get off safely.

‌



All of the people onboard were unharmed, while the aircraft suffered substantial damage, Aviation Herald reported. The flight had been due to travel from Seronera Airstrip in the Serengeti National Park to Zanzibar.

Tanzanian aviation authorities have launched an investigation into the incident, while operations at Kilimanjaro International Airport were temporarily suspended following the emergency landing.

View 2 Images The runway at Kilimanjaro International Airport where the aircraft made its emergency landing. (Image: Google)

Article continues below

It has not yet been officially confirmed whether the collision with the zebra directly caused the landing gear problem.

Seronera Airstrip is one of the main airstrips serving the Serengeti National Park and handles local flights carrying visitors to and from the reserve.

Around 500,000 tourists visit the Serengeti each year.

News.title: Tory members raise doubts over Kemi Badenoch's climate plans after summer heatwaves
News.content:
Tory members raise doubts over Kemi Badenoch's climate plans after summer heatwaves

At the Conservative party conference, some Tory members voiced concerns over Kemi Badenoch's climate change strategy after Britain was ravaged by extreme weather this summer

View 2 Images Kemi Badenoch has said she believes climate change is 'real' but has criticised a ban on new drilling in the north sea, as well as the UK’s target to achieve net zero (Image: Getty Images)

Tory members have voiced concerns over Kemi Badenoch's climate change strategy after Britain was ravaged by extreme weather this summer.

‌



‌



At the Conservative's annual conference in Birmingham, the Conservatives have vowed to scrap Natural England and the Environment Agency, on top of its long-established plans to ditch Net Zero targets.

‌



But a summer of heatwaves and wildfires, with El Nino on the way this winter, has left some Tories worried about the party’s strategy.

‌



David Stinson, a Tory member based in London, told the Mirror: “I think climate change is a huge issue, and I do think we need to take it really seriously. Look at what happened this summer, and look at today. The weather's amazing. It shouldn't be this amazing right now. So I do think we need to start taking it more seriously. So maybe that's one policy that I'm not aligned with.”

Tories and Labour go to war with spoof Bayeux Tapestry mock-ups READ MORE :

View 2 Images The Conservatives have vowed to scrap Natural England and the Environment Agency (Image: Phil Lewis/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

Luke O’Hara, a Tory member based in East Grinstead and Uckfield, said he was not convinced by Ms Badenoch’s strategy on climate change.

‌



He told The Mirror: “The Conservatives will have their reasons for scrapping net zero, scrapping all of this sort of stuff, and that's perfectly justifiable. But what I really haven't seen is any policy towards climate change. You can say: ‘Oh well, scrapping net zero is unrealistic.’ Okay, fine, but what are you going to do to prevent climate change, etc?

"That's the one thing I really haven't seen. The stuff about drilling oil and gas. That's the one policy I'm just not with them on. It won't change prices… basic economics tells you that. Sorry, Kemi, I love you, but that thing, I’m not convinced.”

Deanna Keene, a Tory member based in north London, added: “Even this time last year, I was in a thick cold, but this year I'm even without a coat.

‌



“We keep getting these droughts one minute, then we've got heavy rain and these wildfires coming from nowhere in areas you would never think would ever have that.

“I think it will take for something really drastic to happen, then that's the only time they might act. But it could be too late, so I'm hoping and praying that they will open their eyes and see what they need to do.”

Luke Tryl, More in Common’s executive director, told The Mirror the challenge for the Conservatives is setting out an alternative to net zero, if they’re scrapping the 2050 target to hit it.

‌



“There’s no doubt that worry about climate change is a big issue to voters. Regularly when we ask over two thirds of voters say that it's an issue that they are worried about and they want to see action on.

"Net zero itself is more split. So a group of voters who think net zero is the way to do it. You've got a group of voters who would like another way of tackling climate change. And I think the challenge for the Conservatives is if they're not doing net zero by 2050, but still saying, as I think maybe as Badenoch has, climate change is real. What's your alternative?

“And I think the pressure will grow to be like, how are you going to deal with this? Particularly after a summer when the heatwaves freaked people out"

‌



Ms Badenoch has said she believes climate change is “real” but has criticised a ban on new drilling in the north sea, as well as the UK’s target to achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050

The Tory leader told The Telegraph in July: Climate change is real. The net zero plans are not. They are a political fiction, bankrupting the country, destroying British industry and perversely increasing carbon emissions.

“Banning oil and gas drilling from Aberdeen, which has a low carbon footprint, only to import oil and gas from places that drill in a dirty fashion, makes no sense whatsoever.

Article continues below

“Conservatives care about the environment, clean energy and protecting our natural landscape. But that needs common sense.”

News.title: Asos hacked as company admits customer data 'may have been accessed'
News.content:
Asos said some personal data may have been accessed in a hack after customers received a bizarre push notification earlier today.

Asos hacked as company admits customer data 'may have been accessed'

Online fashion giant Asos is investigating a bizarre notification sent to customers earlier today, and admitted it has been hacked.

Asos does not believe payment-card information or passwords were impacted when a phone alert saying the company has been hacked was sent out to its millions.

However, some "basic personal information including name and contact details" may have been accessed.

The notification sent to app users was titled 'ASOS HACKED'. It read: "Dear Asos DPO and IT, we have fully compromised the Snowflake instance. Engage with us, or we will leak it."

The message, which contained a link to a Telegram chat, sparked concern among customers, with some rushing to delete their payment details.

News.title: British priest blasts Meghan Markle over her new eye-watering £112 Christmas advent calendar
News.content:
British priest blasts Meghan Markle over her new eye-watering £112 Christmas advent calendar

A priest has called out the Duchess of Sussex's new advent calendar over its luxury price and lack of 'the meaning of Christmas', resulting in a huge online row

View 3 Images Meghan's first advent calendar is on sale for £112 (Image: GETTY)

A priest has taken aim at Meghan Markle just days after the release of her luxury advent calendar, with his comments prompting a vicious online row.

‌



‌



Reverend Daniel French, a priest in the town of Salcombe, took to social media as he accused the Duchess of forgetting the true meaning of Christmas, following the release of her luxury calendar with a steep price point.

‌



Last week, Meghan announced her first advent calendar with her lifestyle brand As Ever, which features 24 luxury chocolates in collaboration with Los Angeles chocolatier Compartes and boasts an illustration of the Sussex's lavish Montecito mansion.

‌



Prince William teases hardman Ross Kemp and asks for Celebrity Traitors spoilers READ MORE :

3 View 3 Images Meghan Markle has released her brand's first advent calendar (Image: @aseverofficial/instagram) 3 View 3 Images Meghan's fans call themselves the 'Sussex squad' (Image: PA)

The inside of the box features the words ‘A magical celebration of the season’, and adds that the 24 handcrafted chocolates are there to ‘sweeten each day’ and have been ‘thoughtfully inspired by our Montecito garden’. The calendar will retail for £112, or $148USD, which equates to about £4.60 per chocolate.

After Meghan posted about the new product, Reverend French took to X as he offered an alternative calendar for those counting down to Christmas, with a much cheaper price point and a nook on the religious significance of the holiday.

‌



He wrote: “But for £5.99 you can pre order a Christian Advent Calendar with fairtrade chocolate from the Meaningful Chocolate Company. Donation is made to Leprosy Mission. Includes little booklet on the meaning of Christmas.”

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The pastor’s post was soon flooded with comments, who appeared to criticise the priest and branded him 'Satan spawn' and 'evil', while claiming he had an 'ugly heart'.

‌



The reverend’s friend and colleague Father Chris Phillips, whose parish is south-west London, jumped to French’s defence, which prompted another onslaught of messages, and eventually led to Father Phillips having to set his social media account to private. The Mirror has contacted Reverend French and Father Phillips for comment.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Rev French did however respond to one critic, who said: “Undoubtedly Rev you’re not her target audience. Nah I’ll stick with chocolate I’m familiar with. Comparte chocolate is it. Duchess Meghan products never fail me yet”, to which the priest simply responded: “Enjoy.”

Article continues below

The priest's comments come as Buckingham Palace has also released their own advent calendar just days after Meghan's, as the Royal Collection Trust unveiled its £12 advent calendar, which featured 24 days of milk chocolates.

The design of the advent calendar 'captures the magic of the festive season' with an illustration of a decorated Christmas tree which pays homage to the three royal residences: Buckingham Palace, Windsor Castle and the Palace of Holyroodhouse. Sitting on top of the illustrated tree is a crown, two Union flags and the ceremonial guardsmen who 'stand watch at these iconic locations'.

News.title: Police update after GP mum-of-three killed while hosting kids' sleepover
News.content:
Police update after GP mum-of-three killed while hosting kids' sleepover

Police are continuing to quiz a man, in his 40s, on suspicion of murdering a woman, named locally as mother-of-three Dr Hannah Terry

View 3 Images Dr Hannah Terry, also known as Hannah Cain, who has been named locally as the woman found dead in a £800,000 house in Norfolk (Image: East Anglia News Service)

Police officers are continuing to quiz a man on suspicion of murder, after a GP was found dead while hosting a children's sleepover.

The woman, named locally as mum-of-three Dr Hannah Terry, 45, was said to have welcomed friends of her children in her home when she died. Police were called to the house by the ambulance service shortly after 2.20am on Sunday and arrested a man on suspicion of murder after she was pronounced dead.

The man, who is also aged in his 40s, was still being quizzed by detectives today after police were granted extra time to question him. It is believed that children sleeping over at the house were taken back to their parents’ homes by officers in the early hours of Sunday.

View 3 Images Forensic units have been combing the property as police continue to quiz a man on suspicion of murder (Image: East Anglia News Service)

Murdered Leah Croucher's parents demand fresh law that may have stopped killer sex predator READ MORE :

White-suited forensic officers were today continuing to search the detached house where Dr Terry lived in Fern Hill, Dersingham, Norfolk. The house is surrounded by the 20,000 acre Sandringham estate and is just over a mile from Sandringham House.

Neighbours said they were shocked to hear of her death. Several bouquets of flowers were left on a verge outside the house today with one carrying a message, saying: “Such a tragic loss. A lovely, kind, caring neighbour and friend, but above all a devoted mum. God bless you Hannah and your precious boys.”

View 3 Images Officers have been using strimmers and other equipment as they look for evidence around the property (Image: East Anglia News Service)

Police could be heard today cutting back the property's garden with strimmers and other tools as they searched for clues. Potential evidence from the house was also seen being loaded up into the back of an unmarked police car.

Norfolk Police have not yet revealed the results of a post mortem by a Home Office pathologist which was due to be carried out yesterday to establish how she died. Dr Terry had worked part time as a GP for three days a week at the Grimston Medical Centre since last year, according to the surgery’s website.

The surgery remained closed today with only a dispensary service open for three hours for regular patients to collect urgent medication. A notice on the surgery’s website stated: “We are sorry to let patients know that Grimston Medical Centre, including the dispensary, is temporarily closed due to extremely difficult circumstances affecting our practice team.

“We apologise for the disruption and appreciate your patience and understanding at what is a very difficult time for our colleagues. If you have an appointment today, you will be contacted about alternative arrangements as soon as possible.”

A patient, paid tribute to her on Facebook on a post saying: “Fly high and sleep well dr terry.......you never deserved this to happen, heaven has gained an angel.........you was a lovely dr who listened to us and helped us.......thinking of you and your family and your children and friends and especially ALL staff & colleagues at Grimston medical centre xxxxx— feeling sad.”

Dr Terry was also a director of the Norfolk Sky Aesthetics , specialising in anti-wrinkle and fermal filler treatments. The GP had previously worked for nine years at the Heacham Group Practice in Norfolk until leaving last June “to allow her to spend more time with her young family”.

A statement on the practice’s website added: “We are all very sad to see her leave and are very grateful for all her hard work, support and advice over the last nine years. We wish her all the very best for the future.” One neighbour who asked not to be named said: “It is unbelievable what has happened. I am very upset about it. They are a lovely, lovely family.

“They had a huge field attached to their garden. They cut down some trees on it and were thinking of selling it as a building plot. They were active and always seemed busy. I would see her and the boys heading down to the village playing fields with their backpacks and tennis racquets."

A 95-year-old neighbour who asked not to be named said: “I never heard anything happening during the night and woke up on Sunday morning to see police cars everywhere."

Norfolk Police confirmed that the arrested man remained in custody at the police investigation centre in King’s Lynn, Norfolk. Police said a superintendents’ extension had been granted allowing him to be held for “an additional 12 hours for further investigation and questioning” on top of the 24 hours which police are normally allowed to keep an arrested person in custody.

This was followed by a further extension for an additional 32 hours granted by Great Yarmouth magistrates yesterday. The deadline ends late tonight, but officers are able to apply for further extensions and can hold a suspect in serious cases such as murder for up to 96 hours without charging them.

Det Insp Alix Wright, from the Norfolk & Suffolk Major Investigation Team, said: “We are in the very early stages of this investigation working to establish the exact circumstances surrounding the woman’s death. I’d ask anyone who believes they may have information that could help our investigation to please share this with us.”

One neighbour said of Dr Terry: “She was just a lovely human being with three gorgeous young children. I’m just out of words, we all are.”

An earlier Norfolk Police statement said: “Officers were called to a house in Fern Hill, Dersingham, shortly after 2.20am on Sunday 4 October by the ambulance service. Sadly, a woman aged in her 40s was pronounced dead at the scene shortly after police arrived.

Article continues below

“A man aged in his 40s was arrested on suspicion of murder and taken to King’s Lynn Police Investigation Centre for questioning. He remains in custody. Detectives from the Norfolk and Suffolk Major Investigation Team have launched a murder investigation.”

Dr Terry’s parents Stephen and Kathleen Terry also refused to comment at their home in Dersingham.

News.title: Man City charges LIVE: Punishment causes Premier League split as £300m 'catastrophe' looms
News.content:
Manchester City are still waiting to discover their punishment for being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules, though they have appealed the decision

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's live blog on Tuesday, October 6, where we will bring you the latest on the guilty verdict for Manchester City after breaching Premier League financial rules.

Last Tuesday, the Premier League confirmed that City had been found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges, stating that the club used 'sham' sponsorship deals to inflate their income by almost £900million during the nine-year period.

City, however, have denied any wrongdoing and appealed the decision last Thursday. The club believe they are "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League" and say they have "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" to support their case.

One argument City are said to be using during the appeal is that the extra funding came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the club's owners, Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), something which is allowed under Premier League rules. However, a statement from the main sponsors, Etihad, back in 2015, appears to contradict it.

There is still a lot of talk over what could happen. Stay right here for all of the latest...

News.title: Sussex Police officers who Tasered 92-year-old amputee at care home are sacked
News.content:
Sussex Police officers who Tasered 92-year-old amputee at care home are sacked

Two Sussex Police officers have been dismissed for gross misconduct after using a Taser, PAVA spray and a baton on 92-year-old amputee Donald Burgess at a care home in St Leonards-on-Sea.

Moment pensioner pepper sprayed and tasered by police

Two Sussex Police officers who Tasered a 92-year-old amputee at a care home have been sacked for using “excessive force”.

‌



‌



PC Stephen Smith and PC Rachel Comotto were dismissed without notice for gross misconduct after using a Taser, PAVA spray and a baton on Donald Burgess.

‌



The officers were called to a care home in St Leonards-on-Sea, East Sussex, on June 21, 2022, following reports that a resident had a knife and was threatening to stab staff.

‌



Body-worn camera footage showed PC Smith telling Mr Burgess: “Do you want to be sprayed or Tasered? It's up to you. Can you put that down for us?”

View 4 Images Donald Burgess, 92, was Tasered by Sussex Police officers at a care home in St Leonards-on-Sea. (Image: PA)

He then repeatedly told Mr Burgess to put the knife down, saying: “Put it down, Donald put it down. Seriously last chance. Donald put it down now, come on. Last chance.”

‌



Mr Burgess was then sprayed with PAVA. PC Smith could be heard saying: “Drop the knife, drop the knife, put it on the floor.”

PC Comotto also told him: “Do it now, drop the knife. Put it down.” The footage then faded as PC Comotto was heard shouting: “Taser, Taser.”

Within 90 seconds of arriving, PC Smith had also struck the arm holding the knife with a baton before PC Comotto discharged her Taser.

‌



View 4 Images Donald Burgess suffered from dementia (Image: IOPC)

Mr Burgess was handcuffed and taken to hospital by ambulance. He died on July 13, although a pathologist found the officers’ actions did not cause or contribute to his death.

A police disciplinary panel found both officers breached standards of professional behaviour relating to use of force, discreditable conduct and authority, respect and courtesy.

‌



They were dismissed without notice and will also be placed on the police barred list. The two officers had previously been acquitted of charges of assault occasioning actual bodily harm following a trial in May 2025.

View 4 Images PC Rachel Comotto was dismissed without notice for gross misconduct (Image: PA)

A further allegation against PC Comotto was also proven over a Facebook comment she made shortly after the incident.

‌



After a friend made a light-hearted remark about a birthday and “the care home getting closer and closer”, PC Comotto replied: “We all know what happens in care homes” followed by a lightning emoji.

IOPC Director of Engagement Emily Barry said: “This was not a fast-paced incident where the officers or other care home residents were in immediate danger. Mr Burgess, who was wheelchair bound and holding a cutlery knife, was isolated from other residents and clearly posed little risk to the officers.

View 4 Images PC Stephen Smith arriving at Westminster Magistrates’ Court. (Image: PA)

Article continues below

“Any use of force should have been a last resort and only used when necessary. Rather than de-escalating the situation they immediately threatened Mr Burgess with force and then discharged PAVA spray, struck him with a baton and Tasered him when he didn’t drop the knife.

“Their actions were clearly excessive and unreasonable and PC Comotto then displayed further poor judgement by joking about Tasering Mr Burgess on social media afterwards.

“Their actions have damaged the public’s trust and confidence in policing and they have been held accountable and dismissed from policing.”

News.title: Locals left fuming after council spends £47k of taxpayer cash on 'child like' mural
News.content:
Locals left fuming after council spends £47k of taxpayer cash on 'child like' mural

Locals in Tuxford, Nottinghamshire have been confused by a council's decision to put a mural under an underpass, and were left enraged after finding out how much it cost

View 5 Images Locals have been left fuming at the new mural (Image: Tom Maddick / SWNS)

Locals have been left furious after a council forked over nearly £50,000 of their taxpayer cash on a "child like" mural that was painted on a dark underpass.

‌



‌



Bassetlaw District Council, which is based in Worksop, Nottinghamshire, initially set aside £25,000 for artwork meant to decorate both sides of an A1 tunnel in the neighbouring town of Tuxford. But the costs were sent soaring after the the artist's sprawling work area forced pedestrians and children to walk into the road.

‌



A further £22,000 was added on for temporary infrastructure, including traffic lights, after the artist's materials and ladders blocked a local footpath.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Reform councillor arrested on suspicion of making false statements on nomination papers READ MORE :

View 5 Images Granddad-of-four Peter Choinacki said the mural was 'confusing' (Image: Tom Maddick / SWNS)

Residents have raged that the council spent a total of £47,000 on a project they say "looks more like graffiti" which could otherwise have been funnelled into community projects. Among those voicing their fury is retired trucker Peter Chojnacki, 75, who has lived in the village his whole life.

‌



The granddad-of-four said the mural is "confusing" and complained it was a "massive waste of money". He said: “It’s not just a small waste of money, it’s a massive waste of money.

"For starters it looks like something a child would do at school, secondly it’s in a dark underpass so you can hardly see it. I wouldn’t be surprised if the street artists turn up with their own spray cans and add to it in the next few days. I don't even think the mural actually represents Tuxford's history very well either. It all looks confusing."

View 5 Images The mural ended up costing nearly £50k due to obstruction caused during its making (Image: Tom Maddick / SWNS)

‌



"I think almost £50,000 would have been so much better spent on a village hall or community space everyone could use.” The mural depicts Tuxford’s time as a major coaching hub in the 1800s, its connection to the brewing industry and a 1702 fire that almost wiped out the town.

Tuxford received £1 million in Town Streetscaping Funding in 2024 through Labour-run Bassetlaw District Council, which decided where to spend the cash.

Of the money received, around £335,000 has so far gone on revamping shop frontages, additional CCTV coverage, play equipment on parks, defibrillators, speed reduction signs and market stalls. The mural was approved in 2024 and completed in August, with the artist working with a local school, charity and community group. The council admitted the traffic lights "significantly contributed to the additional costs".

‌



View 5 Images The mural was made following consultation with groups local to Tuxford (Image: Tom Maddick / SWNS)

Residents have however taken issue with its placement, with another saying they felt the underpass was a "strange place" to put the painting.

They said: "At first glance it looks like more graffiti but you can’t exactly stop and admire it because it’s on a busy road and no one wants to spend too much time hanging around an underpass. It's laughable that they had to spend twice as much so kids wouldn't get run over on the way to school.

‌



"Did no one at the council think about the fact the path would have to be closed off while it was painted?" Councillor Steve Scotthorne, cabinet member for planning, identity and place, told the BBC the mural is "something nice to see on a dull underpass".

View 5 Images Residents said the underpass was a 'strange place' for the mural (Image: Tom Maddick / SWNS)

He said: "Not everyone will like what they see but it's about giving Tuxford a positive outlook and getting visitors in." He added Via East Midlands, which provides road maintenance services for Nottinghamshire County Council, raised concerns after work had already started.

‌



He added: "We were quite happy to budget for £25,000 but we had Via say they were concerned about the safety of artists and the people getting involved.

"We needed to spend that money and we tried to make it as low as we could. The cost was disappointing but we want to see our town centres thriving and people talking positively about them."

Via East Midlands said it initially granted the council a licence for the mural works. A spokesperson said: "After receiving complaints from members of the public about school children walking in the road due to the footway being blocked, an inspection of the site took place which resulted in discussions with BDC about how to make the site safe.

Article continues below

"Whilst we're aware the need for additional measures will have increased the cost of the project, the safety of pedestrians and road users was our priority."

News.title: British national arrested in connection with RAF Fairford incident
News.content:
A 22-year-old British national has been arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts in connection with an incident close to RAF Fairford, counter-terror police said.

He was arrested in Westminster, London, on Tuesday as part of the investigation into the incident near the airbase in Gloucestershire on 27 September.

It is the seventh arrest in connection to the incident but no one has been charged.

A major incident was declared and dozens of homes were evacuated after police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase.

Senior national coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, Vicki Evans, said it "remains a live investigation" and police are continuing to "pursue multiple lines of enquiry".

Five men were arrested on 27 September near the base in the connection with the incident and were subsequently released on police bail.

The men, aged between 23 and 25, were detained in the early hours of the morning after vehicles were reported to be travelling towards the base.

They were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, before being released on bail in what police called an "investigative decision" that was "grounded in experience and strategy".

A sixth man, a 25-year-old dual Iranian-British national, was arrested on 1 October in Westminster and was also later released on bail.

RAF Fairford, near the village of Whelford, has been used by the US Air Force for decades.

In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from the base to the Middle East, after the UK approved a request for Fairford to be used for defensive strikes against Iran.

On Sunday, it emerged the US had pulled its bombers out of the base and returned them to America.

US President Donald Trump said the aircraft were removed due to "some threats" to the base without giving specific details.

While speaking to a group of reporters outside the White House on Monday, Trump was asked if a "specific threat" had led the US to pull its bombers from the airbase.

He replied: "Yeah I think we can say that. They didn't fly out by accident.

"There were some threats. And rather than tempting the enemy, we'll capture the enemy and beat the enemy.

"But why should we leave them there? So we moved them around a little bit. Not very far."

Earlier, US Vice-President JD Vance said the bombers were moved "out of an abundance of caution".

The comments came after US media reports suggested the decision was made after intelligence suggested Iran was plotting a drone attack. The BBC has not verified those reports.

On Tuesday, a spokesperson for US European Command, which coordinated American military activity in Europe, said it would be "inappropriate to discuss matters of intelligence" but that the US would "continue to assess the threat environment" at bases.

The spokesperson added the US remains at the "highest state of readiness" and would take "appropriate actions to protect our people, our platforms, and the bases where our forces operate".

Prior to Trump's intervention on Monday, a No 10 spokesperson had insisted RAF Fairford was safe and pointed to his previous comments, where he praised the UK's "police, defence and security services" in relation to the base.

News.title: I'd rather have another election than do a deal with Reform UK, says Badenoch
News.content:
Kemi Badenoch has said she would rather have another general election than do a deal with Reform UK to secure power, if no party wins the next election.

The Conservative Party leader told the BBC that Nigel Farage's Reform are "neck deep in scandal" and joining forces with them would "just be one problem after another".

Polling suggests there would be a hung parliament at the next election, with Labour currently expected to be the largest party followed by Reform and the Tories.

As the Conservative Party conference in Birmingham nears its end, Badenoch has also pledged to cut the cost of hiring 21 to 24-year-olds by halving the rate of employer national insurance (NI) contributions.

Badenoch has been trying to position the Conservatives as a party that is different to the one that suffered an historic defeat in the 2024 general election.

She told BBC Political Editor Chris Mason "we are going back to the authentic Conservative Party, that people knew and loved" after she published a 100-page document, called The Right Way, setting out the party's principles, external.

Badenoch added "politics is volatile", as she tried to talk up the party's chances despite the polls suggesting only one-in-five voters would back them.

She said: "We're in a different political world, and it is within that context that we know that we can win. I'm not saying that we would win.

"The current polling shows a hung parliament, no party getting an overall majority.

"My prediction is that there would be another election immediately after. But we're the only credible alternative to Labour, the only ones with a plan."

A scenario was put to Badenoch in which the Conservatives would be the largest party and Reform have a significant presence in a hung parliament after the next election.

Asked if she would work with Reform in government, Badenoch replied: "If you want Conservative, you have to vote Conservative. I have said we'd have another election if there was no overall majority."

Badenoch added she wants Reform voters to "come back" to the Conservatives, saying people in Farage's party are "neck deep in scandal, it'd just be one problem after another".

She pointed to the arrest of Dan Thomas, who quit last month as Reform's leader in Wales after he was arrested on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviour. Thomas said he had "done nothing wrong".

Badenoch also highlighted the case of Nathan Gill, the former leader of Reform in Wales who was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison after admitting taking bribes for pro-Russia interviews and speeches.

Farage has faced intense scrutiny over financial support he has received, including a Â£5m gift he received from a billionaire Reform donor before he became an MP. He has insisted he has done nothing wrong.

Badenoch added: "I want to get this economy growing, I want to make the country richer, I want to stop the boats, we've got a plan on borders, we've got a plan on welfare, we've got a plan on defence and bringing energy costs down.

"That's what we're about."

Privately, senior Conservatives talk of what they see as the importance of a potential 'tipping point' in support for the Conservatives and support for Reform UK.

Tories hope that if they can draw level and then establish a small lead over Reform in opinion polls, they can begin to make the case that they are the only viable alternative to Labour winning the next general election, potentially then attracting more support.

Badenoch has long said she wouldn't do a deal with Reform before the election, as it was a party trying to destroy the Conservatives.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said last month he was not tempted to call an early general election, arguing it would throw "the country into a backward-looking process". The next one must be held by August 2029.

Farage has previously said Reform have "replaced the old fuddy-duddy existing Conservative Party".

News.title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked
News.content:
Two police officers who pepper-sprayed and Tasered a 92-year-old amputee at a care home have been sacked for gross misconduct.

PC Stephen Smith and PC Rachel Comotto, who were both acquitted of assault occasioning actual bodily harm in May 2025, had been called to Park Beck care home in St Leonards-on-Sea after resident Donald Burgess threatened carers with a dinner knife.

Burgess, who had dementia, was hit with a baton, pepper sprayed and Tasered as he sat in his wheelchair in his bedroom in June 2022.

At Sussex Police headquarters in Lewes earlier, a disciplinary panel decided there had been "unjustified and excessive use of force" and dismissed both officers without notice.

Burgess was taken to hospital after the incident, where he contracted Covid and died 22 days later, but the officers were not held responsible for his death.

The misconduct panel found Comotto and Smith did not attempt to de-escalate the situation before using force and had breached standards of professional behaviour.

Both have been placed on the College of Policing's barred list.

News.title: From films to streaming prices - how the Warner Bros deal could affect you
News.content:
It has been months in the making but Paramount Skydance has finally completed its $110bn (Â£82.8bn) merger with Warner Bros Discovery.

The deal welds two legacy Hollywood powerhouses, uniting franchises like Harry Potter and Game of Thrones, into an entertainment behemoth named Skydance.

Yet behind this milestone lies strict rules about what the combined business can and cannot do - from how many films it must produce a year to the editorial independence of its newsroom.

Here are four ways this could affect you and the movies, TV and news you watch.

News.title: Watch: How Russia responded to US after plague researcher death
News.content:
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has urged people not to "listen to various rumours" after a Russian lab technician died at a plague research centre in Siberia.

Peskov called for people to follow only information from Russia's public health watchdog, which named the official cause of death of the lab technician as pneumonia of unknown origin.

BBC Russia editor Steve Rosenberg also asked Peskov about US President Donald Trump's offer of support to Russia.

News.title: UK special forces could face prosecution as Afghanistan evidence referred to police
News.content:
UK special forces (UKSF) personnel could face prosecution after evidence found following enquiries by the SAS Inquiry, suggesting serious offences may have been committed in Afghanistan, was handed to the military police.

The evidence came to light in court proceedings on Monday and is the first time the inquiry has publicly acknowledged that its findings could lead to criminal prosecutions.

The referral - made by UKSF earlier this year - was required under the Armed Forces Act, which defines Schedule 2 serious offences as including murder and manslaughter.

It relates to a number of detention operations carried out by British personnel between 2010 and 2013.

The Ministry of Defence (MoD) found the evidence earlier this year, following investigation by the SAS Inquiry, and then UKSF referred it to the military police's Defence Serious Crime Unit (DSCU), a specialist unit set up in 2022 to deal with the most serious crimes.

Court documents obtained by the BBC suggest that the DSCU has undertaken a scoping exercise of the evidence, but the unit has paused any criminal investigations until the inquiry has been concluded.

Separately, the MoD told the BBC it was deemed inappropriate for criminal investigations to be undertaken while the inquiry was still ongoing.

The Independent Inquiry relating to Afghanistan is examining allegations that the British Army's Special Air Service (SAS) unlawfully killed people during detention operations in Afghanistan between 2010 and 2013, and that senior officials sought to cover up the true circumstances of the killings.

BBC Panorama has been investigating allegations the SAS executed handcuffed civilians and children, for more than eight years. The public inquiry was established in 2022 in the wake of Panorama's revelations.

The DSCU referral came to light during a High Court hearing brought by a witness to the inquiry.

The witness, a senior British military officer who served in Afghanistan, has won permission to have the inquiry judicially reviewed after military witnesses' legal teams were excluded from closed-door evidence hearings with whistleblowers.

Much of the public inquiry's evidence is being heard in secret.

Lawyers for the senior officer argued the process was unfair and the officer should have an opportunity to question the whistleblowers, either in person or through his lawyers, regarding any allegations made against him.

The inquiry's lawyers said it "must be able to obtain highly sensitive information" from people who may be concerned about giving evidence.

They said protected witnesses had raised fears of "grievous consequences by UKSF" if their identities were revealed.
