Sports.title: How FIA software bug caused chaos in Bahrain GP in Malaysia – and the emergency fix that saved the race
Sports.content:
The start of the first wet-weather race of the 2026 Formula 1 season descended into chaos. Leader Max Verstappen was the first to suffer from a lack of power while driving slowly during the formation laps behind the safety car, after which Lewis Hamilton came to a standstill and several other cars followed.

Race control was forced to stop the formation lap with a red flag, after which there was a 40-minute delay before fans actually got to see some F1 action.

Read Also: Formula 1 FIA explains software glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia race delay

FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis confirmed to media including Autosport that a bug in the software supplied by the FIA and developed together with the teams over the course of multiple years was responsible for the chaos.

“We didn't manage to test the software as extensively as we would have liked because there's been very little wet running this year. There was a bit of a combination of circumstances which caused this bug to kick in,” Tombazis said during an impromptu media session post-race.

“Basically, on the formation lap, some cars went very slowly and almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars and some cars almost stopped completely. That bug prevented then the power to be redeployed and for the cars to start again.”

This is closely related to the reduction in electrical power to 250kW in wet conditions.

Although the software required for this was tested by several teams, including Red Bull and Racing Bulls, it was not tested in the conditions behind the safety car – and therefore not at these extremely low speeds.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

At the Sepang International Circuit, those low speeds were reached in certain minisectors, with all the consequences that followed.

“It was mainly in some sectors where the full power was reduced. I don't know exactly what speed that was, but some cars reaching this very low speed somehow entered into a loop, which meant they couldn't re-accelerate and then it looked as if they came to a stop.”

In practice, this left drivers feeling as though the throttle pedal was no longer responding, something Oliver Bearman told the media with some surprise.

“I've never seen or felt anything like that. I was shocked that… I didn't even know that the FIA could control our throttle pedal. That was quite scary, actually,” the Haas driver said.

“My throttle pedal just stopped working. It was like it was not connected and the engine was just idling. It was so weird, I mean, shocking.”

One of the questions is why the internal combustion engine was also affected, when that should not be the case at extremely low speeds. The FIA does not yet have a formal answer to that question, but the initial suggestion is that the bug caused all throttle input to go towards recharging the MGU-K, which explains why drivers felt there was no response from the throttle pedal at all.

At first glance, it appeared as though the Mercedes-powered cars were less affected by the issue than other manufacturers, but Tombazis explained that there is no technical reason for that. It was simply related to the speeds reached in certain minisectors.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“Not all cars reached the same low speeds on the formation lap. There was a bit of a concertina effect. I think Max slowed down quite a lot, being at the front, and then some cars braked harder as they were surprised and so on. That caused some cars to experience the problem and some others to not experience it.”

How the FIA provided F1 teams with an emergency fix

The FIA then had to react quickly to get the race near Kuala Lumpur under way after all, as Tombazis explained when asked by Autosport.

“Fortunately, our guys understood the issue very, very quickly. I think the update was done very competently. It was obviously a rush job. The priority was to get running as quickly as possible again, so I think the reaction time was quite fast,” he said.

“It wasn't a perfect job and, clearly, we didn't test the updates, but I think it was the way to handle such a case.”

In practice, the update meant that the FIA lifted the energy limit constraint – the restrictions associated with the 250kW limit – for the minisectors in which the low speeds had triggered the bug. Logically, this is not a watertight solution going forward, but it was an emergency measure to ensure the race could go ahead.

“In some of the sectors, some of these reductions of power were overridden,” Tombazis confirmed. “Clearly, we didn't have five days to do the updates. We only had a few minutes, but fortunately, I think we managed to do it without compromising any safety, any racing or fairness.”

How could this happen in the first place?

After the FIA update, all the teams still had to install the modified software, which explains the delay before the restart. The Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was saved as a result, but that still does not explain how the FIA could have missed this issue throughout all its preparations and why it only surfaced in round 16 of the championship.

“The software was tested. It just wasn't tested in those specific conditions,” Tombazis replied. “What caught us out was the fact that cars went in that very, very low speed, which was not normally contemplated.”

FIA Safety Car Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

During the tyre tests in which the software was tested, the extremely low speeds were understandably not reached. Nevertheless, there is a crucial counterargument to that: in the rain, the likelihood of a safety car – and therefore low speeds – is very high. Should the FIA not have anticipated that, and was that the governing body’s biggest mistake?

Asked that question by Autosport, Tombazis responded: “Well, any bug is a product of a mistake. I don't know of any software that doesn't have bugs and updates. Your computer probably gets updated every three days and those are all bugs.

“Of course, anticipating these things is what one hopes to do, but sometimes some very combination of events isn't properly anticipated and causes the problem. I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time and not to have such a situation.”

Although the cause of this problem is now known and a temporary fix has been introduced, the FIA still has many questions to answer internally – also to ensure that it does not happen again.

“We would all like it to be simpler, but the fact is when you have as much electrical energy, it does make it more complicated. I think you appreciate that the race has now finished about one hour ago and we haven't done a full debrief of the situation to see how we can avoid such an issue.

“Every race, we have a long debrief afterwards where we identify criticalities. Obviously, that was a major criticality and we need to make sure we avoid it.

“But can I guarantee it will never happen again? This specific problem, yes. A problem, no. But we will do our best to avoid it, of course.”

Sports.title: The slick tyre gamble that hurt McLaren and Ferrari's chances in Bahrain GP in Malaysia
Sports.content:
When the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia eventually got going after an hour and 33 minutes of delays, it became apparent that the intermediate was the tyre to be on among the opening laps - even if the Sepang circuit had looked like it was drying out.

At the front of the field, Ferrari and McLaren chose to go all-in on the dry tyres for the restart; Ferrari opted for the soft compound, while McLaren went for the mediums. When the race got underway behind the safety car, both teams were left to rue their choices as the circuit was still too slippery.

McLaren bailed on the plan early, stopping before the standing start to ensure Oscar Piastri could get a set of intermediates back onto the car, but Lando Norris and the Ferraris stuck with their choices. Charles Leclerc duly fed into the pitlane at the end of the lap, as the slick-tyre runners were swamped and then left behind by those who'd stuck with the intermediate for the start.

Lewis Hamilton and Norris surmised that, since they'd made their beds, they'd lie in them. Hamilton was asked if he wanted to stop again, but the seven-time champion reasoned that Ferrari might as well stick with the gamble given that the team was well behind - and pitting would only cost more time.

By the end of the eighth lap, the slick times were now equal with the intermediate runners; Valtteri Bottas' subsequent off then presented the inter-shod drivers with the chance to switch to slicks.

Speaking about the decision, Norris stated that the idea of starting on the slick was "quite convincing" and that he was unsure of the performance of the inter; on his recon lap to the grid, the Briton reported that the green-walled tyre was already feeling the pain on Sepang's rough surface.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

"It felt maybe a little bit of a risk, because a slick on a wet track is always a bit of a risk," Norris said. "There was enough people on it that it was quite convincing at the time that it was possibly going to be the right decision.

"The laps to the grid on the inter when it was a similar kind of condition, they had so much grip and my Inter was completely shredded after one lap.

"I was convinced a slick tyre would work, but I think it was just the fact I've never really been on the inter before. Things just felt a lot better than they should have done in a way.

"If we would have had a read on an inter from a previous weekend, maybe I would have been able to understand it more. But that convinced us and it clearly convinced a lot of people.

"Oscar probably made the right decision in boxing and we got it wrong today, that's all."

Leclerc theorised that the roughness of the tarmac made it more difficult to read the track surface, as water pooled up in the gaps - and the drop in temperature that accompanied the rain ensured that the circuit took much longer to dry out than expected. Given the length of the downpour, any residual circuit temperature was swiftly extinguished.

Even though the Monegasque switched tyres, the time loss involved in pitting after the start kept him behind Hamilton, who ran longer on his set of soft tyres and quickly began to make up positions.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

Hamilton joked that he wasn't going to "go to the casino with the guys" after the team's gambles didn't pay off, although praised his team's strategy in keeping him out on the road. The Briton was ultimately less enamoured with the medium after making a stop on lap 31, but the late-race VSC (later a full safety car) presented a chance to return to the soft - which he put to use with a pass on Isack Hadjar for third.

"As we pulled out [of the pits], all the spray came out the back of Max’s car and I was like, 'okay, I’m done. My race is really in trouble,'" Hamilton recounted.

"We just had to stick with it. As everyone’s overtaken me, they [the engineers] were like, 'we stop.' I know we’ve already made another 26 seconds. What’s the difference from that with one minute 40 or whatever I was down? So I was just, 'Let’s just wait it out for the track to dry.'

"And once it did, it felt good that I was catching people. The car felt great then after that. Really good pitstops from my guys in the garage and then good strategy. But for us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that was going to be the case. Of course, I’m really, really grateful that we managed to get back here.

"We’ll definitely have an open dialogue, and I’m really so proud of my team. The mechanics every weekend, just the work they’re putting in, the engineers that accompany here every weekend, the catering, everyone really, really comes and gives it their best.

"Their heart’s all in the right spot. We’ve definitely got areas that we need to improve and we know that, and we’re not in any denial of that. So I think we’ll have a constructive chat, we’ll regroup, we’ll take the positives from this weekend, which the car was really good, and we’ll come back next week fighting."

Sports.title: FIA explains software glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia race delay
Sports.content:
The FIA has given insight into why Formula 1 cars experienced technical issues ahead of Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The start of the Sepang race was delayed by 40 minutes due to a downpour; then a chaotic formation lap saw the likes front-row starters Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton suffer from a glitch which rendered throttle input ineffective, with numerous cars coming to a standstill. The red flag was waved.

The situation was branded “unacceptable” by Sergio Perez, who likened it to ‘being in a rental kart and running out of time’; Lando Norris described it “just horrible” and evidence that “we shouldn't have any of that stuff, the electronic side”, given this was linked to Formula 1’s new machinery, which features 47% electrical power.

FIA single-seater Nikolas Tombazis has now explained that, given F1 had never had competitive running in actual wet conditions this season, it was caught out by the power unit’s reaction to cars driving extremely slowly at that time. A software update therefore had to be carried out, hence a 53-minute delay to get the race restarted.

“We didn't manage to test the software as extensively as we would have liked, because there's been very little wet running this year, and there was a bit of a combination of circumstances which caused this bug to kick in,” Tombazis said.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“Basically, the formation lap, some cars went very slowly, almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars, and some cars almost stopped completely. And that bug prevented the power to be redeployed and for the cars to start again. I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time and not to have such a situation.”

Tombazis praised the FIA’s reaction when it came to fixing the issue as swiftly as possible.

“Once the problem happened, our guys realised very quickly what was happening and had to work under a lot of time pressure for an update to the software, which was issued to the teams, and the teams had to install it on their cars,” he added.

“So all of that took about 20 minutes. It may have felt like five hours for spectators waiting [for] a race and for everybody else, which is understandable, and we are sorry about that. But I think it was quite a fast reaction given the problem.”

Not everyone was so upset about some cars running into trouble, with eighth-placed Fernando Alonso joking at the end of an unusually good day for Aston Martin-Honda: “I had 50% DNFs this year, they never stopped the race for us.”

Sports.title: Russell: “You’ve got to laugh” at bad luck as F1 title drifts away
Sports.content:
Mercedes driver George Russell labelled his misfortune as laughable following Formula 1’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, where a power unit failure cost him a podium finish late on.

Russell was a lowly seventh on the grid at Sepang, but the correct choice of intermediate tyres on a damp track and a lightning getaway saw him surge to second into Turn 1, behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

Russell was however passed by Max Verstappen as early as lap six, but the first safety car period gave him a chance to sweep past Antonelli around the outside of Turn 5 at the restart as the race leader dropped down to third – though the Italian youngster found a way back into second place just eight laps later.

Further drama did not disrupt the status quo in the top three, but a late safety car meant Russell had a chance to challenge his rivals for victory. However, the chance never came as a power unit failure took him out of the race before the final restart.

“You've almost got to laugh,” Russell told Sky Sports F1 after his third retirement this season – his second purely technical DNF. “It's beyond disappointment. It's just, so many times this season it's happened.

“Of course, it's a real shame, but… Just keep on fighting. Just keep on trying to go.

“The podium, of course, looked very certain. Solid race, not amazing race, but solid race.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

“Not the first time, so I'm pretty used to this feeling and these questions, let's say.”

As he said, Russell will “keep on fighting”, but is equally aware of his deficit to championship rival Antonelli reaching an unprecedented 84 points.

The Briton steered clear of any sensational comments – he won’t say the title is out of reach – but his assessment is bleak nonetheless.

“I don't need to say I think it's gone or whatever,” he added. “But, of course, it’s exceptionally unlikely, and that's just the reality.

“I knew if I wanted to come back I needed luck on my side. Unfortunately, I've had luck not on my side. So, you know, a three-point loss today being behind Kimi turned into an 18-point loss. Of course, if the issue was on the other side, it would have been an 18-point gain.

“So, yeah, it's a real shame. It's a real shame, but that's just how it is.”

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said the Bahrain GP in Malaysia had been one of his “worst experiences” personally, as Red Bull claimed its first victory of the year over the Silver Arrows and Russell suffered that setback.

“I'm so massively annoyed,” Wolff told Sky. “I'm not in a happy place.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

“We didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will. Then the race literally went, if you consider the fight with Lewis [Hamilton] behind, went against us. We had such an advantage, one VSC, two safety cars. I mean, you couldn't be more unlucky. And to make things worse, PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points.”

After praising Antonelli for ‘doing the job’, the Austrian added: “It's just this overarching topic, the DNFs, that could cost us dearly also for the remaining seven races. A championship is quickly turned around against you or for you if you have a DNF, and that's why that can't continue.”

Perhaps Wolff was overdramatic there. At Sepang, Mercedes was outscored by Ferrari for just the first time since the summer break, and the Scuderia still is 151 points in arrears in the constructors’ championship. Meanwhile, Hamilton’s deficit to Antonelli in the drivers’ standings is up to 106 points.

Asked how to pull the team together after such a result, Wolff replied: “I think we have a good action plan. James [Allison, technical director] is really fully on top of it with his leadership team.

“That lifts my mood because I know we have such a tremendous group of people. In the same way as we have with HPP, they're going to sort it out. But that gives me real relief for the moment to know they are the best and they are going to find a solution. And I think we will come back strong.”

Sports.title: Stats: Verstappen avoids first win-less season since 2015, Red Bull-Ford’s first win and more | 2026 Bahrain GP in Malaysia stats and facts
Sports.content:
Before the unusually-named Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia began, Max Verstappen made it clear he wanted to avoid ending the season without a victory.

He put that right on Sunday, ensuring he claimed a victory for the 11th season in a row. He only failed to win a grand prix in his debut season at Toro Rosso (now Racing Bulls) in 2015.

But Verstappen needs to keep winning every year until 2030 to equal Michael Schumacher and Lewis Hamilton’s joint record of 15 consecutive winning seasons (from 1992 to 2006 and 2007 to 2021 respectively).

Verstappen claimed the first victory for car number three since his former team mate Daniel Ricciardo won the Italian Grand Prix for McLaren five years ago. Two other drivers on the grid today have won with that number: Fernando Alonso twice in 2013 at Ferrari and Hamilton three times for McLaren in 2011, both in seasons before the FIA introduced ‘career numbers’.

This was the 72nd victory of Verstappen’s career. It came in Malaysia’s first grand prix in nine years, which Verstappen also won, taking the second win of his career at that point.

The race carried the title ‘Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia’ as it took the place of April’s cancelled race in the Middle East. It is by no means unique for one country to hold an event named for another: San Marino, Luxembourg and Switzerland all gave their names to races in other nearby countries: Italy, Germany and France respectively.

But there were a few noteworthy differences. Those latter cases were all events held in addition to rounds which took place in those countries, while F1 is not racing in Bahrain at all this year as it was considered too unsafe due to the proximity to the conflict in Iran. Precisely because of that, the distance between the event and the country it was named after was much greater than those earlier cases, being some 6,000 kilometres.

So instead of the Bahrain International Circuit holding its 23rd race, the Sepang International Circuit held its 20th. In theory Bahrain will hold the first round on the 2027 F1 calendar, but watch this space.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Verstappen’s success vindicated Red Bull’s decision to build their own power unit, in conjunction with Ford. The latter last contributed to a grand prix victory in 2003, when Giancarlo Fisichella won the Brazilian Grand Prix for Jordan (now Aston Martin) powered by a Ford-Cosworth RS1.

The same power units ended Mercedes’ monopoly on pole positions this year. After 15 consecutive Mercedes-powered poles, Verstappen claimed the first for a (partly) Ford-badged engine since Rubens Barrichello put his Stewart at the front of the field for the 1999 French Grand Prix at Magny-Cours.

However a substantial amount of credit must also go to Red Bull, who had already committed to building their own power units before teaming up with Ford. Although they previously ran their Honda-designed units successfully, they deserve to be regarded as a new engine constructor in their own right, and those don’t appear very often.

If we accept this was the first victory for a new engine built by a new constructor, when was the last time this happened? Red Bull’s other wins since 2022 have been credited to ‘Red Bull Powertrains’ and Honda RBPT but all involved the same Honda-derived power units.

Other new names which appeared on the winners lists in previous years were often due to branding exercises. Red Bull previously won races with Renault engines badged as TAG Heuer. Engines produced by Honda and Porsche won races labelled as Mugen-Honda and TAG-Porsche respectively.

Using a strict definition, avoiding all rebranded engines and those related to previous designs by constructors who had already won races, Red Bull-Ford’s win is the first for a new F1 engine constructor since BMW in 1982. That win came courtesy of Brabham’s Nelson Piquet in the Canadian Grand Prix. In an extremely unusual result, his team mate Riccardo Patrese finished that race in second place powered by a different engine: his Brabham was powered by Ford.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The others manufactures on the grid today are either yet to win (Audi) or scored their first wins long ago: Ferrari in 1951, Mercedes in 1954 and Honda in 1965.

A week ago, George Russell grabbed the eighth win of his career, in Baku. Verstappen served notice of Red Bull’s potential there, chasing his rival across the line, the pair separated by just 0.196 seconds. This was the closest finish to a grand prix since the rigged conclusion to the 2002 United States Grand Prix, where Schumacher attempted to contrive a ‘dead heat’ with team mate Barrichello, but instead was beaten to the line by 0.011s.

Finally, Fernando Alonso took advantage of the conditions in Sepang to claim Aston Martin’s best finish of the season with eighth place. Those four points leave his team just five shy of Williams.

Over to you

Have you spotted any other interesting stats and facts from the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia or Azerbaijan Grand Prix? Share them in the comments.

Sports.title: “All cars are lacking power”: How drivers saw Formula 1’s formation lap fiasco | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Confusion reigned when Formula 1 drivers headed out to begin yesterday’s grand prix.

A software glitch struck much of the grid, causing some cars to slow to a crawl and others to stop entirely. Some power units sprang back into life while others stubbornly refused to work again.

Eventually race control abandoned the attempt to start the race and summoned the field back into the pits so the FIA could issue a software update. The process took the best part of an hour.

The problem was widespread throughout the field and affected drivers in different ways. Here’s how several of them experienced the fault.

1st: Max Verstappen

Verstappen’s car almost came to a stop at the front of the field. However a switch change on his steering wheel solved the problem for him.

Verstappen Verstappen slows at turn 10

Well, this is fucked. I can’t accelerate. Lambiase OK, stand by. Verstappen Why doesn’t it work? Lambiase Stand by. Verstappen It’s not working, guys. Lambiase Yep stand by Max, we’re looking. Let’s have fail one fail please, Max. Fail one fail.

The car accelerates away Lambiase Looks like maybe Lewis has a similar problem to you. He’s still struggling between turn 11 and turn 12.

Expecting the start to go ahead, Verstappen was unhappy that the side of the grid he was due to start from was wetter than the opposite side.

Verstappen The right on the grid is not fair, left looks drier, my side. Lambiase Understood, thank you. Lambiase So Max, to try and avoid what happened there on that last lap, let’s keep the engine revs up in the corners please, so as low a gear as you can possibly run. Verstappen [Unclear] Lambiase Yeah, there is a long train of cars struggling, crawling: both Audis, Hamilton, Haas. I don’t think this is related to individual engine issues here Max, I think there’s some kind of relation. So Hamilton has got going. You have both Cadillacs, both Haas, both Audis crawling ahead of you, as is Lindblad.

Verstappen laughed when he saw several cars stuck on the back straight due to the software problem. However he was less amused to spot a nail in his tyre when he returned to the pits.

Verstappen Verstappen follows the Safety Car to the back straight where several cars are stuck

Well, look at this. [Laughs] Lambiase Red flag. Red flag. They’re coming into the pit lane. Slow button please, Max, slow button. Lambiase Just confirming Max, follow the Safety Car ahead into the pit lane. Lambiase This shouldn’t be too long, Max. Verstappen There’s a nail in my tyre. Lambiase On front left. Verstappen Front left. Lambiase Thank you. [Message cuts out] issue. Some kind of… [Message cuts out]

2nd: Lewis Hamilton

The fault struck Hamilton’s car at the same time as Verstappen’s. As a result, he appeared not to realise the Red Bull driver was suffering from the same problem as him. Ferrari had more difficulty finding a solution for Hamilton.

Hamilton I’ve lost power. Santi We are checking. Hamilton Something’s happened, I’ve got no… I’m just ticking over in first gear. Santi Coming back to you. Hamilton Throttle’s not doing anything. Santi No action for the moment. Hamilton I’m pressing the throttle, nothing’s happening. Santi We are coming back to you. Hamilton What can I do? Santi At the moment we have no action, we are looking to… Try a single click of the boost, try a single click of the boost.

Hamilton correctly predicted the loss of power was due to the special settings used to configure the power units for each circuit.

Hamilton The engine’s still running, but I just got no power. Must be something with the track. Santi Try, mode race, mode race. Hamilton Yeah, still nothing. I think something’s happened with the track that’s done it to me and two cars behind. Santi This is a software issue we are trying to solve. Hamilton Anything I can do? Should I stop and reboot the car? Santi Yes, we switch off, switch off. Then wait five seconds then ignition on and fire up again Hamilton It worked, I’ve got power again.

Santi sounded jubilant when Ferrari realised restarting the car had worked. However the team was unsure whether, when the race restarted, Hamilton would be allowed to line up on the front row of the grid.

Sports.title: Fan’s video shows moment software glitch slowed F1 cars to a crawl on formation lap | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1’s 2026 engine regulations faced fresh criticism yesterday following the farcical start to the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The race, which had already been delayed by rain, was postponed by almost an hour more after a software problem struck cars during the formation lap.

Pole-winner Max Verstappen and several drivers behind him slowed to a crawl as their power units would not allow them to accelerate. The cause was a software parameter set by the FIA, which required the governing body to apply new settings to the cars.

Verstappen said he had as much power as he did when the drivers raced in Lego cars in a promotional event.

“It was like the Lego race,” he said. “Same speed. It was insane, it’s the Lego power.

“At some point we were five-wide on the straight because we couldn’t understand what was going on. Then we did a lap and then I see eight other cars crawling still.

“That’s not what you want, right, for the sport.”

The FIA said the cars’ loss of power was due to “an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy management settings and the Sepang circuit’s sector configuration.”

Sports.title: Mercedes ‘don’t know if upgrade made us faster or slower’ – Antonelli | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The long-awaited upgrade package Mercedes introduced last weekend may have made them less competitive, Andrea Kimi Antonelli has admitted.

Antonelli led the opening stages of yesterday’s race ahead of team mate George Russell . However both were overtaken by Max Verstappen , who went on to win the race.

Mercedes originally planned to introduce their new parts for the W17 at this weekend’s race in Singapore. They brought the upgrade forward after Formula 1 added last weekend’s round in Malaysia to replace the cancelled event in Bahrain.

However the unusually abrasive track surface at the Sepang International Circuit complicated the team’s efforts to understand the performance of its upgraded car. Antonelli qualified half a second slower than Verstappen.

He said the performance of the upgrade is “the question we need to answer because we don’t really know if it made us go faster or worse.”

However he pointed out the team has been less competitive at tracks which share some traits with Sepang. “It’s fair to say that this season, whenever we went on really old Tarmac, we’ve struggled. For example, in Zandvoort, McLaren was much quicker than us, especially on the older Tarmac.

“So I think maybe it’s just a fact that the Tarmac is very old and that for the tyres it’s very, very hard, and maybe we just struggle on this kind of Tarmac.

“But, of course, the track and the Tarmac made our life difficult in understanding whether it made us improve or not.”

The championship leader expects the team will have some answers before this weekend’s race. “I’m sure the team – they have a lot of data, especially after this weekend – and I’m sure for Singapore we will come with a much, much better view on the package and hopefully we can extract the full potential out of it.”

Sports.title: Spotlight: ‘Who decided these rules were best for F1?’ asks Sainz | Brief
Sports.content:
The farcical scenes during yesterday’s formation laps which delayed the start of the race by almost an hour prompted criticism from several drivers.

Grand Prix Drivers Association director Carlos Sainz Jnr was among those questioning why Formula 1 committed itself years ago to rules which have proved so problematic.

“[F1] needs to have a hard look at themselves and see how we ended up in this situation,” he said after the race. “It is clear the regs are extremely complicated for the drivers, for the teams, for the power units, for the manufacturers. It is too complicated.

“Again, my only question mark is who five years ago decided that this was the direction to go?”

F1 confirmed its current engine regulations in 2022, though the majority of the changes were substantially agreed before then. Mohammed Ben Sulayem became FIA president in December 2021.

Sainz’s father, multiple world rally champion Carlos Sainz, considered opposing Ben Sulayem in last year’s election, but chose not to. Ben Sulayem won re-election and subsequently moved to end presidency term limits, allowing him to serve as president as long as he likes.

Sports.title: Hamilton suspects he could have fought for win had he not started on slicks | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton believes he could have fought for victory at Sepang had he started on the right tyres.

The Ferrari driver qualified on the front row of the grid alongside Max Verstappen

“We were having a good weekend,” he said. “The car felt great in qualifying. It felt amazing to get to second.

“Me and my engineers were here ’til 11:30 last night just going over everything and I really, really felt today was the opportunity to have at least a good battle with Max.”

The original start was delayed due to rain. A further delay followed after a software problem caused several drivers, including Hamilton and Verstappen, to slow to a crawl during the formation lap.

“My power didn’t come back and I had to stop on-track and restart the car and then we all ended up in the pit lane,” said Hamilton. “Thankfully, we all got back to our positions.”

By the time race control were ready to start the race, the track had dried considerably, though it was still damp. Hamilton and his team chose to start the race on slick tyres.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“There was such a long wait and we were debating what tyre to go on to. And I said, ‘look, there was a lot of spray on the laps to the grid.’

“I went into the pit lane, I looked at the ground, I was like, ‘It’s still wet.’ I went to the pit wall and I was like, ‘It’s still wet.’ And they’re like, ‘Yeah, but because it’s been so long, it’s definitely going to dry up real quick and maybe we’re already in the crossover.’

“So, anyway, as a team we ended up taking that soft and when we were at the end of the pit lane and these two took off their blankets and they were on inters [I knew] we were in trouble.”

The track took a long time to dry and those who opted for intermediates gained a significant advantage at the start. Hamilton urged the team not to bring him into the pits for another change.

“As everyone had overtaken me, they’re like, ‘we stop.’ [But] I know we’ve already [lost] another 26 seconds, what’s the difference from that with one minute 40 or whatever I was down? So I [said] ‘let’s just wait it out for the track to dry.’ And once it did, it felt good that I was catching people.”

Hamilton began to make progress on his softs once the Safety Car came out and he was back within range of other cars.

“The car felt great then after that. Really good pit stops from my guys in the garage and then good strategy.

“For us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that was going to be the case. But, of course, I’m really, really grateful that we managed to get back here.”

He said he will have an “open dialogue” with the team about the decision to start the race on slicks.

“We’ve definitely got areas that we need to improve and we know that, and we’re not in any denial of that.

“So I think we’ll have a constructive chat, we’ll regroup, we’ll take the positives from this weekend, which was the car was really good, and we’ll come back next week fighting. I thought today, as I said, was a chance for us potentially to try and fight Max for the win, but maybe we can do that next week.”

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Fight Could Leave Paramount+ Waiting
Sports.content:
Zuffa Boxing could be left waiting several more months to put Shakur Stevenson on Paramount+ if his proposed fight with Devin Haney takes place on DAZN PPV, as Dan Rafael reports.

“For all the ‘reporting’ about a Haney-Shakur fight supposedly being deep in negotiations, somebody directly involved told me today nothing has changed in weeks & weight remains a major issue,” Rafael posted on X. “IF it happens, I was told it would be on DAZN PPV.”

That would be a letdown for Zuffa’s broadcast partner. Paramount+ is the promotion’s broadcast home in the United States, Canada, and Latin America, but it could miss out on a major fight involving one of Zuffa’s biggest signings.

If negotiations push the Haney fight into January 2027, Shakur would be returning after roughly 12 months out of the ring. Zuffa signed him in July, yet his eventual return could give DAZN the event while Paramount+ continues waiting.

The wait might not end soon afterward. Whether Shakur wins or loses against Haney, recovery time and another training camp could push his Paramount+ debut to May or later. May would be a possible date, rather than something Zuffa could count on.

Getting his next opponent agreed could take longer still. Shakur is a good fighter, but his demands over a catchweight and rehydration restrictions have complicated the Haney talks. If those demands follow him into another negotiation, Zuffa could face another drawn-out effort to get him fighting.

Ryan Garcia would hardly look like an easy agreement if Shakur wanted a 144-pound catchweight alongside a rehydration clause. Ryan has already experienced that combination against Gervonta Davis and has spoken against accepting those restrictions again.

A victory over Haney could make Shakur’s eventual Paramount+ appearance more attractive. Zuffa could also have a promotional role in a DAZN event, depending on the arrangements. Rafael’s report does not establish those details.

Still, signing Shakur and getting him onto Paramount+ are proving to be two different tasks. If his return happens on DAZN in January, Zuffa’s broadcast partner could spend much of the following year waiting for its turn.

Shakur has also said Gary Antuanne Russell and Raymond Muratalla each want $3 million to fight him. “Zuffa gotta cough that up,” he posted on X. He didn’t say Zuffa had refused to pay, but if those are the asking prices, moving on from Haney would leave Zuffa with another expensive fight to negotiate.

Haney could be considerably more expensive. If money is an issue for Zuffa, his asking price could become another obstacle alongside the weight dispute. There is also the question of what that money would buy inside the ring. Shakur and Haney both favor defense, jabs and controlling distance. They could spend long stretches waiting for the other to attack, like two magnets repelling each other.

Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela would offer Zuffa an in-house alternative that could cost less and produce more action. Rayo would be more likely to press Shakur, giving him someone to counter rather than another fighter waiting for him to lead.

Either result would give Zuffa something to build on. A Shakur victory would get its major signing fighting again, while a Rayo upset would raise the profile of another fighter under contract. Paramount+ would get the fight, and Zuffa would have the winner. The remaining question is whether Shakur would accept that option.

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Awaits January Date for Jaron Ennis
Sports.content:
Josh Kelly has agreed to terms to face Jaron Ennis in a 154-pound unification fight, with an early January target as they wait for DAZN to set a date.

The proposed unification would give Ennis a chance to add Kelly’s IBF belt to his WBA and WBO titles at 154 pounds. The venue remains unconfirmed, but a British location could make this a more awkward fight for Ennis than the matchup looks on paper.

“We’ve had our terms agreed for the ‘Boots’ fight for some time,” Booth said to The Ring. “From what I’ve been told, he has agreed to his terms as well. It’s literally waiting for DAZN to give Matchroom a date. It’s frustrating, but that’s the nature of the business.”

Kelly needed minor surgery to fix a broken nose following his July 25 decision victory against Caoimhin Agyarko. Sliding the bout to January offers extra healing time, but holding Ennis at bay presents a massive challenge. His championship victory over Bakhram Murtazaliev failed to convince me he was genuinely superior inside the ring.

Outside of a quick flash knockdown, Kelly rarely launched meaningful attacks during long stretches. He spent large portions of every round circling on the back foot, stealing moments with late bursts right before the bell. When scoring that bout, Murtazaliev clearly landed the more effective blows throughout the contest.

Ennis likely needs a knockout if he travels across the Atlantic to secure a victory. Trailing Kelly across the ring plays into that retreat strategy, inviting judges to score razor-thin rounds for the hometown fighter.

Cutting off escape routes and digging hard hooks downstairs will slow that retreat early. Hunting purely with telegraphed power shots upstairs lets Kelly slip away cleanly. Ennis must remain centered, stringing four-punch combinations together rather than resetting after a missed blow, wearing down that slippery guard until it collapses completely.

Trapping Kelly against the ropes offers Ennis his clearest path to victory. Kelly easily ducks single, isolated punches along the perimeter, but layered combinations splitting head and body take away his room to breathe.

Ennis stopped Xander Zayas in seven rounds back in June. Kelly must limit exchanges to quick flurries before slipping away. Ennis has to plant his feet, trap him along the boundaries, and drag him into heavy inside exchanges.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Offers Shakur Stevenson 145-Pound December Fight
Sports.content:
Devin Haney has offered to face Shakur Stevenson at 145 pounds in December, lowering his proposed weight by two pounds while keeping his demand for no rehydration clause in a post on social media.

“Let’s do this 145 no rehydration clause @ShakurStevenson .. let’s see who’s the real pussy! December.. 2026. Somebody go wake Shakur up.. Tell him we got a deal,” Haney said on X.

The proposal moves Haney off the position he posted on October 4: “147.. no rehydration let’s get it done.” He is now offering to come below the welterweight limit, although the freedom to add weight afterward remains part of his terms.

That is a concession, but it only addresses part of the disagreement. Shakur would get a lower contracted weight without a limit on how much Haney could regain before entering the ring. If his concern is the size of the fighter facing him on the night, 145 pounds doesn’t settle that.

Haney would have to make the extra effort to lose those two pounds. Once the weight check is over, however, he could replenish without a contractual cap. The proposal could still leave Shakur facing a considerably heavier opponent.

From Haney’s side, this gives him something to point to when arguing that he is trying to make the fight. He has lowered his demand and named December as the month he wants. Shakur now has a specific offer to answer, rather than another challenge with no weight attached.

The December date adds urgency if both intend to fight this year. They would need to settle the remaining terms soon enough to arrange the event and prepare properly. A public callout can start that process, but it cannot substitute for their teams reaching a deal.

Haney is giving ground on the contracted weight while holding firm on rehydration. Whether that is enough depends on which concession Shakur wants most. If a cap on Haney’s weight gain remains a requirement, they could still be stuck despite moving closer on the official limit.

Sports.title: Artur Beterbiev Taunts Rivals While His Inactivity Grows
Sports.content:
Artur Beterbiev is taking shots at unnamed rivals while approaching 600 days without a fight, appearing in a gym video shared by The Ring with a message about others running while he works.

“While the bunnies are running, we’re working,” Beterbiev wrote.

He doesn’t name Dmitry Bivol, although the timing invites that interpretation. Bivol’s manager, Vadim Kornilov, has told The Ring that a trilogy is being explored for spring 2027. That remains a possibility rather than an announced fight.

Beterbiev has been out since losing their February 22, 2025 rematch. As of October 6, that is 591 days without a competitive round. A third meeting next spring could stretch the layoff beyond two years unless he fights someone else first.

The lucrative trilogy is understandable as a target. They have one victory apiece, and Beterbiev wants another chance after losing the rematch. But allowing that fight to dictate his schedule comes at a cost, particularly for a fighter who turns 42 in January.

Beterbiev should have pursued another fight while the Bivol talks continued. An opponent below championship level could still have given him rounds, a full training camp and a chance to work through whatever needed correcting after his defeat. Waiting has given him none of that.

The gym footage shows him putting in work, but lifting weights cannot tell him how he will react when an opponent makes him miss, catches him coming forward or forces him to work late in a fight. Those are questions he could have started answering against someone other than Bivol.

There is a financial reason to protect the trilogy payday. Taking another fight brings the possibility of defeat or injury. Yet staying out brings its own danger: Beterbiev could finally secure the opponent he wants after spending two years getting older without fighting.

The “bunnies” can take the insult. Beterbiev still needs to get back into a ring. If he keeps waiting for Bivol, he has to own what that wait costs him.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia And Devin Haney Exchange Rematch DMs
Sports.content:
Devin Haney appears open to a Ryan Garcia rematch, replying, “Let’s make the fight,” in an Instagram DM screenshot shared on X by Dan The Boxing Man and later reposted by Source of Boxing.

Haney’s apparent invitation follows Ryan asking, “Do I have to remind you again.” The exchange then turns to drug accusations, which Ryan denies before making claims about Haney smoking hookah.

Neither fighter discusses a date, weight, or purse in the screenshot. It shows interest in a rematch, but no agreed terms.

Ryan pursuing Haney suggests he may prefer a bigger payday over facing Isaac Cruz or Angel Fierro. That could fit Golden Boy’s plans for a May event, although waiting would bring the inactivity concerns outlined below.

Ryan Garcia Faces Eight Months Out Under Oscar’s Plan

Oscar De La Hoya wants Ryan Garcia to face Devin Haney or Teofimo Lopez in May 2027, saving his final contracted Golden Boy fight for a big payday. The downside for Ryan is that waiting until Cinco de Mayo would leave him inactive for roughly eight months before facing either opponent.

“Obviously we want to build a major fight for Ryan in May. I believe that Ryan should be fighting on those dates. He’s the guy that should be taking the throne on Cinco de Mayo,” De La Hoya told Fight Hub TV. “A Devin Haney or a Teofimo should be next.”

Ryan has discussed returning in December or January, but De La Hoya said he spoke with DAZN and there were no dates available in those months. Neither Haney nor Lopez is secured, with Oscar describing informal discussions rather than official negotiations.

You can understand why De La Hoya wants to wait. Ryan has one fight left with Golden Boy, and Oscar wants it to be a big one. A Haney rematch or a fight with Lopez would likely bring in far more money than Angel Fierro or Pitbull Cruz.

If Ryan finishes his contract against either of those two, Golden Boy could miss out on the bigger payday that follows. De La Hoya wants to continue working with Ryan, but there is no guarantee he will sign another deal.

Ryan has a reason to want that earlier return. Neither Haney nor Lopez is an opponent you want to face after eight months out. Fighting in December or January would keep him busy rather than sending him straight into a difficult fight after a long break.

The trouble is that saving the fight for May benefits Golden Boy more than it helps Ryan stay ready. Oscar gets the chance to cash in on a major event, but Ryan has to beat Haney or Lopez after eight months on the sidelines.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Urged To Face Devin Haney Without Restrictions
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson would give critics a reason to question a victory over Devin Haney by insisting on a catchweight and rehydration clause. Chris Mannix wants him to take the fight at 147 pounds, where the result could be judged without an argument over restrictions dominating afterward.

“If this fight happens with a catchweight and a rehydration clause, there is no way that Shakur Stevenson is going to get full credit for his win if he wins,” Mannix said during his podcast discussion with Sergio Mora. “If you’re Shakur, you should want to fight this guy on a level playing field.”

Mannix pointed to Gervonta Davis’s victory over Ryan Garcia as an example of how contractual limits can remain attached to a result long after the fight ends. His concern is that Shakur could outbox Haney only to spend the aftermath defending the terms rather than discussing his performance.

That is a reasonable concern. Asking Haney to come below welterweight and then limiting how much weight he can regain would create two separate talking points. Neither would automatically explain a defeat, but both would provide an alternative explanation for anyone unwilling to credit Shakur’s boxing.

Mannix also questioned the apparent difference between Shakur’s approach to Haney and his earlier interest in facing Ryan at 147. He qualified that comparison, saying a move to welterweight was what those discussions sounded like, rather than presenting unrestricted terms as an established agreement.

Shakur would still be accepting a physical disadvantage by moving up. Haney’s size could help him in clinches and make it harder for Shakur to control distance across twelve rounds. Superior defensive skills would not erase those demands.

But that additional risk is also what would make the victory more valuable. Beating Haney at his division’s limit, without restricting his recovery afterward, would give Shakur a stronger achievement and remove an obvious contractual argument from the discussion.

Haney doesn’t appear willing to move off his demand for 147 pounds, and Shakur has less room to pressure him than he might against a lesser-known welterweight. An opponent chasing the payday and exposure could be more willing to accept 144. Haney has his own name and earning power, so he can afford to hold his position.

That leaves Shakur with a decision beyond how much credit he would receive for winning. If Haney refuses to come down, Shakur must decide whether this fight is worth moving up for. Wanting Haney as an opponent doesn’t mean he can dictate the weight.

Sports.title: Dave Allen Backs Tyson Fury To Stop Joshua
Sports.content:
Dave Allen backs Tyson Fury to stop Anthony Joshua early, drawing on his experience sparring both heavyweights and his concern over Joshua’s punch resistance. The timing of those gym sessions is unclear, however, leaving questions about how closely they reflect either fighter’s current form.

“The Prenga fight, Joshua’s punch resistance looks to be all gone,” Allen told talkSPORT’s The Verdict with heavyweight Frazer Clarke. He also acknowledged that Joshua could knock Fury out.

Allen has felt both men’s power and tested himself against their timing in sparring, giving him a useful basis for judging the matchup. We don’t know how long ago those sessions took place, though, and he hasn’t revealed which fighter gave him more trouble.

If Joshua can no longer recover quickly from a hard shot, Fury has a reason to attack early. One clean punch could leave Joshua vulnerable to a follow-up barrage before he gets his legs back.

The question is whether Fury still has the speed and reactions to exploit that weakness without getting caught himself.

Fury’s appearance gives the impression that he has aged considerably over the last three years. Appearance alone cannot establish what he has left, but his reactions, balance, and ability to recover are just as important to this matchup as Joshua’s punch resistance. Allen’s sparring memories from an era when Fury had functioning legs solve none of those mysteries.

Marching into the pocket would put both heavyweights in immediate risk. If Fury rushes to wipe Joshua out, he comes directly into the path of a fresh, explosive right hand. Bullying Joshua toward the ropes without a tight guard or a blinding jab invites disaster, because Joshua throws his best counters off the back foot.

Fury could finish Joshua early, as Allen expects, but forcing the pace would put him within reach of Joshua’s right hand. If he rushes in carelessly, Joshua may land first.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall Pressures Teofimo Lopez Over Mandatory Fight
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall is keeping his claim on Teofimo Lopez’s next fight visible while a potential Ryan Garcia matchup attracts attention. Catterall tagged Lopez on X with an eyes emoji and a staring-eyes GIF, a brief reminder that the ordered defense remains unresolved.

The WBA ordered the welterweight champions Teofimo and Catterall to negotiate in September, giving them until October 22 to reach an agreement before possible purse bids. Catterall holds the organization’s regular title, while Teofimo holds its super championship.

Catterall has earned his shot and has little reason to wait while Teofimo pursues Ryan. Agreeing to another delay would let the champion dictate when—or whether—he gets that opportunity. His public reminder keeps pressure on Teofimo to address the ordered defense

👀 @TeofimoLopez https://t.co/I6KqhNC0AN — Jack Catterall (@jack_catt93) October 5, 2026

Ryan brings the massive gate, the circus spotlight, and the blockbuster money for Lopez. Catterall brings none of that. Fighting Catterall means defending a belt against an awkward spoiler who could derail everything for a fraction of the pay.

That leaves Teofimo stuck. Chasing a blockbuster with Ryan sounds great, but the WBA order will not simply disappear. Hunting for a bigger payday is understandable, but actually getting sanctioning body approval to ignore a mandatory challenger is an entirely different battle.

Teofimo might need to vacate his belt to chase the massive check waiting with Ryan Garcia. Taking on Jack Catterall beforehand puts the entire jackpot in jeopardy. One slip against Catterall ruins his leverage, killing the buzz for the megafight.

Pretending the order does not exist invites the WBA to strip him. The October 22 cutoff marks the end of negotiations rather than an instant title stripping, yet Lopez cannot stall forever. Catterall forced the reality into the open: defend against him or walk away from the belt to fight Ryan empty-handed.

Ghana News.content:
Fitch

Attijariwafa Bank’s (AWB) acquisition of a 55.2% stake in Société Générale’s Ghana’s subsidiary is likely to be ratings neutral for the bank (AWB; BB+/Stable/bb+), Fitch Ratings has said.

According to the UK-based firm, Société Générale Ghana had assets of less than US$1 billion, or around 1.0% of AWB’s total assets and 11% of its total equity, at end-2025, and its small size compared to AWB means the acquisition is unlikely to materially increase AWB’s exposure to the rest of Africa or pressure its capital ratios.

“We also expect Societe Generale Ghana to contribute only modestly to AWB’s assets and net income (3% of AWB’s net income in 2025) over the medium term as domestic growth in Morocco should be broadly in line with the growth of AWB’s other African operations”.

It continued that the acquisition will not significantly increase AWB’s exposure to the rest of Africa, although it expects it may slightly diversify AWB’s earnings base due to Ghanaian banks’ healthy profitability metrics.

It pointed out that the sector’s pre-tax return on equity and return on assets were 22% and 4.3%, respectively, in eight months of 2026. Exposure to the region fell to 24% of consolidated assets at end of June 2026 (end-2023: 26%).

“While this remains high, granular country exposures mitigate risks at group level”, it noted.

“We expect continued growth in Morocco to support the relative weighting of domestic operations; Moroccan assets grew by about 4% in half-year 2026, broadly in line with growth in the rest of Africa”, Fitch Ratings added.

Transaction to have no Effect on AWB’s Capital

Fitch continued that the transaction should also have no material effect on AWB’s regulatory capital ratios, given Societe General’s modest size and AWB’s strong earnings generation.

AWB’s internal capital generation is underpinned by its healthy return on equity (half-year 2026: 17.5%, annualised).

“We expect its common equity Tier 1 ratio (end-2025: 10.2%) to remain at 10%-11% in the near term”, it alluded.

AWB also retains capital flexibility and could strengthen its capital position, if necessary, through dividend adjustments or additional core capital from shareholders.

It said AWB’s exposure to Ghanaian cedi volatility and any resulting impact on its regulatory capital ratios should be very limited, given the subsidiary’s small size.

Ghana’s Banking Environment Healthy

Fitch said the Ghanaian banking environment continued to improve following the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme in 2023.

It added that the transaction took place as the operating environment for Ghanaian banks improves, concluding, the macroeconomic conditions are stabilising following volatility associated with the 2024 sovereign debt restructuring.

Ghana News.title: Mahama’s Reset Agenda will make resource wealth benefit citizens – Dr Djokoto
Ghana News.content:
Deputy Director of the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS), Dr Kwesi Djokoto

Deputy Director in charge of operations of the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS), Dr Kwesi Djokoto, has reiterated that President John Dramani Mahama’s Reset Agenda reflects the need to ensure that Africa’s natural resources benefit its people.

Dr Djokoto argued that true independence requires countries to own their resources, process them and retain the economic benefits.

“True independence means owning, processing, and profiting from our own resources,” he wrote.

“Our wealth must work for our people. This is exactly what the Reset Agenda led by President Mahama is about.”

Dr Djokoto supported his position with a quotation attributed to Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, on Africa’s resource wealth and the persistence of neo-colonialism.

“Africa is a paradox which illustrates and highlights neo-colonialism. Her earth is rich, yet the products that come from above and below the soil continue to enrich, not Africans predominantly, but groups and individuals who operate to Africa’s impoverishment,” the quotation read.

Before winning the 2024 general elections, President Mahama described the Reset Agenda as a programme to rebuild Ghana’s economy, strengthen national institutions and restore public confidence, guided by fairness, inclusion and accountability. Its stated priorities include job creation, improved public services and economic transformation.

Initiatives associated with the agenda include the 24-Hour Economy, the National Apprenticeship Programme, Free Primary Healthcare, digital governance and export-led industrialisation.

These are intended to expand employment opportunities, develop skills and strengthen domestic production.

The government has also linked its industrial transformation plans to local value addition, seeking to generate more economic benefits from domestic production and processing.

This aligns with Dr Djokoto’s call for resource wealth to deliver tangible benefits to citizens.

Ghana News.title: La Pleasure Beach to reopen after demolition exercise
Ghana News.content:
La Pleasure Beach is expected to reopen within the next three weeks, according to management, following the demolition of structures at the facility.

The announcement comes after a demolition exercise carried out by the National Security on Friday, 2 October, following a request from the Labadi Beach Hotel for structures it described as encroachments to be cleared from its beachfront.

Communications Director of La Pleasure Beach, Abdul Rahman Ashittey, said the facility’s reopening would largely depend on the speed at which the debris is cleared and the necessary facilities are restored.

Speaking in an interview on Tuesday, October 6, Mr Ashittey said the debris is expected to be cleared this week, allowing management to proceed with the installation of booths and toilet facilities ahead of the facility’s reopening. He explained that the restoration process could be completed within three weeks, provided the debris is cleared as scheduled.

“They have promised this week they will come and clean up the entire beach so that the beach will continue from there. They will just mount our toll booths and then the toilet facility over here. In less than three weeks,” he said.

He further said management had engaged vendors and advised them against erecting permanent structures on the beach once operations resume.

Mr Ashittey also emphasised the financial contribution of the beach to the La community, noting that proceeds from its activities had helped to establish a development fund. He questioned how the community would continue to generate funds for development projects if activities at the beach were to remain suspended permanently.

He added that management had engaged the National Security Coordinator, the Regional Minister, the Local Government Minister, the Chief of La and the management of the Labadi Beach Hotel as part of discussions to determine the way forward.

Ghana News.title: La Pleasure Beach demolition victims to receive compensation
Ghana News.content:
A committee is expected to be constituted by early next week to determine appropriate compensation for persons whose businesses and properties were affected by the recent demolition of facilities at La Pleasure Beach in Accra.

The committee will comprise representatives of the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT), the La Dadekotopon Municipal Assembly (LaDMA), traditional authorities, management of the affected beaches and the Member of Parliament for the area, Naa Odoley Sowah.

Mrs Sowah, who is also the Deputy Minister of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, disclosed this when she appeared before the Committee on Local Government and Decentralisation in Parliament on Tuesday, October 6, 2026.

She said data had already been gathered on persons displaced by the exercise and their circumstances would be assessed to determine the form of compensation to be provided.

She, however, stopped short of giving details of the nature or amount of compensation, saying the matter would be discussed by the committee before a decision was reached.

“We have gotten their data, and the committee is going to look at what we are going to give to them as compensation. So those affected will be compensated, and the decision for the type of compensation has not been finalised, but as the MP I am following up deeply on that to ensure that everybody gets what they are supposed to get,” she said.

Mrs Sowah made this known when the Committee on Local Government and Decentralisation engaged officials of the La Dadekotopon Municipal Assembly over the demolition of beach facilities and related flood mitigation exercises in parts of the Greater Accra Region.

The Deputy Minister said the committee would also consider the needs of persons who might have to be relocated, as well as those who might require financial compensation.

She explained that the exercise involving the La Pleasure Beach facilities was separate from the demolition at Laboma, which she said would be dealt with under a different arrangement.

“Laboma Beach demolition is a different issue, but subsequently Laboma concerns will come up,” she said.

Laboma demolition

Giving an account of the Laboma demolition, the Chief Executive of the La Dadekotopon Municipal Assembly, Alfredos Nii Anyetei, told the Committee that the exercise was undertaken as part of measures to address flooding and restore an ecological site.

He said the Assembly was not consulted but was shown, during a meeting, the locations where the exercise would be undertaken.

He also said he was not aware that the MP had been specifically informed before the exercise.

Chairperson of the Committee, Queenstar Pokua Sawyerr, said the La Dadekotopon Municipal Assembly had the mandate and technical personnel to monitor development and protect waterways within its jurisdiction.

She urged the Assembly to strengthen its enforcement mechanisms to prevent people from refilling areas that had been dredged or cleared to improve drainage.

She said although central government agencies could intervene in emergencies, municipal and district assemblies should take responsibility for developments within their jurisdictions.

Mrs Sawyerr urged the MP and the Assembly to ensure that the concerns of affected persons were properly addressed, assuring them that “we will follow up on the outcome of the committee's work.”

Ghana News.title: NPP Germany congratulates new national executives, calls for unity ahead of 2028 elections
Ghana News.content:
The New Patriotic Party (NPP) Germany Branch has extended its warmest congratulations to the newly elected National Executives of the party following a successful and democratic National Executive Conference.

The branch said it welcomed the mandate entrusted to the new leadership by delegates and party faithful across Ghana and the diaspora, describing the outcome as a reflection of the confidence members have placed in the new executives.

In a statement signed by the Branch Secretary, Kofi Okantah, the NPP Germany Branch said the newly elected leadership had demonstrated the vision, competence and readiness required to steer the party towards what it described as a historic victory in the 2028 General Elections.

“We celebrate the mandate entrusted in the new leadership by the delegates and party faithful across Ghana and the diaspora.”

The branch said the outcome of the national executive elections represented an important moment for the party and expressed confidence in the ability of the new leadership to take the NPP forward.

“This victory reflects the confidence the rank and file place in their visions, competencies, and readiness to steer our great party toward a historic victory in the 2028 General Elections.”

Tribute to unsuccessful candidates

The NPP Germany Branch also extended its appreciation to all candidates who contested the national executive positions but did not emerge victorious.

It praised their patriotism, dedication and loyalty to the Danquah-Busia-Dombo tradition, stressing that their contributions to the party remained valuable despite the outcome of the elections.

“To all candidates who contested but did not emerge victorious, we salute your patriotism, dedication, and loyalty to the Danquah-Busia-Dombo tradition.”

The branch said internal elections should be seen as an important part of strengthening the party's internal democracy rather than as a process that leaves permanent winners and losers.

“In internal party elections, there are no ultimate losers only winners who advance our internal democracy.”

It urged the unsuccessful candidates to remain committed to the party and continue contributing their ideas, energy and experience to its collective development.

“Your ideas, energy, and commitment remain invaluable assets to the NPP.”

The Germany Branch further wished all the contestants success in their future endeavours and urged them to remain steadfast as integral leaders in the party's collective journey forward.

‘The national election is over; now begins the true assignment’

With the national executive election now concluded, the NPP Germany Branch said the party must turn its attention to the larger task ahead — winning the 2028 General Elections.

“The national election is over, now begins the true assignment.”

The branch said the task of securing victory in 2028 would require an unwavering commitment to reconciliation, cohesion and purposeful unity within the party.

It therefore appealed to all stakeholders, including party leadership, grassroots activists, external branches and aggrieved members, to put aside internal contestation and rally behind the newly elected executive team.

“The task of winning election 2028 requires an unwavering spirit of reconciliation, cohesion, and purposeful unity.”

The Germany Branch said unity would be critical to the NPP's ability to achieve its objectives in the next general election.

The branch called on members to work together to translate the party's shared values into an active strategy capable of breaking barriers and securing victory in 2028.

“Together, we must translate our shared values into an active strategy to break barriers and secure victory in 2028.”

Diaspora seeks stronger collaboration

The NPP Germany Branch also emphasised the important role of the diaspora in the growth and development of the party.

It said the diaspora community was looking forward to proactive collaboration with the newly elected national leadership on a number of key priorities.

One of the priorities identified by the branch is the establishment of streamlined and regular consultative forums between the national leadership and external branches.

The branch said such engagement would help strengthen communication and collaboration between the party's national structures and its branches outside Ghana.

It also called for the incorporation of diaspora expertise into the party's policy committees, manifesto drafting teams and governance planning.

According to the branch, members of the diaspora have expertise and experience that could contribute meaningfully to the party's policy development and broader organisational objectives.

The statement also called for support for external branches through capacity-building initiatives to enable them to mobilise Ghanaian communities abroad more effectively.

NPP Germany pledges support

The NPP Germany Branch said it was fully prepared to support the new national leadership and contribute towards the party's efforts ahead of the 2028 elections.

It said it would work to mobilise resources, project the party's vision across the diaspora and establish what it described as an “unshakeable bridge of collaboration” with the newly elected leadership.

“The NPP Germany Branch stands fully prepared to mobilize resources, project the party's vision across the diaspora, and build an unshakeable bridge of collaboration with our newly elected leadership.”

The branch said the next phase of the party's journey must be characterised by unity and reconciliation, with members focusing on the collective objective rather than the divisions that may have emerged during the internal elections.

It stressed the importance of honouring the contributions of all those who contested while embracing genuine reconciliation and maintaining a firm focus on the task ahead.

“By honoring the contributions of those who contested, embracing genuine reconciliation, and focusing firmly on the task ahead, we will build the strength and momentum needed to win the trust of the Ghanaian people once more.”

Focus on winning back the trust of Ghanaians

The NPP Germany Branch said the party's ability to work together would be essential to building the strength and momentum required to regain the trust of the Ghanaian people.

It urged the new national leadership, party stakeholders, grassroots activists, external branches and aggrieved members to work towards a common purpose as preparations for the 2028 General Elections begin.

The branch reiterated its readiness to play its part in strengthening the party's structures and projecting its vision among Ghanaian communities across the diaspora.

It concluded by expressing optimism about the road ahead and reaffirming its commitment to the party's collective objective.

“Together in unity, determination, and service, we look forward to achieving victory in 2028.”

Ghana News.title: Avaricious elitism and intellectualism
Ghana News.content:
Kwame Sowu, the writer

A society eventually loses respect for leaders whose greatness improves only their own lives.

When education produces arrogance, religion finances extravagance and traditional authority becomes a private business, people begin to question the institutions they once revered. They see titles multiplying while opportunities shrink. They hear wisdom preached while selfishness practises openly.

This is avaricious elitism: the belief that superior knowledge, wealth, ancestry or position entitles a person to take more from society while owing it less.

Its intellectual counterpart is equally corrosive. Intelligence becomes a sophisticated instrument for defending privilege. Brilliant people find elegant explanations for arrangements whose principal achievement is to keep themselves comfortable.

In politics, this betrayal is especially destructive.

The grassroots organise, contribute, endure insults and defend the party when doing so brings little reward. Once power arrives, some leaders disappear behind appointments, contracts, tinted windows and inaccessible offices. The people who carried them become an inconvenience.

Then, when defeat approaches, the same leaders rediscover humility, community and the importance of the ordinary voter.

People notice.

Their resentment is not necessarily hostility towards education or competence. Often, it is the accumulated disappointment of discovering that the educated and competent have used their advantages almost exclusively for themselves.

A party cannot keep asking its supporters to admire intellectual excellence that delivers no practical benefit to them. Qualifications must show up in better organisation, fairer opportunities, functioning services and leadership that listens.

Religious leadership faces the same moral test.

A congregation should not have to impoverish itself to prove that its leader is blessed. Where sacrifice flows persistently upwards and comfort rarely flows downwards, spiritual authority deserves scrutiny.

The preacher who demands accountability from politicians must accept it within the church. Members deserve clarity about how their contributions are used. Questions about money are legitimate questions of stewardship.

Faith should strengthen the vulnerable, not make them easier to exploit.

Traditional leadership, too, must justify authority through service.

A stool or skin carries obligations extending beyond ceremony, protocol and entitlement. Where authority concerns communal land, proceeds and development decisions should serve the community through transparent arrangements.

A traditional leader’s success should be visible in the condition of the people: their access to opportunity, the protection of their heritage, the resolution of disputes and the prospects of their children.

A magnificent palace surrounded by neglected lives is a monument to misplaced priorities.

These failures have consequences beyond individual disappointment. They weaken confidence in leadership itself.

When respectable people repeatedly behave selfishly, they make it easier for loud opportunists to claim that knowledge, experience and integrity are worthless. The charlatan gains ground because those better equipped to lead have made competence look socially useless.

But replacing selfish intellectuals with reckless populists merely changes the form of the betrayal.

The answer is to insist that ability carries responsibility.

Educated leaders should mentor, explain, build institutions and widen access. Political leaders should make public opportunity fairer. Religious leaders should practise the sacrifice they preach. Traditional leaders should protect communal interests with the seriousness they attach to their own dignity.

Followers also have a duty. We must stop excusing greed because it wears our party colours, speaks from our pulpit or occupies our ancestral stool. Loyalty that forbids scrutiny becomes protection for abuse.

Elitism earns legitimacy when its advantages spread. Intellectualism earns respect when knowledge becomes useful to others.

A leader’s greatness should be measured by how many people can stand taller because that leader rose.

Elitism must be infectious, not avaricious.
