World.title: Hundreds of schools shut down as France’s student protest intensifies
World.content:
Almost 900 high schools across France have either been partially or totally closed due to clashes between riot police and student protesters in the past days.

The clashes stem from growing student anger over poor conditions in French schools, including teacher shortages, inadequate resources, and deteriorating facilities. What began as a small school protest at Saint-Exupéry high school in a Parisian suburb on 21 September and attracted little attention has now snowballed into a nationwide demonstration.

The French Ministry of Education estimates that 891 schools across France have suspended classes because of the protests.

The country is presently experiencing what appears to be the biggest day of the protest so far. The Guardian reported that almost 90,000 students, staff and parents have taken to the streets in cities across France.

The French high school students’ union said the number of protesters on the streets across the country has “reached a new record” on Tuesday, according to Sky News.

The demonstration has been dubbed “Act Three” by the school union.

Images of the protest, which surfaced online, show riot police facing off with demonstrators in the capital.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The face-off on Monday between the protesters and riot police left several injured. A 15-year-old lost a hand in a grenade explosion in the northern city of Lens. Police reports said that he had picked up a stun grenade.

The AFP news agency reported that the student likely picked up a rubber sting-ball or ”de-encirclement” grenade, fired by riot police, in an attempt to throw it back before it exploded in his hand.

According to French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, hundreds of police officers and students have been injured during recent protests across the country.

Mr Lecornu told the French parliament this afternoon that at least 215 students have been injured since the protests began, alongside 85 school workers and 715 gendarmes and police officers.

He described the numbers as the highest in decades to affect workers in the education system.

He also condemned the “trivialisation” of violence, and said it was “unacceptable.”

“Burning down a high school does not improve the state of high school buildings,” he said. “Lynching a teacher does not help replace teachers.”

He also insisted it was a lie to suggest the government had ordered “police repression” against demonstrators.

World.title: FIFA knew DR Congo used an ineligible goalkeeper against Nigeria, report reveals
World.content:
FIFA is facing fresh questions over the circumstances surrounding Nigeria’s failure to qualify for the 2026 World Cup after reports revealed that its officials knew DR Congo goalkeeper Lionel Mpasi had not completed the process required to switch his international allegiance from France.

The revelation has revived Nigeria’s complaint over DR Congo’s use of players in the decisive World Cup qualifying play-off and raised questions about why no sporting punishment was imposed.

The Super Eagles lost to DR Congo 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw following extra time in the African play-off final in Rabat, Morocco, on 16 November 2025.

Mpasi played all 120 minutes of the match.

Nigeria subsequently complained to FIFA, challenging the eligibility of several DR Congo players. The complaint was rejected on technical grounds.

But a report by The New York Times, published Tuesday, said documents the newspaper reviewed showed that FIFA’s own legal officials later found that Mpasi had not completed the necessary process to change his international association from France to DR Congo.

Le Monde separately reported that FIFA lawyers discovered the problem in March 2026, shortly before DR Congo faced Jamaica in the intercontinental play-off.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mpasi, 32, was born in France and represented the country at youth level. According to the reports, DR Congo began the process to change his international association in 2021, but the process was never completed.

That meant, according to the FIFA documents cited by the reports, that he was not properly cleared to play for DR Congo.

FIFA considered options

The new information is particularly significant because FIFA reportedly considered what action could be taken after Nigeria’s complaint.

According to The New York Times, options considered by the FIFA committee included awarding the match to Nigeria, imposing a sanction on DR Congo, replacing DR Congo with Nigeria in the intercontinental play-off against Jamaica or taking no action because Nigeria’s complaint had been filed late.

The committee ultimately did not impose a sporting sanction that would have changed the qualification process.

FIFA told The New York Times that its committees are autonomous and decide cases based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts before them.

The governing body has not publicly accepted the claim that the handling of the case was improper.

The decision proved costly for Nigeria.

DR Congo went on to beat Jamaica in the intercontinental play-off in March, qualifying for the World Cup for the first time in 52 years.

The Leopards then reached the knockout stage of the tournament after drawing with Portugal and beating Uzbekistan. They lost 2-1 to England in the last 32, with Mpasi starting in goal.

Nigeria considers next steps

The latest reports have given Nigeria a fresh reason to revisit the case.

A senior National Sports Commission official told ESPN that Nigeria is considering seeking compensation from FIFA for the financial losses caused by missing the World Cup.

“Nothing has been decided yet, but we will seriously consider seeking compensation from FIFA for all of the economic losses this has cost Nigeria,” the official said.

The official said the possible losses include revenue that would have gone to the NFF and Super Eagles, sponsorship income, player exposure and the wider economic benefits of Nigeria’s participation in the tournament.

“We are exploring all our options as a country, and nothing is off the table,” the official said.

Former NFF president Ibrahim Gusau, who was in charge when Nigeria filed its complaint, also criticised FIFA’s handling of the matter.

“They just kept quiet, and they can’t tell anyone because they know it’s going to be a serious crisis for them,” Mr Gusau was quoted as saying by TheCable, arguing that FIFA had not fully disclosed what its investigation found.

The NFF had earlier said it was appealing FIFA’s rejection of its complaint.

Nigeria’s original case was broader than Mpasi’s eligibility. The federation had questioned the status of several DR Congo players and alleged that FIFA may have been given misleading information when clearing them to play.

Questions over Infantino

The latest controversy also places FIFA president Gianni Infantino under fresh scrutiny.

There is, however, no evidence in the reports that Mr Infantino personally ordered the case to be dismissed or took part in the decision.

The issue has attracted attention partly because of Infantino’s relationship with Véron Mosengo-Omba, the president of the Congolese football federation.

The two men have a long professional relationship, having studied at university in Switzerland and later worked within European and world football structures.

The New York Times reported that the handling of the eligibility case has raised questions about whether political considerations within football influenced the decision. FIFA maintains that its judicial committees are independent.

The timing is also significant. Infantino is expected to meet African football officials in Cape Verde this week as he seeks support ahead of the FIFA presidential election scheduled for March.

Africa has 54 FIFA member associations, making the continent an important voting bloc.

Previous cases raise questions

FIFA has previously taken strong action against teams that fielded ineligible players.

South Africa forfeited a 2026 World Cup qualifier against Lesotho after using suspended midfielder Teboho Mokoena.

Bolivia also forfeited two 2018 World Cup qualifying matches after fielding Nelson Cabrera, who was found to be ineligible.

The new DR Congo revelations have therefore raised questions about whether FIFA applied its rules consistently in Nigeria’s case.

For Nigeria, the issue is now bigger than simply returning to the 2026 World Cup.

The Super Eagles have already missed the tournament, but the NFF and NSC could still seek a review of FIFA’s handling of the complaint and consider possible financial claims.

Whether FIFA will reopen the case remains unclear.

World.title: BBNaija Season 11: Temi Nkem receives N90 million, Hyundai SUV, other prizes
World.content:
Big Brother Naija Season 11 winner, Temi Nkem, has officially received the brand-new SUV included in her ₦160 million prize package.

The 21-year-old reality TV star took delivery of the vehicle on Tuesday, two days after she was crowned winner of the “Show Ya Sef” edition of the reality show.

Temi arrived at the prize presentation in a royal-blue dress, accompanied by her mother, with several of her fellow Season 11 housemates also present.

The new SUV was displayed at the venue against a branded backdrop featuring Big Brother Naija, MultiChoice, DStv, GOtv and betPawa branding, as representatives formally handed over the vehicle and its keys to the new winner.

Temi, visibly excited during the presentation, thanked God, her family, her fans, the “Teminators,” and everyone who supported and voted for her throughout her 70-day stay in the Big Brother house.

Her car handover completes the physical presentation of the major components of the Season 11 grand prize.

How Temi won BBNaija season 11

Temi was crowned winner during the live finale on Sunday, 4 October, after polling 25.87 per cent of the final votes.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She defeated Aikou, who finished as first runner-up with 23.68 per cent, while Sheba placed third with 9.80 per cent. Temi’s winning margin over Aikou was 2.19 percentage points.

The finale brought an end to 10 weeks of competition involving 24 housemates, with Temi emerging as the fifth female winner in Big Brother Naija history.

Her prize package is valued at ₦160 million and includes ₦90 million in cash, a brand-new SUV and other sponsored prizes. The cash component was reduced from the original ₦100 million after ₦10 million was allocated to the season’s Most Influential Player of the Week (MIPOW) fund.

Temi’s victory came after a season marked by weekly tasks, Head of House competitions, nominations, evictions and several twists, including the Gambit and changing Head of House powers.

She leaves the reality show with both the title and the major physical components of the prize package, following the formal presentation of her winner’s SUV on Tuesday.

World.title: Military Aircraft Crash: Manual bush cutting, difficult terrain impede rescue operation
World.content:
The site of the ATR-42 aircraft crash at Igbokoda, in Ilaje LGA of Ondo State, on Tuesday, witnessed apprehension from residents over the slow and unprofessional deployment of rescue efforts.

Rescue teams arrived at the site of the crash at about 2 p.m. to join some locals who rode on canoes, using machetes to cut through the bush leading to the crash site.

Although the Ondo State Government had ordered the deployment of logistics to the site, the state’s amphibious escavator did not arrive Igbokoda until 1 p.m. on Tuesday.

The difficult terrain also hampered its deployment in the water and as of 2 p.m. on Tuesday when this report was filed, the escavator that would have speeded up the process was still ashore.

With the inability of the escavator to get in, rescuers comprising NEMA officials, firemen, police, soldiers and locals manually paddled their boats into the narrow and grassy water way to commence operations.

Many residents who either came to show sympathy or wanted to see what was going on said they were not sure if the boats could make it to the spot because of the difficulty.

Ondo State Maritime Commander, R. Gajere, said he was the first to locate the site and was only able to access it by a canoe.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Gajere spoke to journalists at Igbokoda shortly after the police leadership paid an on the spot visit to the crash site.

He said he and his team managed to pull out a few pieces of bodies and plane parts.

He solicited cooperation among operating agencies to ensure quick and through evacuation.

World.title: EFCC opposes Diezani’s move to present evidence of UK court acquittal in Abuja case
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has opposed former Minister of Petroleum Resources Diezani Alison-Madueke’s application to present evidence of her acquittal of bribery charges by the Southwark Crown Court, London in the United Kingdom.

The anti-graft agency urged Judge Inyang Ekwo to dismiss the application.

The commission, which filed a counter-affidavit against the application, maintained that the purported acquittal of Mrs Alison-Madueke by a foreign criminal court was not material or relevant to the specific issues for determination before the instant court.

In an earlier filing, the EFCC stated that the assets Mrs Alison-Madueke was seeking to retrieve through the legal action, which has been ongoing since 2023, had been auctioned off based on court orders.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the judge, on 1 July, granted the application filed by the ex-minister to present evidence of the London court.

Mofesomo Oyetibo, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) who appeared for the EFCC at the time, did not oppose the application.

EFCC’s concession to the application, moved by the former minister’s lawyer Godwin Iyinbor, prompted the judge to grant the application.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The UK acquittal

The UK court’s judgement delivered on 17 June cleared Mrs Alison-Madueke of all bribery charges brought against her by British prosecutors.

Mrs Alison-Madueke, who served as Nigeria’s petroleum minister between 2010 and 2015 under former President Goodluck Jonathan, was acquitted of five counts of accepting bribes and one count of conspiracy to commit bribery.

British prosecutors alleged in the case that Mrs Alison-Madueke received lavish benefits and enjoyed what they described as “a life of luxury” in London, funded by oil and gas industry figures seeking favourable treatment and lucrative contracts in Nigeria’s petroleum sector.

They argued that the benefits were provided in exchange for the oil and gas contracts she awarded during her tenure as petroleum minister between 2010 and 2015.

However, the former minister had maintained throughout the trial that she neither accepted bribes nor exercised direct control over the award of government contracts.

The UK discharged and acquitted the embattled former minister of the bribery charges after a jury at the London court returned not-guilty verdicts.

Mrs Alison-Madueke faces pending corruption charges and a flurry of forfeiture orders on slews of assets traced to her back in Nigeria as she came under investigations and prosecutions in the UK.

Battle to recover forfeited assets

The former minister who left Nigeria in 2015 shortly after she left office commenced her suit, suing EFCC as the sole defendant in 2023, to stop the auctioning of her forfeited assets.

She filed an amended version of the suit in February 2025.

In the aftermath of her acquittal by the EFCC in June, filed an application to showcase the UK judgement as evidence of her innocence and legitimate acquisition of the assets.

EFCC has stated in a filing that the assets had been auctioned off based on court orders.

During the previous court sitting, Mrs Alison-Madueke’s lawyer, Mr Iyinbor, moved a motion seeking the permission to file a further/supplementary affidavit for the purpose of bringing fresh and material development with respect to her acquittal by the UK court.

EFCC’s lawyer, Ms Oyetibo, did not raise any objection to the filing the application, leaving the judge with no choice than to grant the request.

The former minister’s lawyer then proceeded to file the further/supplementary affidavit, against which the EFCC filed a counter-affidavit.

In the agency’s counter-affidavit sworn by Oyakhilome Ekienabor, a litigation officer in Ms Oyetibo’s law firm, the EFCC opposed Mrs Alison-Madueke’s request to present the evidence.

EFCC’s opposition

At Tuesday’s proceedings, Queen-Ubokutom Uwe, who appeared for Mrs Alison-Madueke, informed the court the EFCC had just served with EFCC’s further counter-affidavit in response to her client’s further/supplementary affidavit.

She equally reminded the court of their motion to regularise their processes.

Responding, Paul Mgbeoma, who appeared for the EFCC on Tuesday, expressed surprise at the frequency of Mrs Alison-Madueke’s new filings as if it was an election petition case.

Mr Mgbeoma then told the court that he was ready to proceed with the hearing.

The judge consequently fixed 11 November for hearing of the motions.

NAN reports that EFCC’s further counter-affidavit filed on 5 October, described several claims in Mrs Alison-Maduelke’s further affidavit as misleading, immaterial and irrelevant to the substantive issues for determination in her present suit.

“The proceedings before the Southwark Crown Court, London, United Kingdom, and the purported acquittal of the applicant therein, are in respect of a proceeding that is not being prosecuted before any Nigerian court and have nothing to do with the substantive suit before this honourable court,” wrote Oyakhilome Ekienabor who swore the anti-graft agency’s counter-affidavit.

The agency maintained in the filing that there is nothing in the public sale notice indicating that any of the properties listed therein belong to the applicant.

It added that “the order for forfeiture relates exclusively to items of jewelry and does not extend to any other category of assets or properties.”

It accused the applicant of trying to expand the scope of her case through the fresh filings.

“The applicant’s further/supplementary affidavit introduces irrelevant facts into this suit, thereby diverting attention from the core issues before this honourable court,” the counter-affidavit read.

He, therefore, urged the court to reject the further/supplementary affidavit seeking to present evidence of her acquittal in the UK court.

The suit

NAN recalls Mrs Alison-Madueke filed the suit through her lead counsel, Mike Ozekhome.

She argued, as part of the 10 grounds cited in support of the suit, that she commenced the suit challenging, among other things, the public notice issued by the EFCC for the public auction/sale of properties and/or personal effects affecting her proprietary rights.

“A major plank of the applicant’s case before this honourable court is that the respondent had sought to visit the applicant with grave proprietary consequences without conviction, without fair hearing, and without strict compliance with the relevant statutory provisions regulating forfeiture, management and disposal of properties,” her lawyer argued.

The filing added that the amended suit was filed on 19 February 2025 based on the leave of the court granted on 17 February 2025.

“After the filing of the applicant’s processes and while this suit was still pending before this honourable court, a subsequent and material event occurred, to wit: the applicant was acquitted by the Southwark Crown Court, London, United Kingdom, on 17 June 2026, of criminal allegations of bribery brought against her, a proceeding of obvious material relevance to the allegations repeatedly referenced in relation to the applicant.

“The said subsequent development is material and relevant to the applicant’s case, particularly as it relates to the issues of absence of conviction, fair hearing, due process, propriety of irreversible proprietary deprivation, and the need for strict compliance with statutory safeguards before disposal of properties affecting the applicant’s proprietary rights,” the court document read.

READ ALSO: EFCC hands over N107m recovered from property fraud to Lagos victim

It added that the ex-minister did not seek by this application to invite the court to sit in appeal over the said foreign decision or to treat the decision as automatically conclusive of the Nigerian proceedings.

However, the document stated the application is to enable Mrs Alison-Madueke to place before the court subsequent material fact which would assist the court in doing substantial justice.

According to Mr Ozekhome who filed the application on behalf of the former minister, the said fact was not available at the time the applicant filed her earlier processes and could not have been pleaded or deposed to earlier.

He submitted that the court had the power and discretion to allow a party to file the application where such facts would assist the court in the just determination of the issues before it.

He said EFCC would not be prejudiced by the grant of the application.

He said it would be in the interest of justice to grant the application.

(NAN)

World.title: Religious leaders applaud Uba Sani’s inclusive governance
World.content:
Governor Uba Sani’s inclusive leadership style, which emphasises even development across Kaduna State, and the governance philosophy of fairness and justice to all and sundry, have been applauded by religious leaders.

Muslim and Christian clerics commended the Governor for leading the State well at a Special Interfaith Dialogue which held at the Brigadier Abba Kyari Banquet Hall on Monday.

The religious leaders pointed out that Kaduna State now enjoys relative peace and harmony, including peaceful co-existence between Muslims and Christians, since he assumed office over three years ago.

At the event which was organised by the Kaduna State Bureau of Interfaith, speakers noted that the present administration has recorded a lot of achievements and most of them canvassed for Uba Sani’s re-election to continue with what he has started.

Speaking at the occasion, Uba Sani recalled that when he assumed office in 2023, he promised to run an inclusive Government which has now won the hearts and minds of not just the people of Kaduna State but the country at large.

‘’People have been asking me about our model. Our model is very simple. It does not need any study. It is about justice. It is about brining everyone to the table,’’ he emphasised.

‘’When we came into office, we inherited a state that was highly toxic and divided. As a Governor, I allocated land to some people but they refused to build in those places because of their faiths.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

‘’For me, it is unacceptable and we should not allow it to continue in Kaduna State. We are supposed to be the model for everyone to copy in Nigeria. We are determined to restore the glory of Kaduna State.

‘’We are the most diverse state in Nigeria, the most cosmopolitan but unfortunately, we allowed politics to always dictate the direction of our political leaders,’’ he argued.

Uba Sani reiterated that on 29th May, 2023, he took an oath of office and swore by the Glorious Qur’an to be fair to everyone, irrespective of their ethno-religious affiliations.

In his speech, the Kaduna State Chapter of the Chairman of Christian Association of Nigeria(CAN), Rev Caleb Ma’aji, said that the governor has done well and achieved a lot for the state.

Rev Ma’aji recalled that when Governor Uba Sani attend the Christmas Carol on the 22nd of December, 2024, he had requested three main road projects on behalf of his people.

The CAN Chairman who listed the Nasarawa-UNTL-First Bank road, the PAN Drive-Television Garage-Sabon Tasha road and the Romi-Karatudu road as the project, expressed gratitude that two of the roads have been completed and the third one is almost completed.

‘’Last year, His Excellency re-introduced the Christian pilgrimage to Jordan and Jerusalem. We want to place it on record that this is an act that we truly appreciate.

‘’His Excellency sponsored 50 Christians to Jordan and Jerusalem and this year we trust that he will double the number by the Grace of God,’’ Rev Maáji further said.

The clergyman also thanked Governor Uba Sani for the selection of Mr Jerry Adams as his running mate in the coming election, which ‘’is a departure from the culture of old.’’

On his part, the Secretary General of of Jamaátul Nasir Islam, Prof Khalid Aliyu, noted that the theme of the Special Interfaith Dialogue, which is ‘’An Overview of the Impactful Three Years of Peaceful Coexistence and Inclusivity In Kaduna State: Unveiling The Secret’’, coincides with the International Day of Peace.

Prof Aliyu who disclosed that the theme of this year’s International Day of Peace is ‘’Invest In Peace, For Everyone, In Everywhere, Everyday’’, described the Governor as a peacemaker.

Speaking at the occasion, Sheikh Haliru Maraya enumerated the achievements of the Governor Uba Sani administration, which include the slashing of tuition fees in all Kaduna State-owned tertiary institutions to increase access.

According to him, under the previous administration, 4,876 lives were lost due to insecurity and 7,694 people were kidnapped at that time, while 1,660 insecurity incidents were recorded.

‘’Before the coming of this administration, there were 534 schools that were closed due to insecurity. As at today, there is not a single school in Kaduna State that is not open.

‘’Before now, there were 500 hectres of uncultivated land due to insecurity. Right now, owners of those farmlands have returned to their farms,’’ he said, adding that Governor Uba Sani’s ‘’three years, four months and six days in office has brought development in Kaduna State. ‘’

In his goodwill message, the National Secretary of Pentecostal Fellowship of Nigeria(PFN), Bishop David Bakare, confessed that he didn’t vote for Governor Uba Sani in 2023 when he contested the election.

‘’I didn’t believe in anything that you were going to do. I didn’t know you. Your handlers didn’t effectively market you to us well. It is after you began your work in Kaduna State, that I asked myself why I didn’t vote for you.

‘’Now, another opportunity is standing in front of me and I didn’t have to think twice to take a decision this time around, it is not just about me but many,’’ he confessed.

World.title: Vote for NDC is vote to kill APGA — Opara
World.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) has warned its members against supporting the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying any vote for the opposition party would amount to a vote against APGA.

The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Ejimofor Opara, stated this in a statement on recent political developments which, he said, required clarity and guidance for APGA members.

Opara specifically criticised the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, alleging that he had worked against APGA in successive electoral cycles.

“For every seat APGA is contesting, why does Mr Peter Obi have a lineup of candidates waiting to push APGA away? APGA made Peter Obi, yet Peter Obi wants to destroy APGA,” he said.

Opara alleged that Obi had sought to weaken APGA since 2014, saying the former governor of Anambra State supported opposition forces against the party during previous elections.

“Since 2014, Mr Peter Obi has had one mission — to destroy the party that made him. In 2025, while President Bola Ahmed Tinubu stood with APGA, Peter Obi backed the opposition to bury us. Just like he did in 2017 and 2021,” he said.

The APGA spokesman also denied any formal or informal agreement between APGA and the NDC on power-sharing.

“There is no formal or informal consultation or agreement between APGA and NDC for power-sharing. As of today, the NDC is merely a Special Purpose Vehicle, while APGA is a Political Party of Record,” he said.

Opara said APGA’s support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu was not based solely on an unwritten convention of collaborating with the party at the centre.

He said the support was also based on what he described as Tinubu’s commitment to infrastructure development in the Southeast.

“APGA’s support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is not only predicated on the unwritten convention that the party collaborates with the party at the centre.

“It is more fundamentally anchored on the fact that President Tinubu has demonstrated utmost good faith in the infrastructural development of the Southeast, more than any other government since Nigeria’s return to democracy in 1999. This is absolutely factual and verifiable,” he said.

Opara urged APGA members not to be persuaded by what he described as Obi’s abandonment of the party, alleging that he had continued to treat political parties as “Special Purpose Vehicles” to be used and abandoned.

World.title: Umahi To South-East: Don’t live in denial, appreciate Tinubu
World.content:
John Alechenu



Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, has urged Nigerians, especially South-Easterners, to acknowledge infrastructure strides under President Bola Tinubu.

This was contained in a statement by his Senior Special Assistant on Media, Francis Nwaze, in Abuja on Tuesday.

Umahi spoke on Saturday at the 10th Anniversary of De Pinnacle Club International at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre, Abuja.

The Minister, honoured with an Award of Excellence in Public Service and Infrastructural Transformation, said politics should not blind people to tangible progress.

“We shouldn’t live in denial. We have to appreciate President Bola Ahmed Tinubu; even God Almighty appreciates gratitude. It doesn’t stop us from asking for more,” he said.

He said the South-East provides visible examples of projects that moved from years of deterioration to active construction or substantial completion.

He listed the Enugu-Onitsha Expressway, Enugu-Port Harcourt Expressway, Eke-Obinagu Flyover, New Artisan Bridge, Enugu-Abakaliki Road, Calabar-Ebonyi-Benue-Nasarawa-Abuja superhighway and access roads to the Second Niger Bridge.

Umahi said although the Second Niger Bridge was completed before Tinubu assumed office, it could not deliver full economic value due to poor access roads.

“We had the Second Niger Bridge fully completed before President Tinubu came into office, but the means of fully utilising the bridge, which is the access roads, was bad. So we are now building the access roads,” he said.

He said the Anambra section is about 40 per cent complete and the Asaba axis 35 per cent.

He also cited the Lagos-Shagamu Road as a critical link for millions travelling from Lagos through Ogun and Edo to Asaba and beyond.

Umahi said the Tinubu administration has shown unprecedented inclusion of the South-East, noting appointments of an Igbo as Chief of Air Staff and, for the first time, Ministers of Foreign Affairs and Works from the zone.

On vandalism of the First Niger Bridge, Umahi said he was alerted via social media that scrap scavengers were removing bolts and expansion metals.

He said intervention has commenced and the bridge will be fitted with CCTV and control points like the Third Mainland Bridge in Lagos to check vandalism and accidents.

The anniversary, themed “A Decade of Excellence, Legacy and Impact,” was attended by Foreign Affairs Minister Bianca Ojukwu, businessman Obi Cubana, Chief Kenneth Ifekudu and Amb. Elijah Onyeagba, among others.

The club said the award recognised Umahi’s adoption of concrete road technology, stronger accountability and accelerated execution of federal highway projects under the Renewed Hope Agenda.

Umahi dedicated the honour to President Tinubu and to engineers and contractors working nationwide.

World.title: 2027: APC warns members against anti-party activities
World.content:
By Hadiza Yusuf

The All Progressives Congress (APC) has warned its members against engaging in anti-party activities ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The warning was issued on Tuesday at the APC SAK Kano North 2027 programme, where party leaders urged members to remain loyal to the party and support its candidates.

The APC Zonal Chairman for Kano North, Abdullahi Magaji Lamba Bichi, said members were expected to vote for the party’s candidates across all positions.

He said the party’s constitution entitled its members to vote for APC candidates from the top to the bottom of the ballot.

Bichi warned that members who voted for other political parties while supporting APC candidates in other positions could face disciplinary action.

“Anyone who engages in anti-party activities should know that there are consequences. It can affect your position and may lead to disciplinary action by the party,” he said.

He described disagreements within the party as internal matters that could be resolved, urging members to put their differences aside and work together ahead of the elections.

“The minor disagreements within the party are internal and normal, but it is time for us to put them aside, unite and vote for APC candidates from the top to the bottom.

“We must work together to ensure the success of the APC in Kano and across Nigeria, and defeat the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC),” he said.

He also called on APC supporters to embark on grassroots mobilisation and support the party’s candidates, including President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, and candidates for the House of Representatives and State House of Assembly.

The zonal chairman urged members to ensure that the party secured votes across all positions on the ballot.

He also said the APC would reward loyal supporters with plots of land.

Bichi reaffirmed the commitment of the Kano North Senatorial District APC leadership to party unity, discipline and loyalty.

Earlier, the Chairman of the APC in Gharin Local Government Area, Shittu Madaki, welcomed party supporters to the programme and urged them to remain committed to the party.

World.title: Rivers 2027: Why I withdrew Supreme Court case against Fubara — Dumo
World.content:
By Daniel Abia, P/Harcourt

The governorship candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC), Chief Dumo Lulu-Briggs, has explained why he withdrew his case against Governor Siminalayi Fubara at the Supreme Court following the 2023 governorship election in Rivers State.

Lulu-Briggs said he withdrew the case after considering the interest of the Ijaw people above other considerations.

He disclosed this during a media chat with journalists in Buguma, headquarters of Asari-Toru Local Government Area of Rivers State, on Monday.

The NDC candidate said the circumstances surrounding his governorship contests in 2015, 2019 and 2023 were different, noting that several legal issues had affected his ambition in the earlier elections.

According to him, his decision to withdraw the 2023 case at the Supreme Court followed an intervention by the late Pa Edwin Clark and a subsequent appeal by Fubara.

Speaking on the 2023 election, Lulu-Briggs said Clark contacted him and drew his attention to what he described as Fubara’s strong support among the people of Rivers State.

He said Clark appealed to him to withdraw the case, warning that Rivers people might not forgive him if the Supreme Court annulled the election on the strength of his case and the then-Speaker of the Rivers State House of Assembly, Martin Amaewhule, became acting governor.

“He argued that Rivers people would not forgive me if the Supreme Court annulled the election on the strength of my case and the Speaker became Acting Governor,” Lulu-Briggs quoted Clark as saying.

He added that Clark was of the view that Fubara might not secure the ticket to contest another election because of the political crisis between the governor and his predecessor and political associate, Nyesom Wike.

Lulu-Briggs further said that following Clark’s intervention, Fubara personally approached him and appealed to him to withdraw the case.

The NDC governorship candidate said his decision to withdraw the Supreme Court case should not be interpreted as an abandonment of his ambition to govern Rivers State.

He said his clarification was intended to set the record straight on his political ambition.

World.title: A timeline of Nigeria Air Force crashes
World.content:
A Nigerian Air Force plane carrying 25 military and civilian passengers crashed in southwestern Ondo state on Monday, killing all on board.

The accident was one of the worst air diasters in the country in recent years.

Here are some major air crashes involving the Air Force in Africa’s most populous nation, which has one of the strongest militaries on the continent.

– 1980 –

A Fokker F27 aircraft travelling from Lagos to the neighbouring island nation of Sao Tome crashed in Forcados in southern Delta state on May 26, killing all 30 people aboard. It was carrying a Nigerian delegation comprising government officials, army officers and journalists when it came down.

1992 –

A Lockheed C-130H Hercules transport plane crashed and killed all 159 passengers aboard in Ejigbo, Lagos, shortly after taking off from Lagos airport on September 26. Most of the passengers were military officers.

– 1997 –

A Dornier Do 128 plane used for training crashed and killed all three officials on it about three kilometres from the runway of the Kaduna airport on February 24.

– 2000

All six people on a Dornier Do 128 plane were killed when it crashed while approaching the runway at the Warri airport in oil-rich Delta state on October 26.

– 2006

An 18-seater Dornier 228 military transport plane carrying 15 senior army officers and three crew members crashed in Benue State on September 17. Three people survived the crash.

– 2015

A Dornier 228 plane went out of control shortly after taking off from a military air base in Kaduna and crashed into a house in a military cantonment, killing all the seven aboard.

– 2019

An attack helicopter providing support for troops fighting a jihadist insurgency in northeastern Nigeria crashed and killed all five people on board on January 2.

– 2021

On February 21, seven air force officials died when a Beechcraft King Air crashed en route Abuja airport after suffering engine failure on its way to central Niger state, where it was to go on a reconnaissance flight ahead of a mission to free kidnapped schoolgirls, according to the Nigeria Air Force.

– 2021 –

A Beechcraft King Air crashed in bad weather in May while trying to land at northern Kaduna state airport. All 11 people on board, including Lieutenant General Ibrahim Attahiru, then commander of the country’s army, died in the crash.

AFP

World.title: Trump blames France unrest on ‘mass migration,’ Islam
World.content:
Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP.

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday blamed mass student protests in France on “mass migration” and Islam, pushing his global right-wing narrative ahead of tough midterm elections at home.

“What’s happening in France is nothing less than out of control mass migration. This isn’t about schools, this is about Islam wanting to take over a once great Country!” Trump said in a post on Truth Social.

French students have blocked the entrances to hundreds of high schools across the country since late September to demand better conditions, in protests that have descended into sporadic clashes with security forces.

A quarter of a million demonstrators took to the streets across France on Tuesday.

But Trump and his administration have long blamed European social issues on migration, calling on Europe to shut its borders and echoing far-right parties by warning of what they call civilizational decline.

Leading voices in Trump’s Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement have been using the French protests to ram home points about immigration ahead of the US midterm elections next month.

MAGA commentators have repeatedly posted videos of the French unrest, with Trump ally Glenn Beck saying on Monday that the “riots in France are a clear warning to the rest of the West.”

Republicans are doubling down on migration and anti-transgender rhetoric amid fears that Trump’s unpopularity and his Iran war risk losing them control of Congress.

World.title: Shakira, Pique return to court over children visit arrangements
World.content:
Pop star Shakira and her former partner, retired Spanish footballer Gerard Pique, appeared at a Barcelona court on Tuesday to review visitation arrangements for their two children, with the singer seeking changes to limit their travel between the US and Spain.

The Colombian singer has asked for fewer short transatlantic trips by their sons between Miami, where they live with her, and Barcelona, where Pique lives, according to a statement from her legal team.

She argues that frequent travel could affect their emotional, physical and academic wellbeing, her representatives said.

Under her proposal, Pique would travel to Miami during shorter school holidays, allowing the children to spend more time in their home environment and maintain their routines.

The request is not intended to reduce the amount of time the children spend with their father, they added.

Shakira, 49, and Pique, 39, began their relationship in 2011 and have two boys, Milan, born in 2013, and Sasha, born in 2015.

The couple, who lived mainly in Barcelona during their relationship, announced their separation in June 2022 after more than a decade together.

They reached an agreement over custody and visitation arrangements several months later, after which the “Hips Don’t Lie” singer moved to Miami with the kids.

Pique, who played for Barcelona and Spain before retiring from professional football in 2022, has regular periods with his sons each month as well as during school holidays.

Shakira is currently in Madrid for the final leg of a global tour, with 13 concerts scheduled between September 18 and October 12. She added an extra date on Monday.

She began her “Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran” world tour in February 2025, taking its name from her album of the same title.

The album includes “Bzrp Music Sessions, Vol. 53”, her global hit collaboration with Argentine producer Bizarrap, which referenced her split from Pique.

World.title: Scrap NYSC or let participants serve in their states – NAPTAN tells FG
World.content:
File image

By Adesina Wahab

Parents under the aegis of the National Parent Teacher Association of Nigeria, NAPTAN, have called on the Federal Government to scrap the National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, Scheme or allow participants to observe it in their states of origin.

This, according to the association, has become imperative following the soft targets members and prospective members of the scheme have become in the hands of criminal elements who kidnap them.

Speaking in an interview with Vanguard on Tuesday, the Chairman, Board of Trustees of NAPTAN, Chief Adeolu Ogunbanjo, expressed sadness that the scheme is being turned to a curse rather than a blessing to parents and participants.

“Parents are not happy with the incessant abduction and kidnap of our children going for the NYSC scheme. This must stop. Our children that we suffer to train in school should not be seen as soft targets by criminal elements such as kidnappers. They are not items of merchandise that somebody will be haggling about how much to pay for their release.

“There is no doubt that the idea behind the setting up of the scheme is good, but the realities of today are not fully supporting that. Let us look at the percentage of parents who can say their wards or children should go by air to their places of deployment; it may be less than five per cent. It means no matter how long the distance, more than 95 per cent of corps members travel by road to their states of deployment.

“One can imagine the various hazards on the road, even the state of our highways. Highways that are prone to accidents. Is the risk worth it? We are suggesting that the government should let corps members serve in their states of origin. At least, Yoruba elders say that your father’s house cannot be a threat to you.

“Even the condition under which most corps members serve is not good enough. We call for the improvement in the various orientation camps. Graduates should not be treated as animals. Most employers don’t even provide the corps members basic things for their comfort. They don’t give them accommodation.

“Regarding the corps members that are being held captive by abductors, please all hands must be on deck to ensure their quick and safe return. When the kidnappers are demanding millions of naira, where do they expect the parents to raise such money from? Parents who could not afford to send their wards by plane to those places,” he stated.

Ogunbanjo prayed for the quick release of the 19 corps members being help-captive in Imo State.

World.title: Expert Tasks Nigerians on Healthy Eating Habits
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

A medical expert, Dr. Ademola Tosin Ojo, has urged Nigerians to embrace healthy and balanced eating habits, stressing that proper nutrition is essential to preventing diseases and maintaining overall wellbeing.

Ojo, while speaking on ‘Healthy Eating and Nutrition-Food as Medicine’, explained that a healthy diet should include vegetables, fruits, beans, fish, eggs, whole grains and other nutritious foods, while excessive salt, added sugars and unhealthy fats should be limited.

According to him, good nutrition supports energy, growth, immunity and normal body functions, while also helping to reduce the risk of conditions such as heart disease and type 2 diabetes.

He advised Nigerians not to completely eliminate carbohydrates from their diets, but to choose nutritious, high-fibre sources and maintain appropriate portions.

The medical expert also encouraged people to make water their main beverage and reduce their consumption of sugary drinks and highly processed foods.

Ojo noted that healthy eating does not have to be expensive, stressing that affordable locally available foods such as beans, seasonal vegetables, fruits and eggs can provide essential nutrients.

He further advised people living with hypertension and diabetes to adopt appropriate dietary habits while following the treatment plans prescribed by their healthcare professionals.

He then urged Nigerians to make healthy eating a lifestyle, summarising his message in three principles: eat a variety of nutritious foods, control portions, and limit excessive salt, added sugars, and unhealthy fats.

World.title: NGX Urges East African Investors to Key into Dangote’s Vision of Locally-sourced Capital
World.content:
Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja

Chairman of the Nigeria Exchange Group (NGX), Alhaju Umaru Kwairanga, has urged East African investors to embrace the vision of billionaire industrialist, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, by largely relying on locally-sourced capital rather than expensive and unstable foreign loans.

Kwairanga spoke during a high-level investment engagement at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE), Kenya recently.

The NGX Group Chairman underlined the transformational impact of the Dangote Refinery in Nigeria, and expressed confidence that a similar one planned for Kenya will have the same positive impact on the whole of East Africa.

He is also taking that even further by relying to a large extent on locally sourced capital rather than expensive and fickle foreign loans.

He said: “We have already seen the transformational impact of the Dangote Refinery in Lagos Nigeria and I am confident that the one planned for Kenya will have the same positive impact on the whole of East Africa.

“He (Aliko Dangote) is also taking that even further by relying to a large extent on locally sourced capital rather than expensive and fickle foreign loans.

“I invite our East African investors to key into this vision and give leaders like this the capital and support to take Africa to another higher level of development.

“You will be making a good investment decision for yourself and for future generations of Africans.”

He recalled that in recent years, African leaders such as President William Ruto of Kenya and Nigeria’s President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, advocated for Africa to come together and work towards solving its developmental challenges.

That call, he noted, is being met in many practical ways by visionary entrepreneurs like Alhaji Dangote.

“In Nigeria, we have seen how he has led Nigeria’s turnaround from a cement importing nation to one that is self sufficient in cement and even exports the product.

“Now he is doing the same in fertilizer and petroleum products and spreading that vision of an industrialised African continent led by African visionaries across the continent,” he said.

World.title: FMC Yenagoa Seeks FG’s Intervention, Bemoans Non-release of Funds for Capital Projects,
World.content:
Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja

The Medical Director of the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, Dr. James Enimi Omietimi, has raised concerns over the non-release of the centre’s 2025 capital allocation, saying the development has negatively impacted the progress of ongoing projects and the overall operations of the medical facility.

Omietimi, who made this known when he received the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC) team conducting physical verification of select Federal Government projects in the South-south region, particularly called for the timely release of capital allocations, to enable the institution complete its ongoing projects and provide effective healthcare services.

The FRC verification team, led by the Head of the Strategic Communication Directorate of the commission, Mr. Bede Ogueri Anyanwu, visited the FMC, Yenagoa, as part of the commission’s ongoing exercise to ascertain the level of implementation of some capital projects funded by the Federal Government.

According to a statement from the FRC,

Omietimi said the delay in the release of the 2025 capital funds had made it difficult for the centre to sustain the momentum of work on its ongoing projects.

The situation, he said, has also exposed the institution to operational challenges, making it increasingly difficult to provide the expected level of healthcare services to residents of Bayelsa State and neighbouring communities.

The statement quoted him as saying:

“We should not pretend because things have not been too good lately,” adding that the realities confronting healthcare institutions on the ground were sometimes different from what was being portrayed in the media.

He explained that the day-to-day realities of running a tertiary healthcare institution were demanding, noting that the centre had been struggling to keep the system functioning effectively amid the prevailing financial constraints.

Omietimi also expressed concern over the changing attitude of some residents towards orthodox medicine, noting that some patients now resort to traditional medicine practitioners before seeking professional medical attention.

He said many patients only return to FMC Yenagoa when their health conditions have deteriorated and require advanced medical intervention.

He appealed to the Federal Government to urgently intervene by ensuring adequate funding for the centre, particularly the timely release of capital allocations, to enable the institution complete its ongoing projects and provide effective healthcare services.

Earlier, the leader of the FRC verification team, Mr. Bede Ogueri Anyanwu, explained that the purpose of the exercise was to ascertain the extent to which funds appropriated and released for Federal Government projects were being utilised and to ensure that the projects deliver value to Nigerians.

Anyanwu said the exercise was part of the commission’s statutory responsibility of promoting transparency, accountability and prudent management of public funds, in line with the provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007.

He said that the presence of the FRC team at FMC Yenagoa was not intended to persecute the management of the centre or any government institution, but to establish the facts on the ground regarding the implementation of the selected projects.

“Our mission is to promote transparency, accountability and prudent management of public funds as contained in the mandate of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission and the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007,” Anyanwu said.

He added that the team was particularly interested in determining whether funds released for the projects had been appropriately utilised and whether the projects were achieving the intended objectives for which they were approved.

According to him, physical verification provides an opportunity for the commission to establish the actual status of projects, identify challenges affecting implementation and ensure that government investments translate into tangible benefits for citizens.

World.title: Senate Suspends National Security Summit Over NAF Crash
World.content:
• New date to be announced later

• Senate mourns fallen military personnel

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Senate has postponed indefinitely its planned two-day National Security Summit following the tragic crash of a Nigerian Air Force (NAF) ATR-42 aircraft in Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, which claimed the lives of 25 officers and seven crew members.

The National Security Summit, originally scheduled for Monday, October 12, and Tuesday, October 13, was convened by the upper chamber to examine Nigeria’s worsening security challenges and develop practical measures to strengthen the protection of lives and property across the country.

The Leader of the Senate and Chairman of the Senate Ad hoc Committee on the National Security Summit, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, announced the postponement in a statement he personally signed on Tuesday in Abuja.

Bamidele said the decision followed the declaration of three days of national mourning by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in honour of the military personnel who died in the crash.

The president had also directed that the national flag be flown at half-mast nationwide as the country mourns the fallen officers and crew members.

Explaining the Senate’s decision, Bamidele said the summit had been fully planned after the completion of the zonal public hearings, but the tragedy involving the NAF aircraft made it necessary for the Senate to suspend the event.

“The Senate has resolved to defer the National Security Summit till further notice in honour of the victims of the tragic crash involving a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft in Igbokoda, Ondo State,” he said.

The Senate Leader said the postponement was also in recognition of the gravity of the national tragedy and the period of mourning declared by the president.

He added that a fresh date for the summit would be announced in due course, urging stakeholders who had prepared to participate in the event to bear with the Senate.

The summit, according to the Senate, was designed to bring together key stakeholders to review Nigeria’s perennial security challenges and develop pragmatic recommendations capable of addressing threats to lives, property and national stability.

The upper chamber had already undertaken zonal public hearings as part of preparations for the summit, with the ad hoc committee concluding arrangements for the national gathering before Monday’s aircraft disaster.

Bamidele expressed the Senate’s condolences to President Tinubu, the Nigerian Armed Forces, particularly the Nigerian Air Force, and the families of the deceased personnel.

The Senate, he said, mourned the officers and crew members who “paid the supreme price in active service to the fatherland”.

The Senate Leader stated: “The Senate extends its heartfelt condolences to the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR; the Nigerian Armed Forces, particularly the Nigerian Air Force; and the families of the gallant officers and crew members who paid the supreme price in active service to the fatherland.”

He appealed to all stakeholders who had been expected at the summit to take note of the national disaster and understand the decision to defer the meeting.

“We appeal to all stakeholders to take note of the national disaster and bear with the Senate during this period of national mourning,” Bamidele added.

The postponement means that the Senate’s planned national conversation on the country’s security challenges will now await a new date.

The summit was expected to provide an opportunity for federal and state authorities, security agencies, lawmakers, experts and other stakeholders to assess the country’s security architecture and propose measures for improving the safety of Nigerians.

No new date was announced in the statement, with the Senate saying the details would be communicated in due course.

World.title: 2027: Ex-Gov Bello Returns Home, Ready for Senatorial Election
World.content:
Ahead of the 2027 general election, the immediate-past Governor of Kogi State, Yahaya Bello, has relocated to Okene, the headquarters of Kogi Central senatorial district in preparation for the electoral battle ahead.

Bello, who returned home to a massive reception organised by the supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 Kogi Central senatorial election, expressed gratitude for the support.

The homecoming, which attracted a huge crowd across the district, was marked by colourful displays, chants, and enthusiastic supporters who trooped out in large numbers to welcome the former governor and APC senatorial candidate.

Bello, who governed Kogi State from 2016 to 2024, emerged as the APC candidate for the Kogi Central senatorial seat after winning the party’s May 2026 primary.

They enumerated some of the legacy projects of Bello when he governed the state, declaring that the senatorial hopeful is naturally loved by the residents of Kogi State many years after meritoriously completing his two terms in office.

Many stakeholders and residents across Kogi Central who led their constituents to welcome Bello vowed to further demonstrate their gratitude for the “good works” of the former governor by voting for him massively next year.

In his remarks, former Kogi State APC Chairman and Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Abdullahi Bello, described the reception as a demonstration of the affection and confidence the people of Kogi Central have for the former governor.

“This is the homecoming of a leader that liberated the whole Ebiraland, and we all trooped out to welcome him. It is not an easy thing. We love him, and we have to demonstrate that,” Abdullahi Bello said.

He declared that the APC structure in Kogi Central was fully prepared for the forthcoming election, stressing that the district remained a stronghold of the party.

“I will not flatter you with words, but obviously, as you can see for yourself, Ebiraland in Kogi Central is the home of the All Progressives Congress. APC is here. APC lives here; and we preach APC,” he said.

According to him, the massive crowd witnessed during the homecoming was not merely a political gathering but an indication of the level of acceptance he said Bello enjoys among the people.

He expressed confidence that APC members and supporters across the five local government areas of Kogi Central would mobilise behind Bello at the polls, saying: “APC is 100 per cent prepared to vote Alhaji Yahaya Adoza Bello to the Red Chamber next year.”

Bello’s emergence as the APC flag bearer followed a direct primary in which he was declared winner with 72,399 votes across the district.

He said: “The era of using professional influence or advantage, I think, is over. The law will put an end to that when you beat a candidate mercilessly with a very clear margin. Then I think you’ll learn some lessons, and that is going to happen in this election.”

Addressing the overwhelming crowd that welcomed the former governor, the former APC chairman said he was not surprised by the turnout, insisting that Bello’s political appeal cuts across age and gender.

“I am not surprised because Alhaji Bello has done so much to the extent that every Ebira person, both young and old, man and woman, believes so much in him. Even if you hear his name, you just have to join the queue,” he said.

He further claimed that the message of the APC campaign was already resonating with party members and supporters across the district.

The former chairman also linked the reception to what he described as the security situation in Kogi Central during Bello’s tenure as governor, recalling that the area had previously experienced episodes of violence and insecurity.

“Before now, especially 2007 and 2008, this district used to be a battlefield, with burning of houses and killing of innocent people. But the coming of Alhaji Yahaya Bello put an end to all that,” he said.

Responding, the former governor expressed happiness at the show of love by his people, describing the massive crowd that came to honour him as “organic” and proof that the sense of appreciation of the people of the state, especially in Kogi Central, is “inborn.”

Addressing journalists at the palace of the Ohinoyi of Ebira Land, Bello emphatically stated that all APC candidates for the 2027 general election would emerge victorious at the polls, saying: “I have never doubted that my people are with me and supporting the APC 100 percent. I have never doubted that my people will support and vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu 100 percent, and I have never doubted that my people are with my governor, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo 100 percent.”

“I have never doubted that my people are going to vote for me as the senator representing Kogi Central and all of our other candidates on the platform of the APC because they know very well what this party has done to liberate our people and bring infrastructure to the people and ensure that the dividend of democracy is

delivered to our people and still being delivered to our people,” Bello pointed out.

Last Friday’s homecoming, according to stakeholders, provided a striking display of the mobilisation surrounding the former governor, with supporters turning out in large numbers to receive him as he formally reconnects with his political base ahead of the 2027 National Assembly election.

World.title: Ebonyi South Senatorial NDC Candidate Flags Off Campaign
World.content:
Benjamin Nworie in Abakaliki

A two-time member of the House of Representatives and Ebonyi South senatorial candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Hon. Linus Abaa-Okorie, has formally flagged off his campaign for the 2027 general election.

He stressed that he has learnt from previous service, and the zone can no longer afford representation that was ceremonial, distant, or uncertain.

Okorie said he would be a senator who would not disappear after the election but would operate a functional constituency system through which citizens can submit complaints, propose community projects and receive information on legitimate opportunities.

In his declaration at Okposi in Onicha Local Government Area of the state, the senatorial candidate noted that his zone must be represented by someone who can speak for their communities at home, engage institutions in Abuja and understand how wider development partnerships can be mobilised for opportunity.

According to Okorie: “I know the National Assembly. I know its possibilities. I also know its limits. I, therefore, ask you for your mandate not to experiment, but to work.

“I served for eight years in the House of Representatives, from 2011 to 2019. I chaired the House Committee on Agricultural Colleges and Institutions.

“I participated in legislation, appropriation, and oversight, worked with federal institutions, and facilitated employment, empowerment, education, healthcare, agricultural interventions, electricity projects, community development, and welfare support.

“For those eight years, I also served as a member of Nigeria’s standing delegation to the ACP-EU Joint Parliamentary Assembly (JPA) — the inter-parliamentary body that brought together parliamentarians from African, Caribbean and Pacific states and Members of the European Parliament, and whose successor framework is today the OACPS-EU Joint Parliamentary Assembly.”

He added: “That responsibility gave me practical exposure to international parliamentary cooperation, democratic oversight and partnership dialogue beyond our national borders.

“Through that platform, I engaged with issues that remain directly relevant to our people: human rights and democratic governance; sustainable and inclusive economic growth; trade and development cooperation; environmental sustainability and climate action; peace and security; and migration and mobility.”

“That experience matters because effective Senate representation should be able to connect local priorities with national policy and credible international partnerships.”

Okorie added: “Across Ebonyi South, the same story repeats itself in different forms. Graduates wait for jobs. Farmers wait for inputs and markets. Communities wait for development. Patients wait for healthcare. Traders wait for support. Artisans wait for tools. Young people wait for opportunities. Students wait for assistance, and indigent families wait for succour.”

He further added that all the candidates of the party in the zone were working together to ensure total victory in the general election.

World.title: New Google Trends Data Shows Nigerians’ Growing Taste for Cold Brew, Sweet Lattes
World.content:
Vanessa Obioha

Nigerians are showing growing interest in cold brews, dessert-inspired lattes and making café-style coffee at home, according to new Google Trends data.

Released following International Coffee Day on October 1, the data highlights the coffee varieties, flavours and equipment that attracted the most search interest in Nigeria in 2026, offering a glimpse into how Nigerians are exploring their coffee preferences.

Cold brew was the fastest-rising coffee search in Nigeria this year. Flat white and drip coffee also recorded strong growth, while instant coffee made the top five fastest-rising coffee searches.

Made by steeping coffee grounds in cold water, cold brew has gained attention as a refreshing alternative to hot coffee, particularly in Nigeria’s warm climate.

The trend is not limited to how coffee is served. Nigerians are also experimenting with sweeter flavours. Hazelnut latte was the top trending latte in 2026, followed by red velvet latte, cold brew latte, banana latte and Spanish latte.

These rankings reflect the latte varieties whose search interest grew fastest compared with the previous year, rather than those with the highest overall search volume. Red velvet and banana, for instance, are better known as desserts and snacks, while Spanish latte is traditionally made with condensed milk.

There is also growing interest in recreating the café experience at home. The French press was the fastest-rising coffee gadget in searches this year, while the kettle remained the most searched piece of coffee equipment. Coffeemakers, espresso machines and grinders followed, suggesting more Nigerians are exploring ways to prepare coffee at home.

Despite the growing appetite for new flavours and brewing methods, the classics remain firmly in the lead when it comes to overall search interest. Espresso was the most searched coffee in Nigeria in 2026, followed by latte, cappuccino, mocha and iced coffee.

The distinction between the two lists offers an interesting picture of Nigeria’s coffee culture: while the familiar varieties continue to attract the most searches overall, newer and more experimental options are gaining ground fastest.

Google said the search data also reflects how people increasingly use Search to explore coffee, from finding cafés nearby to learning how to prepare particular drinks at home.

With AI now integrated into Google Search, users can ask conversational questions such as which coffee is least bitter or how to make a Spanish latte at home and receive answers to guide their search.

Communications and Public Affairs Manager, West Africa at Google, Taiwo Kola-Ogunlade, said the trends showed Nigerians experimenting with coffee while adapting it to their tastes and social lives.

“We’re thrilled to see how much fun Nigerians are having with coffee. People are trying new flavours, hosting friends with drinks they have made themselves and putting a local twist on a global favourite,” he said.

Kola-Ogunlade added that Google Search, with AI built in, makes it easier for users to move from searching for information to preparing coffee at home.

World.title: H1 Report Puts Dapper Ahead of Nigerian-Owned Music Companies
World.content:
Iyke Bede

Dapper Music and Entertainment led Nigerian-owned music companies in the first half of 2026 with a 3.82 per cent market share, according to TurnTable Charts’ H1 2026 Market Share Report.

YBNL Nation followed with 2.40 per cent, while GIRAN Republic recorded 1.99 per cent.

The ranking places Dapper Music and Entertainment at the top of the Nigerian-owned category eight years after the company was established in 2018.

Reacting to the report, Dapper Group Founder and Group CEO, Damilola Akinwunmi, said the ranking reflected the work of the company’s artists and wider team.

“Eight years ago we started with a conviction that Nigerian music built properly, artist first and for the long term, could compete with anyone. To be recognised at the top of this list is a reflection of that work, and it belongs to every artist, writer, producer and member of this team who has contributed to it. We are building for the next eight years, not celebrating the last.”

Dapper Music and Entertainment is the record label arm of Dapper Group, a Lagos-based music and entertainment company. The wider group comprises Dapper Music and Entertainment, Dvpper Digital, S94 Publishing, Bangers Only Productions and Dapper Live.

World.title: British Airways flight turns back to Heathrow: Here’s what happened
World.content:
British Airways flight BA295 was travelling from Heathrow to Chicago on Monday 5 October when the aircraft repotedly descended from approximately 36 000 feet to around 9 000 feet over Ireland.

BRITISH AIRWAYS FLIGHT TURNS BACK TO HEATHROW

British Airways crew returned the aircraft toward London Heathrow. The flight reportedly spent several hours in the area to burn fuel before safely landing back at Heathrow. All passengers and crew were able to disembark normally following the landing. British Airways said it was making arrangements to assist affected passengers with their onward travel.

So, what caused this? The technical problem that prompted the rapid descent has not yet been publicly established. Aviation authorities and the airline are expected to investigate the aircraft.



WHEN DO RAPID DESCENTS OCCUR?

Rapid descents can be carried out when an aircraft needs to reach a lower altitude quickly. This includes when in response to a potential pressurisation problem. However, the descent itself does not establish the cause of the incident, and no definitive explanation has yet been released.

Despite the disruption, the aircraft returned safely to Heathrow Airport in London. There were no immediate reports of serious injuries among passengers or crew.

The incident comes as British Airways continues a broader programme of fleet and customer-experience investment. This includes planned cabin refurbishments and changes to its international flying schedule.



A passenger aboard Flydubai flight described how two relief pilots stepped in during a violent cockpit incident, helping bring the aircraft safely down in Saudi Arabia.

World.title: KwaZulu-Natal loses the most SASSA beneficiaries in 3 months
World.content:
SASSA drops over 200 000 beneficiaries in 3 months. Image: Pexels

The South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) has been cracking down on social grant beneficiaries.

In three months, the agency dropped 241 046 grant beneficiaries, despite having a record number of applications.

KwaZulu-Natal had the highest reduction in beneficiaries.



KZN Loses the Most Beneficiaries

KwaZulu-Natal lost 56 263 grant beneficiaries between April and June.

At the end of March 2026, the province had 4 217 843 beneficiaries. By the end of June, 4 161 481 beneficiaries remained.

That’s a 1.27% drop.

The report doesn’t reveal how the agency achieved the decline.

In KwaZulu-Natal, the province received 81 543 grant applications in the three months ending June.

Of those, the agency only refused 9 834.



The remaining 71 674 were approved.

Despite these applications and approvals, KwaZulu-Natal still contributed 23.3% to the decline in beneficiaries.

The report does show that 86 238 grants lapsed.

Temporary disability grants typically lapse every 6 months to 1 year.

In KwaZulu-Natal, SASSA refused 8 272 disability grant applications between April and June.

This contributed most to the declines.

But grants can also lapse if a beneficiary hasn’t withdrawn the grant money for 3 consecutive months.

According to the data, most lapsed grants impacted children.

Only 6 439 disability grants and a further 4 964 Old Age Grants lapsed.

However, 11 047 grants lapsed for children under 2.

Other Provinces Impacted

It’s not only KwaZulu-Natal that has been dropping grant beneficiaries.

Every province had a drop in grant recipients.

Gauteng lost the second most beneficiaries. In the second quarter, the province lost 39 673 beneficiaries.

The Western Cape was next, losing 35 150 grant recipients.

The Northern Cape lost the fewest grant beneficiaries.

Province Decline in Grant Beneficiaries (April – June 2026) KwaZulu-Natal -56 362 Gauteng -39 673 Western Cape -35 150 Eastern Cape -31 878 Limpopo -23 280 Mpumalanga -16 222 Free State -16 068 North West -14 759 Northern Cape -7 654

Who is Losing their Grant?

The agency revealed that most of the decline in grants comes from Child Support Grants.

The grant saw a decline of 277 546 beneficiaries in three months.

Disability grants were next affected. 4 716 beneficiaries no longer get a disability grant.

The War Veteran Grant declined by 1 beneficiary.

Every other grant, including the grant-in-aid, old age and foster care grants, increased.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs take Red Arrows to Durban for CAF Confed Cup
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have decided to take their CAF Confederation Cup match against Red Arrows to Durban’s Moses Mabhida Stadium.

Amakhosi are scheduled to face the Zambian outfit over two legs in the second preliminary round of the competition.

The winner of this tie will advance to the group stage, and Chiefs are aiming to advance for the second season in a row.



The Glamour Boys had received a bye for the first preliminary round after being seeded while Red Arrows defeat Madagascar’s FC Rouge.

Red Arrows twice beat FC 2-0 to set up a date with Chiefs after advancing on a 4-0 aggregate win over FC Rouge.

Now, the first of the two legs will be played at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium in Zambia on Saturday, 17 October.

Kick-off is at 15:00 SA time.

The return leg is scheduled for Friday, 23 October at Moses Mabhida Stadium which will host the MTN8 final between Orlando Pirates and Mamelodi Sundowns.

Amakhosi hardly ever play their CAF Confederation Cup matches at FNB Stadium, and this was evident even last season when they used the venue just once.



And that was against Kabuscorp on 27 September in the preliminary rounds of the same competition.

World.title: Bafana Bafana: Who could return against Kenya in November?
World.content:
Pitso Mosimane is expected to have Mbekezeli Mbokazi back against Kenya in November 2026. Image: Wikimedia Commons, Chicago Fire website.

Pitso Mosimane may have more firepower when Bafana Bafana reunites in November.

In his first games back in charge, injuries heavily impacted selections and rotations.

Mbekezeli Mbokazi, Evidence Makgopa, and Lyle Foster were among those who missed out.



Here’s who could rejoin the team when the 2027 AFCON qualifiers resume next month.

When is the next 2027 AFCON qualifier?

South Africa are set for two crucial games against the Harambee Stars next month.

Bafana Bafana host Kenya first on 13 November, before the return leg on 17 November.

The SAFA website states that kickoff times and venues for both fixtures are not yet confirmed.

Kenya have already qualified for the main 2027 AFCON as co-hosts, leaving just 1 spot in the group to fight over.

Bafana Bafana are leading the standings with 6 points, ahead of Guinea in second.



While the Harambee Stars have their place already confirmed, they could still trip up the others in the group.

After the November matches, the qualifiers take a long break until the final games in March 2027.

Who could return for Bafana Bafana vs Kenya?

Mbekezeli Mbokazi made a triumphant comeback from a thigh injury on 26 September.

The centre-back played 80 minutes in Chicago Fire’s win over Charlotte FC, including a crucial goal-line clearance.

Meanwhile, Teboho Mokoena was substituted off injured in the 2-1 win against Guinea.

The midfielder was subsequently left out of the 5-0 thrashing of Eritrea and the 1-0 friendly victory over Egypt.

However, a KickOff report suggests he will be fit for Mamelodi Sundowns’ MTN8 final clash against Orlando Pirates this weekend.

Left-back Aubrey Modiba was also missing for the Egypt game in Cairo, but is expected to return to action as early as this weekend.

Mosimane has already stated that he wants to see these players back in the mix for the 2027 AFCON qualifiers in November.

Speaking to the media after the 1-0 win over Egypt, according to FARpost, he said:

“I hope those injured will come back. I saw Mbokazi playing; Teboho [Mokoena] is not bad. He will also come back to play.”

Midfielder Thalente Mbatha and forward Evidence Makgopa are also working towards full fitness.

Per Africa Soccer, Orlando Pirates coach Abdeslam Ouaddou said both players have returned to full-team training.

Players who could be out long-term

Midfielder Bathusi Aubaas missed the Egypt game after injuring his leg against Eritrea.

Sundowns have kept mum about the extent of his injury, but reports indicate he could be out for a long spell.

Similarly, Khuliso Mudau is out until early next year after rupturing his Achilles tendon in August.

One of the surprise omissions from Mosimane’s first Bafana Bafana squad was Houston Dynamo forward Lyle Foster.

He recently debuted for the MLS franchise, and the belief is that he could miss out for South Africa going forward.

Likewise, Pirates’ Sihle Nduli will undergo a two-week rehabilitation before he even rejoins full-team training.
