World.title: Gayton on Andre Esterhuizen K-word scandal: ‘He is not a racist’
World.content:
Gayton McKenzie has defended Andre Esterhuizen over allegations of a racial slur. Like the Minister of Sport, Arts and Culture, the Springbok has been accused of using the K-word in the past.

The incident took place in 2012 when the rugby player was just 18 years old.

GAYTON MCKENZIE CALLS ON SA RUGBY FOR ANSWERS FOR ANDRE ESTERHUIZEN INCIDENT

In a clip posted on his Facebook account, Gayton McKenzie addressed the media about the social media storm surrounding Andre Esterhuizen’s old K-word scandal.



Last month, SA Rugby, or SARU, refused to respond to questions about the racial slur during a press conference with Esterhuizen, who led the Springboks as captain in their test match against the Wallabies.

As a result, the Minister of Sport revealed that he would be meeting the organisation this week, which would provide him with a full report.

He said, “SARU must understand that people are hurt; they have not explained the issue. They have failed in explaining the rationale behind it.”

‘I DON’T BELIEVE HE IS RACIST’

In the clip, Gayton McKenzie also defended Andre Esterhuizen, urging the public not to write him off.

He said: “I am a product of second chances. People change, people make mistakes. I’m a living example.

“I hope that Andre Esterhuizen has apologised to the victim. I hope that he has seen the error of his ways. I’ve done worse things than Andre Esterhuizen and I’ve been forgiven”.



He continued: “Andre was a young boy, and he has changed. I don’t believe people should be punished for the rest of their lives. He has made a mistake.

“We can use him to show the public that racism is not the way. I don’t believe he is a racist. I’ve spoken to one or two guys who work with him, and they have good things to say about him”.

WHEN DID GAYTON, ANDRE ESTERHUIZEN SAY THE K-WORD?

In 2012, Adriaan Andre Esterhuizen, a Matric learner at Klerksdorp High School, was accused of calling Thabo Molete, the coach of the Potchefstroom Gymnasium, a “f**king k*****” during a rugby match spat.

The then 18-year-old was found guilty of misconduct and was handed a year’s ban, which later became a six-month suspension, provided he underwent a life skills course.

As a result, he missed participation in Craven Week.

Last year, screenshots of Gayton McKenzie’s old X [formerly Twitter] posts caused widespread backlash.

The Minister of Sport, Arts and Culture, who is also the Patriotic Alliance leader, has defended some of the tweets and apologised for a few he claims were “insensitive and stupid”.

However, he claimed that several – which contained the K-word, were “AI-generated”.

He said in a Facebook Live at the time: “I never thought people would accuse me of racism.

“In my entire life, I’ve never called anybody the K-word. We are the victims. This is a political campaign driven by the EFF, together with some influencers on X. Let them show me where I used the K-word referring to someone. They can’t.

A few days later, parliament spokesperson Moloto Mothapo stated that an ethics committee could not probe Gayton’s old tweets from 2013 – 2017 as he was not an MP at the time. However, the South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC) pledged to open an investigation against the minister.

World.title: 28-year-old man drowns in Richards Bay
World.content:
A 28-year-old man has died after drowning in Richards Bay on Sunday (4 October).

MAN DROWNS IN RICHARDS BAY

Manie le Roux, NSRI Richards Bay deputy station commander, said that a 28-year-old man drowned in Richards Bay at 06:45 on Sunday 4 October. NSRI Richards Bay duty crew were activated following reports of a drowning in progress at the Bay Hall area, in front of Zululand Multi Sports Club.

“NSRI rescue swimmers, our NSRI rescue vehicle, the SA Police Service, Police Search and Rescue – WPDS (Water Policing and Diving Service), uMhlathuze Fire and Rescue Service and Medcare 24 EMS ambulance service responded,” read a statement.



“On arrival on the scene NSRI and emergency services commenced CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation) efforts on a 28 year old local man who had been recovered from the water, we believe by bystander Good Samaritans, following a drowning accident,” read a statement.

MAN DECLARED DECEASED BY PARAMEDICS

uMhlathuze lifeguards, who reported for duty on the day, assisted on the scene. Despite extensive CPR efforts, after all efforts to resuscitate the man were exhausted. The man was sadly declared deceased by paramedics.

The body of the man has been taken into the care of Police and Government Health Forensic Pathology Services. Police have opened an Inquest docket.

This comes as a teen boy was also reported missing after he was caught in a rip current at Cape Vidal beach on Saturday (3 October) afternoon.

World.title: US visa social media checks just expanded again. Here’s who in Mzansi it affects
World.content:
More US visa applicants must now make their social media profiles public. Image: Pexels, for illustrative purposes. Image: Pexels

US visa social media checks have expanded again, and some South Africans need to pay attention.

From 1 October, more visa applicants must make every social media profile public.

That means consular officers can scroll through your posts before deciding on your visa.



So who in Mzansi is affected?

The newest change affects journalists and media workers most directly.

Students, exchange visitors and skilled workers on certain visas were already covered.

Tourists still have to list their social media accounts, but this latest change doesn’t require them to make those profiles public.

WHAT CHANGED ON 1 OCTOBER

The US Department of State announced the change on 18 September 2026.

The screening now covers three more visa categories: I, TN and TD.



I visas are for foreign media representatives, including journalists.

TN and TD visas are for Canadian and Mexican professionals and their dependents, so they don’t apply to South Africans.

Applicants in these categories must change the privacy settings on all their social media profiles to “public” or “open.”

The department was blunt about it.

A US visa, it said, remains “a privilege granted at the government’s discretion, not an entitlement.”

WHO IS ALREADY BEING SCREENED

This isn’t the first expansion.

According to immigration law firm DiRaimondo & Schroeder, applicants for F, M and J visas have been covered since June 2025.

These visas are for students and exchange visitors.

The J visa covers exchange programmes such as au pair and work-and-travel programmes.

Skilled workers on H-1B visas, and their H-4 dependents, were added in December 2025.

On 30 March 2026, the screening was extended again to fiancé visas and several other categories, including K, R, T, U, Q and H-3 visas.

The department says it uses every available source of information to identify applicants who may pose a threat to national security or public safety.

WHAT THE US VISA SOCIAL MEDIA RULES MEAN FOR TOURISTS

If you’re applying for a holiday visa, you’re not off the hook entirely.

Since 2019, almost all US visa applicants have had to list the social media platforms they’ve used in the past five years on the DS-160 visa application form.

Anyone who lies about their social media use could face serious immigration consequences.

The good news? State Department guidance says consular officers won’t ask for your passwords.

HOW TO PREPARE

Experts advise applicants to assume their online presence will be reviewed and compared with their application.

Inconsistent employment history, or posts that conflict with what you’ve told the embassy, could lead to extra questioning or delays.

The extra screening may also slow things down.

The department hasn’t announced new processing times, but delays are possible in individual cases.

So check that your LinkedIn job history matches your application, and leave extra time before you travel.

I’ll admit, the idea of a stranger scrolling through my Instagram before approving a trip feels a bit strange.

But for South Africans heading to the US to study, work or report, this is now part of the process.

My advice? Treat your social media like part of your CV. Because, as far as the US is concerned, it is.

World.title: World Migratory Bird Day: the West Coast’s smallest record-breaker is back
World.content:
A map tracking WEMBERE's journey from Velddrif to the Arctic and back. Image: BirdLife South Africa.

World Migratory Bird Day takes place on Saturday, 10 October.

And this year, one tiny traveller has given South Africans a very good reason to look up.

He weighs about 60 grams.



In less than seven months, he has flown further than halfway around the world.

Now he’s home on our West Coast, resting before he does it all again.

His name is Wembere, and he’s a Curlew Sandpiper.

He’s also living proof of why this year’s World Migratory Bird Day matters.

The 2026 theme is “Every Bird Counts – Your Observations Matter!”

It celebrates the role ordinary people play in protecting migratory birds.



WHAT IS WORLD MIGRATORY BIRD DAY?

World Migratory Bird Day is marked on the second Saturday in May and the second Saturday in October.

The two dates reflect the fact that birds migrate at different times in the northern and southern hemispheres.

This year’s theme highlights community science, also known as citizen science.

It also coincides with the 60th anniversary of the International Waterbird Census, a global effort to monitor migratory waterbirds.

THE 60-GRAM BIRD THAT FLEW 25,000KM

According to BirdLife South Africa, Wembere has travelled more than 25,000km in under seven months.

He was fitted with a satellite tracker at Velddrif in February 2026.

Velddrif is a small fishing town on the West Coast, about two hours’ drive north of Cape Town.

Wembere left South Africa on 27 February and flew to his breeding grounds in the Arctic tundra.

Now he’s back in Velddrif, where he will spend the next few months resting and refuelling before heading north again.

BirdLife South Africa flyway and migrants project manager Jessica Wilmot said she was “in awe of the lines on the map.”

WHY MIGRATORY BIRDS IN SOUTH AFRICA NEED PROTECTION

Wembere‘s journey comes with a warning.

According to BirdLife International’s State of the World’s Birds report, 45% of migratory bird species are now in decline.

One in nine is threatened with extinction.

Illegal hunting is part of the problem.

BirdLife International and EuroNatur’s Killing 3.0 report estimates that between 11 million and 36 million birds are illegally killed or taken in the Mediterranean region every year.

That’s why BirdLife South Africa recently signed the Nairobi Flyways Declaration, a global commitment to protect migratory birds across their entire journey.

As Wilmot put it, birds don’t recognise national borders, and conservation efforts can’t either.

HOW TO MARK WORLD MIGRATORY BIRD DAY

This year’s flagship species include the Abdim’s Stork, a bird that follows the rain across Africa.

South Africans can get involved by recording their own bird sightings.

Every observation adds to the data scientists use to protect birds like WEMBERE.

Groups planning a bird walk or count can also register their event on the official World Migratory Bird Day world map of events.

Registration is also now open for Birding Big Day 2026, BirdLife South Africa’s annual birding challenge.

I think there’s something humbling about a bird lighter than a cellphone flying to the Arctic and back.

It’s easy to forget these journeys happen right above our heads.

This Saturday, it might be worth stepping outside and looking up.

World.title: Khan's legal team breaks silence after Padayachee's murder
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Hours before his death, Preggy Padayachee warned disgraced former Deputy Head of Crime Intelligence Feroz Khan that his upcoming Madlanga Commission testimony would "ruffle some feathers."

Padayachee was shot and killed in Ekurhuleni on Monday night, while one passenger remains hospitalised in serious condition and a third walked away unharmed.

Now, following Padayachee's fatal shooting, Khan’s legal team has broken their silence.

READ | Feroz Khan's relative shot dead in Boksburg

Speaking exclusively to eNCA, Muhammed Vally expressed grave concerns over their client's safety.

According to Vally, Padayachee was a close relative of Khan.

“We now see that there's a family member that has been shot. So, the concern, I think, is a legitimate concern and it's an ongoing concern,”

Vally said they had engaged with the Madlanga Commission and would work with it to address their concerns.

Khan was meant to testify before the Madlanga Commission on Tuesday, with proceedings expected to be conducted remotely.

However, his testimony was postponed following the death of his uncle-in-law.

READ | UPDATE: Feroz Khan in-camera testimony postponed

Vally added that Khan was not in the right condition to proceed with the testimony in the aftermath of the shooting.

“I believe that they accepted that there were sufficient grounds to permit the postponement. They will obviously keep the public posted, as they have this morning through their public release, and we can take a lead from them in due course.

Adding to Vally, Kylen Ghirao said this is a difficult time but are hoping for investigations to ‘unmask the perpetrators’

World.title: South Africa, India, Qatar among nations who want to host 2036 Olympics
World.content:
PARIS - India, Qatar and South Africa were confirmed on Tuesday among the seven countries interested in hosting the 2036 Summer Olympics.

Germany, Hungary, Turkey and South Korea make up the rest of the current list issued by the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

Other countries have until October 31 to declare an interest.

In March 2027, the IOC Executive Board will draw up a shortlist of the interested parties, who will then enter dialogue with the Olympic body.

The IOC said that the 2036 hosts would be assessed on factors such as funding, and political and public support.

"Wherever the Games take place, one thing must never change: athletes have to be at the heart of everything we do," IOC President Kirsty Coventry said in a statement.

"That is why, for every future host, delivering the best possible experience for the athletes must always be the starting point," the Zimbabwean former swimmer added.

India has stated its intention to host an Olympics for the first time, centred on Ahmedabad, the key city in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's home state of Gujarat.

Ahmedabad will host the 2030 multi-sport Commonwealth Games, seen as a major rehearsal for an Olympics. The city is also home to the world's largest cricket stadium.

South Africa hosted the 2010 football World Cup and the 1995 Rugby World Cup but has never played host to an Olympics.

Qatar hosted the 2022 football World Cup, although the awarding of that tournament was later mired in allegations of corruption within football's world governing body FIFA.

An Olympics in the Gulf would have to be moved to later than its traditional July-August slot due to the heat.

The German National Olympic Committee voted last month to select Munich as its candidate city for a Games that will take place a century after the infamous 1936 Berlin Olympics which were overseen by the Nazi regime.

The Turkish Olympic authorities hope to go one better than in the bidding for the 2020 Summer Olympics when Istanbul came second to Tokyo.

The 2028 Summer Olympics will take place in Los Angeles, while Brisbane has been awarded the 2032 edition.

World.title: 'They are failing us': Multimillion rand wall project leaves workers unpaid
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Workers employed on a multi-million-rand Prasa wall project have had enough.

The workers employed by Spec Africa Holdings claim their employer has failed to pay for their September wages and that they have had to fight for their money various times since 2024.

This wage delay has left many struggling to afford basic necessities, including paying for rent and food.

Six contractors that supply the project also remain unpaid, leaving workers without essential resources.

READ | Higher salaries offer little relief as inflation bites

The company was contracted to construct a protective barrier wall between Pretoria Station and Wolmerton.

The contract is valued at nearly R385 million.

In a letter dated 30 September, Spec Africa Holdings confirmed it could not pay salaries on time, blaming delayed client payments and a cash-flow shortfall.

But this has added to workers' frustrations.

Spec Africa’s management staff and vehicles have been removed from the sites, and its Midrand office was closed.

In a written response to eNCA, the company blames delayed client payments but says confidentiality prevents it from disclosing details.

It said it's looking for money to settle outstanding wages, denies recurring salary delays and maintains it has kept workers informed.

World.title: Accused 3 in AKA and Tibz murder trial granted separate trial
World.content:
DURBAN - The judge in the Kiernan “AKA” Forbes and his friend Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane trial has granted accused number three, Siyanda Myeza, a separate trial.

Seven suspects accused of murdering AKA Forbes and Motsoane returned to the High Court in Durban on Tuesday.

READ | AKA, Tibz trial resumes with defence seeking separation

The pair were shot dead outside a restaurant on Florida Road in Durban in 2023.

The seven accused face charges of murder, attempted murder, and the unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition.

All seven have pleaded not guilty.

World.title: ANC yet to announce mayoral candidates
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC has once again failed to announce its mayoral candidates for the country's major metros, strategic secondary cities, and towns.

The party initially committed to announcing its mayoral candidates in September, after failing to do so in August.

But that month has come and gone, and no announcement, or at least an indication of when it'll do so, has yet been made.

READ | ‘Andile Lungisa not entitled to public office’ - ANC

ANC secretary general Fikile Mbalula assured that they have done interviews and will be revealing people who have the potential to be mayoral candidates.

“The ANC campaign is not dependent on candidates. It is driven and dependent on the face of the campaign who is the President. The add on is the candidates, which is the decision that has been taken by the leadership and therefore in this particular instance we are following that. We are doing it in a systematic way.

But with weeks before the all-important local government elections, leadership expert Mazwe Majola warned that the ANC can not wait until the ‘eleventh hour’ only to say that it has been experiencing problems.

World.title: Mbeki, Zuma to testify before TRC cases inquiry
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Former presidents Thabo Mbeki and Jacob Zuma are set to testify before the TRC cases inquiry after all.



Mbeki will appear before Justice Sisi Khampepe on 19 and 20 October, while his successor Zuma will testify on 22 October.



The two ex-presidents tried unsuccessfully to get Justice Khampepe to recuse herself as chairperson of the judicial inquiry into possible political interference in post-TRC apartheid prosecutions.



Their legal battle to force Khampepe out hit the final brick wall before the Constitutional Court at the end of August.



Families and survivors of apartheid-era gross human rights violations - known as the Calata Group - want to know why apartheid-era crimes identified by the TRC have not been properly investigated and prosecuted.

World.title: Thabo Bester fires lawyers, to represent himself in prison escape trial
World.content:
BLOEMFONTEIN - Convicted rapist Thabo Bester has fired his legal representatives in his prison escape trial and will represent himself when the trial begins in April 2027.

He will challenge his treatment behind bars at the Free State High Court on 16 October.

Bester claims prison restrictions have limited his access to lawyers, legal resources and communication.

The prison escapee is charged alongside his partner, Nandipha Magudumana, and seven other co-accused.

He faces charges stemming from his escape from Mangaung Correctional Centre in May 2022. Magudumana and six others are accused of aiding his escape.

Meanwhile, Magudumana’s Constitutional Court challenge over her deportation remains pending.

Bester has previously said he struggles to consult with his legal team while in prison.

World.title: Govt warns against panic buying as record fuel prices take effect
World.content:
Economist Dawie Roodt says the impact will be felt across the economy, with transport and agriculture among the sectors likely to be affected first.

“Transport is an obvious one. Unfortunately, we make extensive use of diesel. We shouldn’t be using this much diesel. This freight should be in trains, for example.

“Agriculture is another industry that will be affected. And in the end, everybody will be affected.

“This is likely to put upward pressure on inflation.”

Roodt says the fuel shock comes at a difficult time for the economy, with interest rates still relatively high.

He says this could further weigh on economic growth and household finances.

“There will always be some sort of international crisis. What we need to do as South Africans is make sure that we are prepared when something like this happens.

“Because of our local domestic issues, the South African economy is just not in a position to absorb this.”
