What the New Plant Adds

Sal de Oro already produces. Its first phase is a lithium hydroxide plant in the industrial park at General Güemes, in the Salta lowlands. It opened in October 2024 with a design capacity of 25,000 tonnes a year. The company says it now runs at about 85 percent of that.

Plant II sits up on the salt flat itself and makes lithium carbonate, a different battery-grade product. Together the two plants come to about 48,000 tonnes a year, El Tribuno calculated from company figures. Production at the new site is due to rise gradually through 2027, the company said at Tuesday’s briefing, so real volumes will lag the headline capacity for some time.

At a press briefing in Salta on Monday 28 September, POSCO Argentina said its exports in September came to 8,526 tonnes worth US$138 million. It also reported more than 600 direct employees and more than 270 local suppliers. These are company figures and have not been independently audited.

Sal de Oro capacity in tonnes a year: the Phase 1 hydroxide plant, the new Plant II carbonate plant, both combined, and the 100,000-tonne expansion target. (Chart: The Rio Times; data: POSCO Argentina via El Tribuno, Resolution 1157/2026, C5N)

The Money Behind It

The legal backbone is Resolution 1157/2026 of the Economy Ministry. It was signed on Wednesday 29 July and published in the Official Gazette on Friday 31 July. It admits “Sal de Oro II” to the RIGI, the incentive regime for large investments.

The RIGI is President Milei’s flagship tool for foreign capital. It offers projects long-term tax, customs and currency stability in return for minimum investment commitments.

In the resolution, POSCO declared US$207.9 million in qualifying assets. It committed US$98 million within the first two years, and must meet the minimum investment by Tuesday 31 July 2029. The ministry dates the project’s entry into the regime to Friday 12 June 2026.

Local press, citing company figures, gives larger totals. El Tribuno reports about US$633 million in total spending on this phase and more than US$2 billion across the whole project. The resolution counts only qualifying assets, and the gap has not been explained publicly.

When the approval was announced in June, Economy Minister Luis Caputo estimated the new plant could generate more than US$300 million a year in exports. POSCO Argentina also says it expects up to US$700 million in financing from the Inter-American Development Bank for working capital at both plants.

What It Means for You

For investors, the POSCO lithium plant is one more sign that Argentina’s lithium pipeline is moving from promises to plants. The same salt flat hosts projects by Rio Tinto and Australia’s Galan Lithium. Rio Tinto’s plans nearby were covered in Rio Tinto Plans US$2.7 Billion Lithium Project in Salta.

For carmakers and battery buyers in the United States, more carbonate from South America widens the choice of suppliers outside China. The volumes are still modest against global demand, and they depend on prices that have swung hard in recent years.

For Argentina, each new plant adds export income. Earlier figures are in Argentina Mining Exports Top US$6 Billion in Eight Months as Lithium Jumps 190%. The risk is concentration: a handful of foreign operators now carry much of that growth.

What Is Not Known

The programme included the signing of a memorandum of understanding with the national government on Stages III and IV, aiming for 100,000 tonnes of lithium a year, C5N reported. No post-event report has yet confirmed that it was signed. POSCO said only that it plans further expansion stages and has given no timeline, phases or investment figure.

The buyers of the new carbonate have not been named. Nor is it clear how fast the new POSCO lithium plant will ramp up in 2027, or what lithium prices will be when full volumes arrive.

The text of the memorandum, the speeches and any new investment pledges made at the ceremony have not been published.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the POSCO lithium plant in Argentina?

It is Plant II of the Sal de Oro project on the Salar del Hombre Muerto, between Salta and Catamarca provinces. It is designed to produce about 23,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate a year for export.

How much is POSCO investing?

Economy Ministry Resolution 1157/2026 lists US$207.9 million in qualifying assets for this phase, with US$98 million due in the first two years. Company figures cited by local press are higher.

When will the plant reach full output?

Not right away. Production is due to rise gradually during 2027. A separate plan to lift Sal de Oro to 100,000 tonnes a year, the subject of a memorandum on the inauguration programme, has no published timeline.

Sources: Argentine Economy Ministry, Resolution 1157/2026, Official Gazette, 31 July 2026 and Infoleg summary; El Tribuno, 5 October 2026 and 28 September 2026; C5N, 5 October 2026; El Esquiu, 6 October 2026; BAE Negocios, 6 October 2026.

World.content:

SOUTH AFRICA · GOLF

Key Facts — When it happens Rounds run Thursday 3 to Sunday 6 December 2026, after two Pro-Am days. The shop lists 7am starts, the organiser a noon tee-off.

— Where to go The Nedbank Golf Challenge is played at Gary Player Country Club in Sun City, within a two-hour drive of Johannesburg.

— Who is playing American Bryson DeChambeau makes his debut. Justin Rose and defending champion Kristoffer Reitan are among seven confirmed players.

— What it costs Day tickets cost R450 (US$27) on Thursday and Friday and R500 (US$30) at the weekend, on the official Ticketpro shop.

— What it means for you Americans need no visa for stays under 90 days, but passports need two blank pages and 30 days’ validity after departure.

— Still open The rest of the 66-player field, the pairings and the official tee times for each round have not been published yet.

The Nedbank Golf Challenge tees off at Sun City, a South African resort, from Thursday 3 to Sunday 6 December 2026. Two-time US Open champion Bryson DeChambeau makes his debut at the event billed as “Africa’s Major”.

Round tickets cost R450 (US$27) to R500 (US$30), and up to two children under 18 get in free with each adult. The players compete for US$6 million in prize money on a course with a brand-new first hole.

What the Event Is and Why It Matters

The Nedbank Golf Challenge is a four-day professional golf tournament held in honour of Gary Player, the South African golfing great. The 2026 edition is the 44th, and the Gary Player Country Club has hosted it since 1981.

It is a stop on the DP World Tour, a men’s professional circuit, early in its season-long Race to Dubai ranking. The organisers describe an exclusive field playing for US$6 million in total prize money.

The event has a long American thread. Johnny Miller won the first edition in 1981, and Ray Floyd followed in 1982.

Corey Pavin won in 1995, Jim Furyk in 2005 and 2006, Max Homa in 2023 and Johannes Veerman in 2024. That makes six American champions with seven wins at Sun City.

For a US visitor, the Nedbank Golf Challenge offers world-class golf at a modest price. The resort around it has a water park, casinos and a national park next door.

The 2026 Field and the New Course

Bryson DeChambeau, who won the US Open in 2020 and 2024, plays the Nedbank Golf Challenge for the first time. He said he has won Jack Nicklaus’s Memorial and Arnold Palmer’s Invitational, and now wants to win Gary Player’s tournament.

DeChambeau already knows South African crowds. He won the first LIV Golf event in South Africa, at Steyn City in Johannesburg, in March, Business Day reported.

England’s Justin Rose, ranked 12th in the world when he was announced on Tuesday 18 August, was runner-up here in 2007. Norway’s Kristoffer Reitan returns to defend the title he won by one shot last year.

The confirmed list also includes England’s Marco Penge and the South Africans Casey Jarvis, Christiaan Bezuidenhout and Hennie Du Plessis. Up to 10 places can go to players from the top 70 of the FedExCup, the US PGA Tour’s season ranking.

The full field will have 66 players, and there is no cut, so everyone who starts plays all four rounds. Entries close on Thursday 19 November 2026.

The course has had the biggest changes in its history, the organisers say, including a new 470-metre (514-yard) par-four first hole. The old first hole has become the course’s first practice range.

There is also a new spectator viewing area between the seventh and 12th greens. Sun International, the hotel group behind Sun City, put R50 million (US$3 million) into the work, its chief executive told Business Day.

Tickets, Prices and What Is Included

Nedbank Golf Challenge tickets are sold on the official shop at tickets.nedbankgolfchallenge.com, run by the ticketing company Ticketpro. Prices are per adult, as listed on Tuesday 6 October 2026.

The Pro-Am days on Tuesday 1 and Wednesday 2 December, when professionals play with amateur partners, cost R250 (US$15). Round 1 on Thursday 3 December and Round 2 on Friday 4 December cost R450 (US$27).

Round 3 on Saturday 5 December and the final round on Sunday 6 December cost R500 (US$30). Up to two children under 18 get in free with each adult ticket.

A ticket covers entry to Sun City and the course, free parking, grandstand seats, the practice range and free WiFi. On other days, an adult day visitor pass to Sun City and its Valley of Waves water park costs from R395 (US$24).

Places in the Hospitali-TEE Lounge cost from R8,250 (US$496) on Thursday and Friday and R8,950 (US$538) at the weekend. Conversions use 16.65 rand to the US dollar on Tuesday 6 October 2026.

Outside food and drink, cooler boxes, weapons and video cameras are banned, and so are cameras on tournament days. Phones are welcome on silent, and photos are fine with the flash off.

Getting to Sun City and the Course

Sun City opened in 1979 and sits on the edge of Pilanesberg National Park in North West province. The resort describes itself as within a two-hour drive of Johannesburg.

During the Nedbank Golf Challenge, spectators park at the main gate and take the Sky Train to the Welcome Walkway. Wheelchair users are advised to keep to the hard-surfaced roads on the course.

The US State Department advises against driving outside metropolitan areas at night, citing animals, broken-down vehicles and crime. Plan the drive from Johannesburg in daylight, or stay at the resort for the week.

Staying put has another benefit. Game drives into neighbouring Pilanesberg National Park offer a chance to spot the Big Five: lion, leopard, elephant, rhino and buffalo.

Three Evening Concerts at the Resort

The Nedbank Golf Challenge also runs a concert each evening from Friday to Sunday, with separate tickets on the same official shop. A general access concert ticket includes entry to the resort.

On Friday 4 December, Scorpion Kings headline a beach party at the Valley of Waves from 4:30pm to midnight. Tickets start at R1,000 (US$60).

Scorpion Kings are Kabza De Small and DJ Maphorisa, two stars of amapiano, a South African style of house music.

On Saturday 5 December, a concert billed as +LIVE+ runs at the Superbowl, the resort’s concert venue, from 4:30pm to 10pm. Tickets cost R1,195 (US$72) to R5,000 (US$300).

The American rock band Live uses the same billing for its Cape Town and Pretoria shows the following week.

On Sunday 6 December, the house DJ Shimza closes the week at the resort’s Sun Park from 4:30pm to 2am. General access costs R1,000 (US$60) and a VVIP package place R3,750 (US$225) per person.

Tips for US and Foreign Visitors

Americans do not need a visa for stays of less than 90 days. Your passport must be valid for 30 days after you leave and have two consecutive blank visa pages.

A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you arrive from a country with yellow fever risk. Families should read the State Department’s page first, because South Africa has special requirements for minors.

The State Department rates South Africa at Level 2, “Exercise increased caution”, in an advisory dated Tuesday 27 May 2025. It warns of violent crime and smash-and-grab attacks on cars, so keep bags out of sight while driving.

December is summer, and the organisers recommend cool clothes, sensible shoes, a hat and sunscreen. If the lightning siren sounds, put down your umbrella and take shelter at once.

Sun City is seven hours ahead of New York in December. That puts 7am at the course at midnight on the US East Coast, and noon at 5am.

If you are staying on, J. Cole plays Johannesburg on Saturday 12 December. That makes a golf week and a stadium show an easy pairing.

What Is Not Confirmed Yet

Only seven of the 66 players are confirmed so far, and the organisers have said more big names will follow. The pairings and the official tee times for each round have not been published.

The ticket shop lists each tournament day from 7am, while the organiser’s ticket page shows a noon tee-off. The official event app carries the latest tournament information, so check it before setting off.

Stage times and support acts for the three evening concerts have not been announced either. The organisers have not said whether Saturday’s +LIVE+ show belongs to the same tour as Live’s December dates.

The dates, the course, the ticket prices and the official seller for the Nedbank Golf Challenge are confirmed. That is enough to book a December trip to Sun City now.

Frequently Asked Questions

When and where is the Nedbank Golf Challenge 2026?

The Nedbank Golf Challenge runs from Thursday 3 to Sunday 6 December 2026 at Gary Player Country Club in Sun City. Pro-Am days are on Tuesday 1 and Wednesday 2 December.

How much do Nedbank Golf Challenge tickets cost?

Adult day tickets cost R450 (US$27) on Thursday and Friday and R500 (US$30) on Saturday and Sunday. Pro-Am days cost R250 (US$15), and up to two children under 18 enter free with each adult.

Do Americans need a visa to visit South Africa?

No visa is needed for stays of less than 90 days. Your passport must be valid for 30 days after you leave and have two consecutive blank visa pages.

World.title: Débora do Batom Gets Semi-Open Regime, Stays at Home
World.content:
Society: Brazil

Key Facts —Who. Débora Rodrigues dos Santos, a hairdresser known in Brazil as “Débora do Batom” (Débora of the Lipstick), and Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes. —What. Moraes moved her from the closed to the semi-open sentence regime and credited 212 days off her 14-year sentence, but kept her under house arrest. —Where. Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court (STF) in Brasília; she serves her sentence at home in Paulínia, in São Paulo state. —When. The decision was signed on 2 October and made public on Tuesday, 6 October 2026. She was convicted on 25 April 2025. —As of 6 October 2026, 14:45 GMT.

Débora do Batom, the woman who wrote “Perdeu, mané” in lipstick on a statue outside Brazil’s Supreme Court during the 8 January 2023 riots, has been moved to the semi-open regime. In practice little changes for now, because Justice Moraes kept her under house arrest, which he called the more favourable way to serve her sentence.

Her case is one of the best-known of the January 8 prosecutions, when supporters of former president Jair Bolsonaro stormed the seats of Brazil’s three branches of government in Brasília. US readers who follow Brazil’s politics and the legal fallout of that day will recognise the name.

What We Know

Moraes granted the change of regime after the federal prosecutor’s office (PGR) backed it, according to Migalhas and Gazeta do Povo. He also recognised 212 new days of sentence reduction for prison work, reading and study, on top of two days credited earlier.

Those days break down as 108 for work, 100 for passing the national school exam ENEM in 2023, and four for reading one book. Her defence had asked for 281 days. Moraes followed the prosecutors and refused extra credit for a second ENEM result in 2024.

Under Brazilian law, a prisoner can move up a regime after serving a share of the sentence. In her case that share was 25%, or three years and six months.

The decision says she had served three years, six months and 14 days of effective time. With remission counted, the total reached four years, one month and 16 days on 1 October, according to Gazeta do Povo.

Moraes found that the subjective requirement was also met, because there was no record of serious misconduct or of breaching her electronic monitoring since she went home.

The Supreme Federal Court in Brasília, with the “Justice” statue in front. (File photo)

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Case Behind the Name

On 8 January 2023, Débora wrote “Perdeu, mané”, roughly “you lost, pal”, in lipstick on the “A Justiça” statue in front of the Supreme Court.

On 25 April 2025, the court’s First Panel convicted her. The sentence was 14 years: 12 years and six months of reclusão (the harsher form of prison term) plus one year and six months of detenção, starting in the closed regime.

The charges included armed criminal association, attempted violent abolition of the democratic rule of law, coup d’état and damage to protected heritage. Gazeta do Povo reported that Moraes, Cármen Lúcia and Flávio Dino backed 14 years, Cristiano Zanin proposed 11 and Luiz Fux argued for one year and six months.

She has served her sentence under house arrest since March 2025, with an ankle monitor. Our earlier reporting covers how the court counts time toward January 8 sentences.

What Is Not Known

Brazilian outlets disagree on what the new regime changes at home. Agência Brasil reports that she may now leave the house during the day, while her defence says nothing changes immediately.

Her defence said any new permissions would be reviewed later and granted gradually with court approval. It also lamented the delay in recognising the progression.

The updated sentence calculation, with the final date she could reach the next regime or finish her term, has not been published. One outlet reported a cut to 10 years, but the other reports on the decision, and the arithmetic of the 25% threshold, use 14 years, so we use that figure.

What It Means for US Readers

The ruling shows that January 8 sentences are still being worked through one case at a time, even as Brazil heads to a presidential runoff on 25 October 2026. The length of those sentences remains a live argument inside Brazil.

For readers tracking the court and its justices, see also our coverage of the court freezing January 8 sentence reductions and the wider Brazil section.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Débora do Batom?

Débora Rodrigues dos Santos is a hairdresser convicted over the 8 January 2023 riots in Brasília. She wrote “Perdeu, mané” in lipstick on the Justice statue outside the Supreme Court.

What did Justice Moraes decide?

He moved her to the semi-open regime and recognised 212 days of sentence reduction. He kept her under house arrest, which he described as more favourable than the semi-open regime.

Is she going back to prison?

No. According to the reports, she stays at home under house arrest, where she has been since March 2025.

How long is her sentence?

The Supreme Court’s First Panel sentenced her on 25 April 2025 to 14 years. That is the figure Brazilian outlets cite in coverage of the new decision.

World.title: Riverdance 30 Plays Pretoria and Cape Town in April 2027
World.content:

SOUTH AFRICA · DANCE & MUSIC

Key Facts — When it happens Riverdance 30 plays Pretoria from Friday 9 to Sunday 11 April 2027, then Cape Town from Friday 16 to Sunday 18 April.

— Where to go Pretoria’s shows are at the Sunbet Arena in Time Square; Cape Town’s are at the Grand Arena in GrandWest.

— When the curtain rises Evening shows start at 8pm on Friday and 7:30pm on Saturday, with matinees at 2pm Saturday and 1:30pm Sunday.

— How to buy Ticketmaster South Africa is the only authorised seller, and tickets bought on Viagogo will not get you in.

— What it costs The venues list tickets from R715 (US$43) in Pretoria and from R745 (US$45) in Cape Town.

— What it means for you Americans need no visa for stays under 90 days, but need two consecutive blank visa pages.

— The catch Only starting prices are listed by the promoter and venues, Platinum seats move with demand, and tickets reach your account 30 days before.

Riverdance 30 – The New Generation, the anniversary production of the Irish dance show, plays eight times in South Africa in April 2027. For an American visitor, it is a family-friendly night out to fit around a trip to Pretoria or Cape Town.

Big Concerts, the South African promoter behind the dates, sells tickets only through Ticketmaster South Africa. The two venues list seats from R715 (US$43) in Pretoria and R745 (US$45) in Cape Town.

What Riverdance 30 Is and Why It Matters

Riverdance began in 1994 as a seven-minute dance number at the Eurovision Song Contest, a televised European music competition. It then grew into a full-length stage show of Irish dance and live music.

Bill Whelan’s music for the show won a Grammy Award in 1997. Big Concerts says Riverdance has been seen live by more than 31 million people around the world.

Riverdance 30 – The New Generation is the show’s 30th-anniversary production, with new choreography, costumes, lighting, projection and motion graphics. For the first time, every performer was born after the show began.

Moya Doherty, who commissioned the original 1994 piece, is still the producer, and John McColgan directs. Whelan is still credited as the composer.

Riverdance’s website also lists a 2027 US tour, with stops from New Haven, Connecticut, to Denver and Los Angeles. The South African run is shorter, with four performances in each city.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Pretoria Shows at the Sunbet Arena

Pretoria is South Africa’s administrative capital and lies in Gauteng, the province that is also home to Johannesburg. The Sunbet Arena sits inside Time Square, a casino, hotel and entertainment complex at Menlyn Maine.

The street address is 209 Aramist Avenue, Waterkloof Glen. Time Square opened in April 2017, and Sun International, which runs it, describes the arena as an 8,500-seat venue.

Riverdance 30 opens there on Friday 9 April at 8pm, with doors at 6:30pm. Saturday 10 April has a 2pm matinee, with doors at 12:30pm, and a 7:30pm show, with doors at 6pm.

The Pretoria run closes with a 1:30pm matinee on Sunday 11 April, with doors at noon. Each performance lasts about 1 hour and 40 minutes, plus a 20-minute interval.

The Sunbet Arena is a cashless venue, so bring a bank card. Weapons, cooler boxes and food are not allowed, and secured parking costs R20 (US$1.20).

The Gautrain, Gauteng’s rapid rail line, has stations at OR Tambo International Airport and in Pretoria, including Hatfield. Read more on the Gautrain and Gauteng’s transport plans.

From the station, an app-based taxi or a car booked through your hotel is the simplest way to reach Time Square.

The Cape Town Shows at GrandWest

GrandWest is a casino and entertainment complex at 1 Jakes Gerwel Drive in Goodwood, a short drive from Cape Town’s city centre. It opened in December 2000, and Riverdance 30 plays in its Grand Arena.

The Cape Town run starts on Friday 16 April at 8pm, with doors at 7pm. Saturday 17 April has a 2pm matinee, with doors at 1pm, and a 7:30pm show, with doors at 6:30pm.

The last South African performance is a 1:30pm matinee on Sunday 18 April, with doors at 12:30pm. GrandWest says parking on the complex costs R20 (US$1.20).

After an evening show, book your ride back from inside the venue rather than waiting at the roadside. A matinee is the simpler choice if you prefer to travel in daylight.

The same two arenas host the American R&B singer Kehlani in December; see the guide to Kehlani’s South African shows.

How Riverdance 30 Tickets Work

Big Concerts names Ticketmaster South Africa, at ticketmaster.co.za, as the official and only authorised ticketing partner for the tour. General sales opened on Friday 7 August 2026.

Tickets for Riverdance 30 start at R715 (US$43) in Pretoria and R745 (US$45) in Cape Town, according to the two venues. Conversions use 16.65 rand to the US dollar on Tuesday 6 October 2026.

Official Platinum tickets, sold as the best seats in the house, are priced by demand, much like airline seats. There are no VIP packages for this show.

Each customer can buy up to eight tickets per city. All tickets are digital and appear in your Ticketmaster account or app only 30 days before the show.

Bring photo ID that matches the name on your ticket. If you buy for a group, use the free Ticket Transfer tool to send each person a ticket once it goes live.

Tickets from Viagogo and other resale sites are not valid for entry. Both venues warn that holders of such tickets will be turned away without a refund.

Tips for US and Foreign Visitors

US citizens do not need a visa for stays of less than 90 days, according to the US State Department. Your passport must be valid for 30 days after you leave South Africa.

You also need two consecutive, completely blank visa pages on arrival. Travellers arriving from a yellow fever risk country must show a vaccination certificate.

South Africa has special entry requirements for minors, so families should check the Department of Home Affairs rules before flying. Children under three are not allowed into the venues.

Every minor needs a ticket, ear protection and a responsible adult. The weekend matinees of Riverdance 30 are the easiest fit for younger viewers.

The State Department rates South Africa at Level 2, “Exercise increased caution”, in an advisory issued on Tuesday 27 May 2025. It says violent crime is more common in big-city downtown areas, especially after dark.

It advises against walking alone after dark and suggests reputable dispatched taxis or hotel cabs. It also warns that card skimming at cash machines is common.

The advisory notes that some crime victims have been followed from OR Tambo airport to their home or hotel. Keep bags and phones out of sight when you land and on the drive in.

The Pretoria dates fall a week before the Cape Town dates. That leaves time to see both cities, or to choose the show that fits your route.

What Is Not Confirmed Yet

Neither the promoter nor the two venues have published a full price list, only starting prices. Platinum seat prices can rise with demand.

The lead dancers and musicians for the South African dates have not been named. Ticket delivery is also delayed, so buyers receive only an order confirmation at first.

If you are planning a trip around a particular seat type or price, check the Ticketmaster seat map before you book flights.

The dates, venues, showtimes and official seller for Riverdance 30 are confirmed. That is enough to start planning an April trip to South Africa.

Frequently Asked Questions

When and where does Riverdance 30 play in South Africa?

Riverdance 30 plays the Sunbet Arena at Time Square in Pretoria from Friday 9 to Sunday 11 April 2027. It then plays the Grand Arena at GrandWest in Cape Town from Friday 16 to Sunday 18 April.

How much do Riverdance tickets cost in South Africa?

The venues list tickets from R715 (US$43) in Pretoria and from R745 (US$45) in Cape Town. Ticketmaster South Africa is the only authorised seller.

Do Americans need a visa to see Riverdance in South Africa?

No visa is needed for stays of less than 90 days. Your passport must be valid for 30 days after you leave and have two consecutive blank visa pages.

World.content:

KENYA · LIVE MUSIC

Key Facts — When it happens Camp Mulla Funky Town runs from 6pm on Saturday 7 November 2026 until 4am on Sunday.

— Where to go The night takes place at Masshouse, a bar and events venue inside Ngong Racecourse in Nairobi.

— Who is behind it Camp Mulla, the first Kenyan act nominated for a US Black Entertainment Television (BET) Award, presents the night with Sirocco Ent.

— What it costs Early Bird tickets cost KES 2,500 (US$19) and VIP tickets KES 6,000 (US$46) on the Mookh platform.

— What it means for you US visitors need an approved Electronic Travel Authorisation before flying; a standard single entry costs US$30.

— The catch No line-up has been published, entry is strictly 18 and over, and tickets cannot be refunded.

Camp Mulla Funky Town takes over Masshouse, an events venue in Nairobi, on Saturday 7 November 2026. Camp Mulla, the hip-hop group behind it, was the first Kenyan act nominated for a US Black Entertainment Television (BET) Award.

Tickets are on sale from KES 2,500 (US$19) on Mookh, a Kenyan ticketing platform. The organisers promise “one major surprise” but have not yet published a line-up.

What Funky Town Is and Why It Matters

Funky Town is a one-night party at Masshouse, presented by Camp Mulla with the entertainment company Sirocco Ent. It runs from 6pm on Saturday 7 November until 4am on Sunday 8 November.

The ticket page calls it “a celebration of Nairobi’s golden era” and of “the sounds that shaped a generation”. It also promises “one unforgettable night, one major surprise”.

Funky Town is also the title of the group’s 2012 album. Its single “Hold It Down” was a tribute to Nairobi, the city that made them, Capital FM reported in April 2012.

For a US visitor, the Camp Mulla Funky Town night is a homegrown Nairobi party rather than a touring stadium show. The same venue hosts the American rock musician Jack White on Friday 18 December.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Kenya expat life Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Camp Mulla Are

Camp Mulla, a hip-hop and R&B group, came together in Nairobi around 2009, when its members were teenagers. Their 2012 line-up was Karun, Taio Tripper, Yung Kass (later Shappa Man) and the producer K’Cous.

Hits such as “Party Don’t Stop”, “Fresh All Day” and “Addicted” made them chart fixtures. Capital FM recalled in 2023 that they ruled the airwaves in the early 2010s.

In May 2012 the group became the first Kenyan act nominated for a BET Award, Capital FM reported at the time. The nomination came in the Best International Act: Africa category, alongside the Nigerian star Wizkid.

The line-up split at the height of its success, Capital FM wrote in 2023. In May 2013, The Standard reported that Karun was leaving for university in the United States, while Taio Tripper went solo.

A few years before 2023, an attempt at a reunion failed, the same Capital FM article noted. In October 2024, Karun brought out former bandmate Shappa Man at Nairobi’s Blankets & Wine festival for two Camp Mulla songs.

Karun has since joined the Recording Academy, the body behind the Grammy Awards, as a voting member. Capital FM reported the news in July 2025.

The Venue: Masshouse at Ngong Racecourse

Masshouse describes itself as a bar, restaurant and events venue. It sits inside Ngong Racecourse, on Ngong Road, west of Nairobi’s city centre.

The racecourse hosts horse racing, and its Kenyatta Cup race day falls on Sunday 11 October. The venue’s own calendar lists a run of concerts and themed nights into December.

Masshouse’s own page links to a map pin for the venue, which is the easiest thing to send a driver. Allow plenty of time for Saturday evening traffic, especially if you are coming from a hotel across town.

The organisers of Camp Mulla Funky Town warn that parking is limited. A ride-hailing app or a car arranged through your hotel is the simpler way to get there and back.

For more nights out, see the guide to what to do in Nairobi in October 2026.

How Camp Mulla Funky Town Tickets Work

Camp Mulla Funky Town tickets are sold on Mookh at mookh.com/funkytown, the page the venue links to. Mookh is a Kenyan ticketing platform.

Early Bird tickets cost KES 2,500 (US$19) and VIP tickets KES 6,000 (US$46). Both conversions use 129.75 Kenyan shillings to the US dollar on Tuesday 6 October 2026.

The terms say tickets cannot be refunded once bought. Entry is strictly for those aged 18 and over, and management can refuse entry.

Outside food and drink are not allowed, and drugs, firearms and weapons are banned. The terms also warn of loud sound levels, so earplugs are worth packing.

Buy through the Mookh page linked by the venue, and treat resale offers on social media with caution.

Tips for US and Foreign Visitors

Americans do not need a traditional visa, but each traveller, children included, needs an approved Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) first. Apply only on Kenya’s official portal, etakenya.go.ke, or its official mobile app.

A standard single-entry eTA costs US$30, and processing usually takes three days. The portal advises applying at least two weeks ahead, and an urgent service costs US$100 more.

Americans who visit often can choose a five-year multiple-entry eTA, which the portal prices at US$185. Your passport needs six months of validity and at least one blank page.

The US State Department rates Kenya at Level 2, “Exercise increased caution”, in an advisory issued on Tuesday 28 July 2026. It tells visitors not to travel to the Nairobi neighbourhoods of Eastleigh and Kibera because of crime and kidnapping.

The advisory says Uber and Bolt are common in Kenya’s major cities. It warns against hailing taxis on the street and asks visitors to use caution when walking or driving at night.

For a Camp Mulla Funky Town night that ends at 4am, book your ride home before you go in. Keep your phone and cards out of sight in the crowd and when you step outside.

Nairobi is eight hours ahead of New York on 7 November, after US clocks go back on 1 November. A 6pm start in Nairobi is 10am on the US East Coast.

If a short trip turns into a longer stay, the guide to moving to Kenya covers permits and costs for foreigners.

What Is Not Confirmed Yet

The organisers have not published a full line-up or said which Camp Mulla members will perform. The promised “major surprise” has not been revealed either.

Set times after the 6pm start are not public. The seller has also not said what tickets will cost once the early-bird batch is gone.

If you are planning around a particular performer, wait for the line-up before buying, because tickets are non-refundable.

The date, venue, current prices and official seller for Camp Mulla Funky Town are confirmed. That is enough to start planning a November trip.

More: Kenya news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

When and where is Camp Mulla Funky Town?

Camp Mulla Funky Town runs from 6pm on Saturday 7 November 2026 until 4am on Sunday 8 November. It takes place at Masshouse, inside Ngong Racecourse in Nairobi.

How much do Funky Town tickets cost?

Early Bird tickets cost KES 2,500 (US$19) and VIP tickets KES 6,000 (US$46) on Mookh. Tickets are non-refundable, and entry is strictly for those aged 18 and over.

Do Americans need a visa to visit Kenya?

No traditional visa is needed, but US citizens must get an approved Electronic Travel Authorisation online before travelling. A standard single-entry eTA costs US$30 on the official portal, etakenya.go.ke.

World.content:

CHILE · CONCERTS

Key Facts — What happened Puerto Rican star Luis Fonsi opens the Chile leg of his Mar Infinito World Tour in Santiago.

— The night He plays Santander Arena, the domed former Movistar Arena in Parque O’Higgins, on Thursday 1 April 2027 at 9pm.

— How to buy PuntoTicket is the only official seller, and the arena’s own box office opens on show days.

— What it costs Tickets run from 34,800 pesos (US$35) to 232,000 pesos (US$235), with the service charge included.

— What it means for you US citizens need a valid passport but no visa for tourist stays of up to 90 days.

— The catch Every price includes a 16% service charge, and the 20% presale discount needs a Banco Ripley card.

— Still open No door time or opening act has been announced; the arena posts door times on Instagram.

Luis Fonsi, the Puerto Rican singer behind the 2017 global hit “Despacito”, plays Santiago, Chile, on Thursday 1 April 2027. Tickets are on sale now, and US fans need no visa for the trip.

The show at Santander Arena, the former Movistar Arena, opens the Chile leg of his Mar Infinito World Tour. Fonsi grew up in Orlando, Florida, and the tour itself opens in Puerto Rico on Saturday 20 February 2027.

Who Luis Fonsi Is and Why This Show Matters

Luis Fonsi was born in San Juan, Puerto Rico, in 1978 and grew up in Orlando, Florida. At school there, he sang in a vocal group with Joey Fatone, later of the boy band NSYNC.

His global breakthrough came with “Despacito”, recorded with Daddy Yankee and released in January 2017. The remix with Justin Bieber spent 16 straight weeks at number one on the US Billboard Hot 100.

That run tied the record then held by “One Sweet Day” by Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men, Billboard noted. The “Despacito” video was also YouTube’s most-watched until November 2020.

The tour’s name is Spanish for “infinite sea”, a nod to the ocean and his Puerto Rican roots, Pudahuel reported. MAR also joins the initials of his daughter Mika, his wife Águeda and his son Rocco.

Tour announcements in Chile promise “Despacito”, “Échame la Culpa”, “Aquí Estoy Yo” and “No Me Doy por Vencido”. His recent releases “Cambiaré” and “Me Despido” are on the bill too, Cooperativa reported.

The tour starts in Puerto Rico and then visits Europe, Latin America, North America and Asia. In Chile, Luis Fonsi plays four dates, and Santiago comes first.

His official tour page then lists Gran Arena Monticello, in the O’Higgins region south of Santiago, on Friday 2 April. Concepción follows on Tuesday 6 April and Antofagasta, in the north, on Thursday 8 April.

Fans in the US have a closer option on Friday 11 December 2026, at the Prudential Center in Newark, New Jersey. He joins Amor En Vivo there, a radio station concert with several other artists, the arena says.

Tickets and Prices for the Santiago Show

PuntoTicket is the only official seller for Luis Fonsi in Santiago, as for every show at Santander Arena, the venue says. The arena also sells tickets at its own box office on show days.

The promoter is Producciones e Inversiones Swing, a Chilean company named on both the venue’s event page and the PuntoTicket listing. General sale opened on Thursday 17 September, with a limit of six tickets per purchase.

The prices below are totals, with PuntoTicket’s 16% service charge included. They are converted at 989 Chilean pesos to the US dollar, the rate on Tuesday 6 October 2026.

The cheapest seats are in the Tribuna section at 34,800 pesos (US$35). Platea Alta Silver costs 58,000 pesos (US$59), and Platea Alta Golden costs 69,600 pesos (US$70).

In the Platea Baja sections, prices run from 83,520 pesos (US$84) for Silver to 109,040 pesos (US$110) for Diamante. Golden Lateral costs 69,600 pesos (US$70), Golden 81,200 pesos (US$82), Platinum Lateral 104,400 pesos (US$106) and Platinum 127,600 pesos (US$129).

Diamante Lateral costs 162,400 pesos (US$164), Diamante 185,600 pesos (US$188), and Primeras Filas, the front rows, 232,000 pesos (US$235). Wheelchair places and companion seats cost 52,200 pesos (US$53) each, with limited stock.

Credit and debit cardholders of Banco Ripley, a Chilean bank, get 20% off the face value but not the service charge. With that discount, a Tribuna seat costs 28,800 pesos (US$29).

The offer covers a stock of 3,000 tickets, and PuntoTicket still showed it as available on Tuesday 6 October. Everyone who enters the arena needs a ticket of their own.

Santander Arena: The Venue and How to Get There

Santander Arena, where Luis Fonsi plays, stands inside Parque O’Higgins, a public park in central Santiago. Ticket listings give its address as Beaucheff 1204.

It was called Movistar Arena from 2008 until September 2026, when Banco Santander bought the naming rights, BioBioChile reported. It is the same indoor arena, with the same entrances.

Building work began in 1958 for the 1959 basketball world championship. The shell then stood unfinished for decades and earned the nickname “white elephant”.

It finally opened in 2006 as Arena Santiago, with a visit by the Dalai Lama. Today it holds about 15,500 people under a dome 50 metres (164 feet) high, according to the venue.

Walk-in access is through the Parque O’Higgins Metro station or from Tupper street, the arena says. The station sits on Line 2 of the Santiago Metro.

Parking is limited and must be bought in advance on PuntoTicket. Cars enter from Avenida Viel or Avenida Tupper, as shown on the parking ticket.

Every guest passes a security check with metal detectors. Bottles, food and drink, sharp objects, umbrellas, professional cameras and banners on sticks are not allowed, the venue’s rules say.

Smoking and vaping are banned inside the building. There are bars, terraces, two cafés and 13 snack counters on site, and free Wi-Fi covers parts of the arena.

Tips for US and Foreign Visitors

US citizens need no visa for tourist stays of 90 days or less, the US State Department says. Your passport must be valid for the whole stay.

The department also says tourists must be able to show at least US$46 a day for expenses. It adds that you receive a tourist card on arrival and must hand it back when you leave.

Take that passport to the show. The arena asks every guest to present a ticket together with an ID card or passport.

The State Department rates Chile at Level 2, “exercise increased caution”, and says street crime is common. It names Plaza de Armas, Bellavista, Barrio Lastarria and Mercado Central among Santiago’s pickpocketing hotspots.

It also warns that criminals have drugged and robbed US citizens. Keep your drink in sight, and keep your phone out of view in crowds.

Ride-share apps and taxis with orange and yellow licence plates are generally safe, the department says. It calls public transport generally safe, available and inexpensive.

A 9pm start on a Thursday means a late finish. Plan your ride back to the hotel before the show, not after the encore.

Peso prices are fixed, so the US$ cost moves with the exchange rate. Your card issuer may also add a foreign transaction fee to the bill.

The same arena hosts other big names before April, among them Def Leppard on Sunday 8 November. For more ideas this month, see what to do in Santiago in October 2026.

What Is Not Confirmed Yet

Door times have not been published. The venue says it announces them on its official Instagram account for each show.

No opening act has been named, and PuntoTicket lists Luis Fonsi alone on the bill. The songs named so far come from tour announcements, not from a published set list.

Only one Santiago date is on sale, and no second night has been announced. Tickets for the other Chile shows are sold separately through Ticketmaster, Puranoticia reported.

The US$ figures here are a guide. You pay in Chilean pesos, and the dollar amount will shift with the exchange rate before April.

More: Chile news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

When and where does Luis Fonsi play in Santiago?

Luis Fonsi plays Santander Arena, the former Movistar Arena in Parque O’Higgins, on Thursday 1 April 2027 at 9pm. It is the first of four Chile dates on his Mar Infinito World Tour.

How much are Luis Fonsi tickets in Santiago?

PuntoTicket, the only official seller, lists Luis Fonsi tickets from 34,800 pesos (US$35) to 232,000 pesos (US$235). These totals include a 16% service charge, and Banco Ripley cardholders get 20% off the face value.

Do Americans need a visa to see Luis Fonsi in Chile?

No. US citizens can see Luis Fonsi in Chile on a tourist stay of up to 90 days without a visa. Bring a passport valid for the whole stay, and carry it to the arena as ID.

World.content:

COSTA RICA · EXPATS & NOMADS

Key Facts — The country Costa Rica, in Central America, gets more tourists from the United States than from any other country.

— What happened Breeze, United, Delta and Southwest are adding nonstop flights to Costa Rica from five US cities between October and March.

— The first route Breeze Airways launched Tampa to San José flights on Saturday 3 October and now flies Wednesdays and Saturdays.

— The holiday flights United flies Washington Dulles to Liberia daily from Thursday 17 December 2026 to Monday 4 January 2027.

— New York Delta has scheduled weekly New York JFK to Liberia flights from Saturday 19 December 2026 to Saturday 10 April 2027.

— Late winter Southwest adds Nashville to Liberia from Saturday 13 February and Austin to San José from Saturday 13 March 2027.

— The catch Most routes are seasonal, and United’s Dulles flights run for only 19 days over the holidays.

New nonstop flights to Costa Rica start this season from Tampa, Washington, New York, Nashville and Austin. For US travelers in those cities, each route cuts out a change of planes on the way south.

The flights land at Costa Rica’s two main gateways, near the capital San José and in Liberia, close to the Pacific beaches. Most run only weekly or for a few weeks, so the dates shape your trip.

Five New Routes and When They Start

Four US airlines are adding nonstop flights to Costa Rica for the 2026-27 high season. In Costa Rica, the peak travel months run from December to April.

The United States is the country’s largest source of visitors. Close to 1.6 million US travelers arrived by air in 2025, according to the Costa Rican Tourism Institute (ICT).

Breeze Airways opens the list with its first-ever Costa Rica service, from Tampa to Juan Santamaría International Airport near San José. The ICT announced flights every Wednesday and Saturday from Saturday 3 October, on an Airbus A220 with 137 seats.

Tampa International Airport says Breeze launched the route on Saturday 3 October, with a gate party for the first passengers. The Tico Times, a Costa Rican English-language paper, listed a 6:40 a.m. departure and a 7:55 a.m. local arrival.

The airport calls these its first nonstop flights to Costa Rica in over 25 years. Breeze is currently the only airline flying the route nonstop, The Tico Times says.

United Airlines follows on Thursday 17 December with a daily flight from Washington Dulles to Guanacaste Airport in Liberia. It runs only until Monday 4 January 2027, covering Christmas and New Year.

The flight leaves Dulles at 8:51 a.m. and lands at 12:50 p.m. on a Boeing 737 MAX 9. Tom Kozlowski, United’s senior manager of network planning for Latin America, said it targets East Coast travelers heading for the beaches.

Delta Air Lines plans to return to Liberia from New York JFK on Saturday 19 December, The Tico Times reported. The weekly Saturday flight runs until Saturday 10 April 2027 on an Airbus A321neo.

Delta last flew the route about a decade ago. When it filed the plan in June, it had no New York flights to Costa Rica at all.

Delta’s filed schedule, as listed by the route-tracking site AeroRoutes, shows a 10:40 a.m. departure from JFK. The flight lands in Liberia at 3:25 p.m. local time.

Southwest Airlines adds Nashville to Liberia on Saturday 13 February 2027, The Tico Times reported. The weekly flight uses a Boeing 737 MAX 8 with 175 seats.

It is a new link for Guanacaste. Southwest flew Nashville to San José for a short run in March 2026.

On Saturday 13 March 2027, Southwest opens a weekly Austin to San José route. The outbound leaves Austin at 10:25 a.m. and lands at 2:05 p.m., The Tico Times reported.

San José or Liberia: Where the Flights Land

Costa Rica has two main international airports, and the new flights to Costa Rica split between them. Juan Santamaría International Airport, near the capital San José, is the busiest.

Breeze from Tampa and Southwest from Austin land there. It suits trips that start in the capital or in the Central Valley around it.

United, Delta and Southwest’s Nashville flights land at Guanacaste Airport, officially Daniel Oduber Quirós International, in Liberia. It is the closest major airport to the northern Pacific beaches.

Those beaches include Tamarindo, Playas del Coco, Flamingo, Nosara and the Gulf of Papagayo. For a beach trip, Liberia usually means a shorter drive than landing in San José.

The new routes add to nonstops that already exist. United flies to Liberia from Newark, Denver, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Houston and Chicago.

Delta serves Liberia year-round from Atlanta, Boston, Detroit and Minneapolis–St. Paul. Southwest connects it with several US cities, including Houston, Denver and Baltimore.

Southwest Adds Summer 2027 Flights to Guanacaste

On Friday 2 October, Guanacaste Airport and the ICT announced more Southwest flights for the summer of 2027. Austin to Liberia will run on Saturdays and Sundays from Saturday 5 June to Sunday 1 August 2027.

Nashville to Liberia comes back on Saturdays from Saturday 5 June to Saturday 31 July 2027. Both routes use the Boeing 737 MAX 8, and the airport says no Austin to Liberia nonstop operates today.

ICT executive president Marcos Borges said the routes give American travelers more connections and bring tourism jobs to Guanacaste. Renata González, the airport’s commercial and communications manager, called the United States its main international market.

Those summer flights to Costa Rica fall in the green season, when afternoon rain is common on the Pacific coast. Hotels often have more rooms free than in the December to April peak, The Tico Times noted.

Tips for US Visitors Flying to Costa Rica

US citizens need no visa for tourist stays of under 180 days, the US State Department says. Officers may grant fewer days, so leave by the departure date you are given.

Your passport must be valid for your whole stay, and you need a return ticket. Travelers arriving from parts of South America or Africa may need proof of yellow fever vaccination.

The State Department rates Costa Rica at Level 2, exercise increased caution, in an advisory issued on Thursday 2 April 2026. The reason given is crime, and this guide to safety in Costa Rica in 2026 has the details.

A colón near its strongest level on record means prices set in colones cost more in dollars than a few years ago. On Tuesday 6 October 2026, the rate was about 458 colones to the US dollar.

Book flights to Costa Rica early if you want the short holiday routes. United’s Dulles flights run for 19 days, while Delta’s and Southwest’s winter routes fly once a week.

Planning to stay for months and work online? Costa Rica offers a digital nomad visa for foreigners who earn a steady income from abroad.

What Is Not Confirmed Yet

Plans for new flights to Costa Rica can change before the first departure. Southwest announced a daily Las Vegas to San José route earlier this year, then cancelled it in July, citing fuel costs.

Check the last date of Southwest’s winter Nashville flights when you book. June reports gave Saturday 6 March 2027, but the airport’s October release says February to April.

United has not said whether its Dulles route will return for a longer season. Delta’s New York schedule ends on Saturday 10 April 2027.

Times quoted here are local times and can still shift before departure. For the background to the United and Austin routes, see how Costa Rica landed two new US flight routes in July.

More: Costa Rica news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which new flights to Costa Rica start in December 2026?

United flies daily from Washington Dulles to Liberia from Thursday 17 December 2026 to Monday 4 January 2027. Delta has scheduled Saturday flights from New York JFK to Liberia from 19 December 2026 to 10 April 2027.

Do US citizens need a visa to visit Costa Rica?

No visa is needed for stays under 180 days, the US State Department says. Officers may grant fewer days, and you need a passport valid for your stay plus a return ticket.

Which Costa Rica airport is closer to the beaches?

Guanacaste Airport in Liberia is the closest major airport to Tamarindo, Playas del Coco, Nosara and the Gulf of Papagayo. Juan Santamaría International Airport, near San José, suits trips that start in the capital.

World.title: Mexico Arrests Jalisco Cartel Operator ‘El Tanque’
World.content:
Guadalajara, capital of Jalisco state, where Zapopan forms part of the metropolitan area. File photo. Photo: "Catedral metropolitana de Guadalajara 01" by ProtoplasmaKid, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.

Security: Mexico

Key Facts —Who. Iván Cazarín Molina, known as “El Tanque” (the Tank), described by Mexican officials as a regional operator of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG). —What. Arrested on Monday 5 October 2026 by Army special forces, the National Guard and federal security officers, caught in the act, according to Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch. —Where. Zapopan, a city in the Guadalajara metropolitan area in Jalisco state, western Mexico. He is said to have operated in Veracruz, Oaxaca, Tabasco and Puebla. —US link. The US Treasury sanctioned him in September 2024 over the cartel’s fuel-theft business. —Status. These are allegations by the authorities. He is a suspect, and no court has ruled. —As of. 6 October 2026, 14:30 GMT.

Mexican federal forces arrested Iván Cazarín Molina, alias “El Tanque,” in Zapopan, Jalisco, on Monday 5 October 2026. Officials call him a regional operator of the Jalisco cartel and a trusted associate of its late founder, “El Mencho.” The US Treasury had already sanctioned him in 2024, and the cartel is a major source of the fentanyl and violence that reach US communities.

What We Know

Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch announced the arrest, saying it came from “intelligence work, investigation and coordination,” according to El Financiero. Mexican media report that Army special forces, the National Guard and the federal security ministry took part. They add that the National Intelligence Center and the federal prosecutor’s investigation agency supplied information.

Milenio reports that officers seized one vehicle, one firearm and a quantity of drugs. It says he was caught in the act. Excélsior adds that information was exchanged with the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) during the operation.

Officials describe him as a regional operator for the cartel in four states: Veracruz, Oaxaca, Tabasco and Puebla. They say he was close to Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, “El Mencho,” the cartel’s founder.

The authorities link him to homicide, extortion, illegal detention, fuel theft, money laundering and drug trafficking. El Universal reports that he is also linked to a 2015 attack on an Army helicopter in Jalisco, which killed soldiers and federal police. Excélsior dates that attack to 1 May 2015 in Villa Purificación and counts nine dead.

Officials gave his name only as “Iván N,” the usual Mexican practice before charges; Milenio and Excélsior give the full name, which matches the US Treasury sanctions list. Media accounts also differ on his rank. Most call him a regional operator or leader, while Excélsior’s headline calls him a co-founder. We use the officials’ wording.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Jalisco (Mexico) Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why the US Treasury Already Knew Him

On 10 September 2024, the US Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned a network linked to the cartel’s fuel theft. The action covered nine people and 26 Mexican companies. Treasury called Cazarín Molina a senior cartel member in El Mencho’s inner circle. It said his fuel-theft operation, in Jalisco and Veracruz, earns tens of millions of dollars a year for himself and the cartel.

The sanction freezes any US assets and bars Americans from doing business with him. Stolen fuel is one way the cartel turns crime into cash, alongside drugs and extortion.

The Cartel Without Its Founder

The arrest comes seven and a half months after the Army killed El Mencho in Tapalpa, Jalisco, on 22 February 2026. Violence and roadblocks followed in about 20 states. We reported in September that Mexico confirmed Juan Carlos Valencia González, known as “El Pelón,” as the new leader.

It is also the latest in a run of arrests of senior figures. In April we covered the capture of “El Jardinero”, described then as the second CJNG boss to fall since February.

A National Guard patrol in Guadalajara. File photo.

What Is Not Known

Officials have not said where he is being held or when he will face a judge. The cases against him will go to the federal prosecutors who handle organised crime, according to Mexican media, but no charges have been made public.

It is also unclear how much his arrest will disrupt fuel theft in Veracruz and neighbouring states, or whether the cartel will respond with violence, as it did in February. No US extradition request has been reported.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

For Americans, the main link is the sanctions record. Anyone with business ties to Mexican fuel retail or logistics should note that Treasury has named companies tied to him. This arrest does not remove those sanctions.

Guadalajara and the wider Jalisco area are popular with US visitors and residents. No unrest linked to the arrest had been reported in the coverage we reviewed. Travelers should follow the US State Department’s advisory for Jalisco and local alerts.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is “El Tanque”?

Iván Cazarín Molina, known as “El Tanque,” is described by Mexican officials as a regional operator of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel in Veracruz, Oaxaca, Tabasco and Puebla. The US Treasury sanctioned him in September 2024 over the cartel’s fuel-theft business.

Where and when was he arrested?

He was arrested in Zapopan, Jalisco, on Monday 5 October 2026 by Army special forces, the National Guard and federal security officers, according to Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch.

What is he accused of?

The authorities link him to homicide, extortion, illegal detention, fuel theft, money laundering and drug trafficking, and to a 2015 attack on an Army helicopter. These are allegations, and no court has ruled.

Why does this matter to US readers?

The US Treasury sanctioned him in 2024, and the Jalisco cartel is a major source of fentanyl and violence affecting US communities. The DEA is reported to have exchanged information during the operation.
