World.title: Chinese refiners increase oil imports from Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chinese independent refiners are swiftly increasing their imports of Iraqi and Qatari crude to compensate for a sharp decline in Iranian oil supplies.

As their stockpiles near depletion, private refineries in China are paying considerable premiums to acquire alternatives, according to Reuters.

Experts see that the step represents a desperate search for alternatives due to logistical obstacles, rather than a true rebound in Chinese domestic crude demand.

Private refineries in China have historically relied on deeply discounted, sanctioned Iranian oil to optimize their refining margins, previously importing over one million barrels per day. However, the US naval blockade and the higher cost of Russian oil alternatives are two major geopolitical factors that have forced a shift.

A rigorous US blockade linked to the larger crisis involving Iran has trapped at least 50 tankers transporting mostly Iranian petroleum off the Chinese coast, cutting off the refiners’ key supply source.

State-owned Chinese refiners have successfully secured the majority of the available Russian crude oil. As a result of the fierce competition, Russian barrels now command significant premiums of roughly $30 per barrel above Brent, driving smaller independent refiners out.

Refiners have purchased at least 12 million barrels of Iraqi and Qatari oil for October and November delivery, with total estimates ranging from 15 million to 20 million barrels.

Buyers are mostly interested in the sulfur-rich Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy grades. Independent refiners normally reject these higher grades in favor of lighter Iranian or Russian choices, but they are embracing them since they are readily available.

Major global commodities trading firms such as Vitol Group, Trafigura Group, Mercuria Energy Group, and TotalEnergies SE are facilitating the deals.

This move is being aided by a steady recovery in total exports leaving the Arabian Gulf via the Strait of Hormuz, making Middle Eastern options physically available even as regional tensions remain.

World.title: Turkey to turn Iraq’s Development Road into multi-fuel energy corridor
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkey intends to develop the planned Development Road from Iraq’s southern ports to Europe into a multi-fuel energy corridor worth $80 billion annually.

According to Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar, this strategic route will go beyond typical freight transit by incorporating crucial infrastructure for oil, natural gas, and power transmission.

In a statement to Anadolu Agency (AA), Bayraktar expressed Turkey’s enthusiasm for building the Development Road not merely as a transport corridor but also as a strategic energy route. This route would be bolstered by the inclusion of oil, natural gas, and electricity transmission lines along its path.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi instructed in July the establishment of a defined structure to finance and implement the strategic project of the Development Road, assuring the start of practical steps within a planned timeline.

In early June, the head of the state-owned General Company for Ports of Iraq (GCPI), Farhan al-Fartousi, said that the planning process for the project and the al-Faw Grand Port has made tremendous progress, with essential operating plans already submitted to the government.

The project will enter the implementation phase following government approval in the coming months, according to al-Fartousi.

The $17 billion project, which will connect the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq to the Turkish border by constructing a railway and road network, is anticipated to transform Iraq into a transit center by cutting the time it takes to travel from Asia to Europe.

In addition to pipelines for energy transportation, the project’s railway will significantly assist in the transportation of commodities, with a first-phase capacity of 3.5 million tons and a second-phase capacity of 7.5 million tons.

By connecting the port city of Basra to Turkey via an overland route, the logistics project will compete with Egypt’s Suez Canal and establish Basra as a gateway to Europe.

In 2024, Turkey formed a council involving Bulgaria, Hungary, and Serbia to arrange the connection of Europe with Iraq’s Development Road.

As a worldwide corridor for commodities and energy transportation, the project is expected to attract international commerce and create considerable employment opportunities and investment possibilities in Iraq and other countries in the region.

World.title: Iraq’s seaborne oil exports jump to 2.57 million bpd in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s crude oil exports rose for the fourth consecutive month in September, growing by over nine percent—equivalent to 218,000 barrels per day—to reach their highest level since the start of the Iran war.

Iraq’s seaborne crude oil exports jumped to 2.57 million barrels per day in September, up from 2.35 million barrels per day in August.

Despite the monthly improvement, Iraqi oil exports in September remained 25 percent lower than the 3.41 million barrels per day recorded during the same month in 2025.

Iraq’s oil exports gradually recovered in September, after hitting a low of 98,000 barrels per day in May.

Iraq’s average crude oil exports plummeted by 52 percent between January and September 2026, to an average of 1.6 million barrels per day, down from 3.34 million barrels per day in the same period in 2025.

The volume of oil exports surpassed three million barrels per day at the beginning of the year before experiencing a major shock due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which caused shipments to collapse to 540,000 barrels per day in March.

Exports continued to fall sharply, reaching historic lows of more than 90 percent in April and May before gradually recovering to 2.57 million barrels per day in September.

World.title: Iraq targets 1M electric vehicles via Green Taxi initiative
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Environment reaffirmed on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, that private sector investment forms the bedrock of its national “Green Taxi” initiative and the phased transition toward deploying one million electric vehicles (EVs).

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Haidar Qasim Al-Darraji, Director General of the General Company for Carbon Economics at the Ministry of Environment, outlined a comprehensive framework to transform Iraq’s transportation grid into an investable, eco-friendly ecosystem.

Al-Darraji emphasized that the green transit transition cannot operate as a conventional state-run enterprise, but rather as an integrated public-private partnership (PPP) bringing together government regulators, commercial banks, private equity investors, energy providers, and automotive innovators.

Under this model, the state will establish statutory and technical codes, streamline the regulatory climate, lay foundational infrastructure, and verify carbon credit baselines. In turn, private industry will handle capital expenditure, vehicle manufacturing, importation, fleet operations, maintenance logistics, and the rollout of solar-powered charging networks.

Inter-agency groundwork is already underway through coordinated channels involving the Ministry of Environment, the Ministry of Transport, and the General Company for Private Transport Management. The bodies are evaluating existing municipal transit garages and public transport depots for conversion into EV charging hubs powered by distributed solar photovoltaic systems.

Clarifying the scale of the transition, Al-Darraji noted that the target of one million electric vehicles is a phased, metrics-driven national roadmap rather than an overnight influx. Rollouts will begin via scalable pilot projects across Baghdad before expanding into the provinces.

The strategic objective is to cultivate an integrated domestic industrial value chain around e-mobility—spanning local assembly, maintenance, bank lending, commercial insurance, ride-hailing software, and monetization under sovereign carbon credit mechanisms—thereby curbing state fiscal burdens and generating skilled technical employment.

In tandem with public sustainability policies, regional automotive distributors are expanding their electrified footprints across the domestic market. Ahmed Al-Ani, Branch Director of Toyota Iraq, revealed to INA that Iraq has emerged as a major regional adopter of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), ranking as the second-largest consumer of hybrid cars in the Middle East.

Highlighting consumer demand for green mobility, Al-Ani announced the official domestic market launch of two electrified Toyota flagships: the all-electric bZ4X Touring SUV and the RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle (PHEV), offering extended electric range and modern efficiency tailored to Iraq’s expanding charging landscape.

World.title: US dollar holds above 160,000 IQD in Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar held firm above the 160,000-dinar threshold across Iraq’s parallel currency markets on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, consolidating Monday’s steep gains across trading hubs in Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra.

The persistent gap between free-market rates and the Central Bank of Iraq’s official peg of 131,000 dinars per $100 continues to hover near 22.5 percent as exchange bureaus navigate heavy cash demand.

Market data showed that exchange bureaus and trading counters in the capital city of Baghdad maintained cash selling rates at 160,500 dinars per $100, while buying bids ticked slightly higher to 160,150 dinars, narrowing the intraday bid-ask spread.

In Erbil, the regional hub of the Kurdistan Region, parallel counters offered greenbacks at 160,000 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 159,750 dinars. In the southern trade center of Basra, rates rose to match the 160,000 mark, with cash sales quoted at 160,000 dinars per $100 and buying bids settling at 159,500 dinars.

The elevated rates across major cities reflect ongoing liquidity pressures as retail merchants and unbanked importers seek physical foreign currency outside the formal electronic transfer platform. Despite regular market interventions and central bank oversight, speculative buying and regional fiscal uncertainties continue to anchor cash prices above key psychological thresholds.

World.title: Yemen’s Houthis claim attack on Riyadh airport, deny losing territory
World.content:
Sanaa – Yemen’s Houthis claimed an attack on the main airport in the Saudi capital while also denying on Tuesday losing territory to government forces, as fighting intensified.

After declaring a counter-offensive, government forces claimed Monday to have pushed the Houthis out of the Bab al-Mandab area, a key shipping route in the Red Sea, as well as the port city of Mocha, which was captured last month.

Claims by both sides have been impossible to independently verify with the situation on the ground moving fast and access for journalists difficult.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed on Telegram that the group still held all territory recently seized, including strategic areas along the Red Sea coast.

Their fighters “have full control over all their advances on the ground”, he said.

He said the Houthis had carried out dozens of strikes in the past few hours targeting government forces in Yemen’s Al-Jawf and Marib regions, while also attacking Taiz governorate.

On Monday night, the Houthis said they had struck Riyadh airport and a refinery belonging to Saudi state oil giant Aramco.

Loud explosions rattled the Saudi capital on Monday evening.

On Tuesday Saudi Arabia’s civilian aviation authority said at least three people were also wounded in attacks on Jazan and Najran airports near the Yemen border a day earlier.

Saudi Arabia, the main backer of the Yemeni government, has been providing air support for a counter-offensive launched by government forces.

– ‘Victories on several fronts’ –

Yemen’s government forces claimed late Monday that they had achieved “victories on several fronts”, but military sources with the government nevertheless refrained from officially confirming taking Mocha, only saying they had cut the one supply route to the area.

They also said they expelled the Houthis from several areas in Taiz in the southwest, where fighting has surged in recent days.

Yemen’s government has announced a goal of retaking all Houthi territory — home to most of the country’s population, and much of it held for more than a decade.

Yemen’s civil war flared up again in July after years of relative calm, opening a new front in the wider Middle East war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February.

The Houthis last month seized control of the entire western coastline of Yemen along the Red Sea in the country’s deadliest fighting in years.

Since then, they have regularly targeted oil and military installations in Saudi Arabia and have declared a maritime blockade on its ships.

Pakistan and Turkey have pledged to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia under a mutual defence pact following weeks of Houthi attacks.

The Yemen conflict has caused a humanitarian crisis. Since the renewed fighting broke out, more than 184,000 people have been displaced from their homes, according to the United Nations.

A spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was “deeply concerned by the sharp escalation in fighting”. He condemned “the continued Houthi cross-border attacks” on Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Iraq welcomed record 10 million tourists in 2025
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq welcomed approximately 10 million international tourists throughout 2025, marking an unprecedented modern benchmark for the country’s travel sector, according to official figures disclosed on Monday, October 5, 2026, by Fadhil Al-Badrani, Undersecretary of the Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities.

The influx, which encompasses both religious pilgrims and cultural heritage travelers, underscores the country’s growing appeal as regional connectivity expands. Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Al-Badrani detailed the institutional mechanisms governing inbound traveler verification.

He explained that entry data is tracked through an integrated federal reporting apparatus linking the National Data Center, the Ministry of Interior, the Border Ports Commission, and international civil airports across Baghdad, Najaf, Basra, and Erbil.

These inter-agency registries are channeled directly to the Tourism Commission and the Ministry of Culture to compile precise statutory records.

Al-Badrani acknowledged that international tourism flows during 2026 experienced an unavoidable slowdown, driven by regional security volatility and logistical strains that dampened cross-border leisure travel across the Middle East.

However, he contrasted current headwinds with the record-setting performance of 2025, where sustained domestic stability and streamlined entry visas facilitated massive arrivals.

The 10-million visitor total was primarily anchored by Iraq’s religious tourism corridors—chiefly major annual pilgrimages to holy shrines in Karbala, Najaf, Kadhimiya, and Samarra—supplemented by an expanding cohort of international visitors touring Mesopotamian archaeological landmarks, including Babylon, Ur, Hatra, and the UNESCO-listed Iraqi Marshlands.

Al-Badrani emphasized that surpassing 10 million arrivals represents a milestone compared to previous decades, demonstrating the tourism industry’s capacity to serve as a vital pillar for economic diversification and sovereign non-oil revenue generation.

World.title: Iraq considers raising official dollar rate to 1,500 IQD and dropping currency zeros
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Safaa Al-Jabri, member of parliament for the Al-Sadiqoun bloc and member of the Parliamentary Economic Committee, revealed that the federal government is reviewing a proposal to adjust Iraq’s official exchange rate from 1,310 dinars to 1,500 dinars per U.S. dollar, while advancing high-level deliberations to redenominate the national currency and potentially remove zeros.

Speaking in a televised interview, Al-Jabri projected that sovereign state revenues for the 2027 federal budget will surpass $110 billion, declaring that Iraq has successfully weathered the acute economic fallout triggered by past disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz and Basra export halts.

According to Al-Jabri, fiscal parameters for the upcoming national budget are being restructured on the back of rising non-oil customs and tax receipts, an unprecedented $8 billion to $10 billion generated from domestic petroleum sales, and projected crude oil export earnings exceeding $85 billion.

He noted that Iraqi crude sales currently benchmark around $80 to $82 per barrel, generating approximately $5 billion in monthly export revenues, providing budgetary headroom as trade bottlenecks and logistics gradually normalize.

Regarding currency and fiscal policy, Al-Jabri highlighted key government plans:

Official Exchange Rate Revision: Leaked preliminary drafts of the federal budget proposal—which carries a planned deficit between 25 and 30 trillion dinars—contain a formal submission from the Minister of Finance proposing to adjust the official statutory exchange rate to 150,000 dinars per $100 (1,500 IQD per USD). Al-Jabri noted that no binding cabinet decision has been finalized to date.

Currency Redenomination: Serious technical discussions are underway between the Prime Minister’s Office and the Central Bank of Iraq regarding currency redesign and the removal of three zeros. The measure is currently stalled only by legal jurisdictional reviews to identify the specific governing authority legally empowered to greenlight and execute the structural transition.

Critique of Past Budget Frameworks: Al-Jabri criticized previous administrations for populist fiscal practices, claiming that state budgets were prepared through rote copy-paste mechanisms for nearly twenty years under former Finance Minister Taif Sami, who had risen through the ministry ranks from director general of budget to minister.

Public Liabilities & Contract Terminations: The lawmaker highlighted structural financial arrears inherited by the treasury, including outstanding wheat procurement payouts owed to local farmers, unpaid rationing supply dues claimed by Al-Owais Company across 2025 and 2026, and 33 billion dinars in overdue liabilities tied to road and bridge construction. In response, Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi has canceled legacy public work contracts where execution progress remained below 20 percent.

The potential devaluation of the official dinar to 1,500 IQD per dollar represents an effort to narrow the spread with the parallel currency market—which recently traded above 160,000 dinars per $100—while curbing the planned fiscal deficit for the 2027 fiscal cycle.

World.title: FIR against BJP BLA over 'false' Form-7 applications, first such case in Telangana
World.content:
NEW DELHI: An FIR has been registered against a BJP Booth Level Agent (BLA) for allegedly filing "false" Form-7 applications seeking the deletion of 30 voters from the electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

The case is the first FIR registered in Telangana over allegations of submitting Form-7 applications containing "false" information, news agency PTI reported.

The FIR was registered at Chikkadapally Police Station against BJP BLA S Balachander following a complaint by an election official. Police have invoked relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Representation of the People Act.

"Following a complaint that the BLA submitted forms for deletion of 30 electors, we have registered an FIR. The matter is under investigation," a police official told PTI.

Earlier, Telangana Congress leaders had approached Chief Electoral Officer C Sudharshan Reddy, alleging that Balachander, the BJP's BLA in Musheerabad, had submitted Form-7 applications seeking deletion of the names of 30 electors.

The Congress alleged that the applications amounted to an attempt to unlawfully remove genuine voters from the electoral rolls and sought legal action against those responsible.





The Telangana Congress also approached Hyderabad Police Commissioner VC Sajjanar, seeking registration of an FIR and an SIT investigation into what it described as a suspected BJP plan to carry out large-scale deletion of genuine voters during the SIR.

In its complaint, the Congress alleged that the BJP BLA in the Musheerabad assembly constituency had submitted Form-7 applications seeking deletion of the names of another BJP BLA, Sharfuddin, and members of his family.

Form-7 is used by voters to file objections to the proposed inclusion or seek deletion of a name from an existing electoral roll.

The BJP has rejected the allegations. Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao said that no BJP BLA had submitted any such Form-7 applications.

NEW DELHI: Captain Smit Machchhar is âmaking steady progressâ and âregaining his healthâ after being seriously injured in an attack by his co-pilot on a flydubai flight last week, the Indian Embassy in the UAE said on Tuesday.Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot, an Omani national with a crash axe, an emergency tool typically kept in the cockpit during flydubai flight FZ1073 on Wednesday. World.title: Jack Dorsey’s Bitchat taken off Indian app stores over law-and-order concerns: Report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Jack Dorseyâs Bluetooth-based messaging app Bitchat has been removed from Indian app stores following government intervention, putting the spotlight on concerns over decentralised communication.

Government sources quoted by news agency PTI said on Tuesday that the app posed a law-and-order concern and therefore had to be taken down.

The sources told PTI that Bitchat allows users to send messages through multiple Bluetooth âhopsâ without relying on conventional internet connectivity, raising concerns that it could be used to bypass restrictions imposed by authorities.

âThe government is duty-bound to maintain law and order,â sources said, adding that the app's ability to facilitate communication through Bluetooth was a concern.

On proposals to restrict minors' access to social media, government sources said there was no such proposal under consideration. They pointed to Australia's experience, saying restrictions had not prevented children from accessing social media without accounts.

The government is instead consulting industry representatives and experts, including those with expertise in psychology, sources said.

âWe have to find a better solution...when the right solution comes, we will bring it in front of you,â the sources said, stressing that a solution needed to be found.





Apple removed Bitchat from the India App Store following a demand from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Dorsey said in an X post on Saturday.

âGovernment of India officially removes Bitchat from the App Store,â Dorsey wrote, sharing a screenshot of Apple's App Review notice.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The notice said the removal was âper demand from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)â because the app âincludes content that is illegal in Indiaâ.

It cited Section 69(A) of the Information Technology Act, 2000, under which the takedown demand was issued.

Google has also removed the app from the Play Store in India, while Apple said it remained available in other territories selected by the developer. Its TestFlight version would also no longer be available for testing in India.

Bitchat had previously faced government action in July. The Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C) had then directed GitHub to restrict access to its repositories, citing concerns that the decentralised network could enable communication during internet restrictions and make lawful detection more difficult.

World.title: US House passes resolution honouring Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar, condemns 'act of terrorism'
World.content:
Smit Machchhar is recovering in Abu Dhabi hospital from multiple injuries

Resolved, That the House of Representativesâ (1) honors Captain Smit Machchhar for extraordinary courage in protecting every soul aboard his aircraft; (2) commends the heroic actions of the off-duty pilots, cabin crew, and passengers who secured the flight deck and brought the aircraft safely down; (3) wishes Captain Machchhar and all who were injured a full recovery; (4) condemns the attack on Flydubai Flight 1073 as an act of terrorism and as an attack on the safety of international civil aviation; and (5) calls for a full and expeditious investigation by the Governments of Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, and for the United States and Israel to be kept fully informed.

The US House of Representatives have introduced a resolution honouring Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar who was stabbed by his Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami on September 30.The resolution introduced as "Honoring Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew and passengers of Flydubai Flight 1073, and condemning the attempted terrorist attack on that flight" by Josh Gottheimer, Don Bacon and Michael McCaul, described the incident and hailed Machchhar."On September 30, 2026, Flydubai Flight 1073 departed Dubai International Airport for Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, Israel, carrying approximately 174 passengers, the majority of them Israeli citizens, including 4 United States citizens and 27 children," it stated."Whereas, midway through the flight, the first officer attacked the captain on the flight deck with the aircraftâs emergency crash axe and attempted to seize the flight controls, and the aircraft lost more than 14,000 feet of altitude in under 30 seconds," it desribed the incident. Whereas Captain Smit Machchhar, a citizen of India, fought off the attack and, despite grave injuries, used his remaining strength to unlock the cockpit door so that off-duty pilots could enter and land the aircraft and so that crew and passengers could restrain the first officer; Whereas the aircraft landed safely at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia with all passengers and crew accounted for; and Whereas, on October 3, 2026, the Attorney General of the United Arab Emirates announced that the Emirati investigation had determined that the first officer attempted to carry out a terrorist act," it added.Then it went to resolve as follows:On September 30, Flydubai Flight FZ1073, carrying more than 170 passengers and crew from Dubai to Tel Aviv, was forced into an emergency diversion after the co-pilot attacked Captain Smit Machchhar in the cockpit with a crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft.The plane rapidly lost altitude before Machchhar, despite suffering serious injuries, managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to overpower the attacker; two off-duty pilots then helped land the aircraft safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.The UAE subsequently launched an investigation, and on October 3 its Attorney General said the probe had found that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a terrorist act. Investigators are continuing to examine the circumstances, motive, possible links and physical and digital evidence, with authorities in other countries also looking into the incident.

World.title: Anti-ragging guidelines drawn up, State informs Kerala HC
World.content:
The Keralam government informed the Kerala High Court on Tuesday that the Anti-Ragging and Student Welfare Guidelines have been drawn up to prevent and prohibit ragging, punish culprits and provide a healthy atmosphere on campuses. The Division Bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice C. Jayachandran had previously directed the State to issue guidelines based on the draft Kerala Prohibition of Ragging (Amendment) Bill, until it was enacted. The guidelines were drawn up with the objectives of preventing ragging and explaining the legal rights and responsibilities of students and educational institutions. The guidelines also aim to establish a clear mechanism for reporting complaints, safeguard victims and witnesses in ragging cases, ensure free and fair enquiry, clarify legal and disciplinary consequences of ragging and achieve “absolute welfare of students”.

The guidelines would apply to all educational institutions in Keralam and other spaces accessed by students during studies such as hostels, other dwelling places, means of transportation and waiting places for transportation. The Kerala State Legal Services Authority (KeLSA), the petitioner, pointed out that the punishment had not increased in the draft guidelines. KeLSA also suggested certain changes in wording to clarify the spaces encompassed under the guidelines. The court directed the State to issue the guidelines with the suggested change in phrasing. However, it held that enhancement of punishment would require an amendment to the governing Act, which would be considered at a later point.

The guidelines stated that any act of physical abuse and ragging through digital modes, body shaming, teasing, abusing, or playing practical jokes to hurt a student would be considered ragging. A person who commits, participates in, abets or propagates ragging within or outside an educational institution would be punished as per the Kerala Prohibition of Ragging Act, 1998. A student convicted of such offences would be dismissed from the educational institution and would not be admitted to any other institution for three years from the date of dismissal.

The guidelines stated that every educational institution must have an anti-ragging committee, an anti-ragging squad, a mentoring cell, and a wellness clinic and counselling cell. The universities would also be tasked with setting up an anti-ragging monitoring cell. The guidelines also require that a State-level anti-ragging monitoring cell or anti-ragging commission be established.

If a complaint is prima facie verified, it must be handed over to the police within 24 hours, and the accused student must be suspended immediately. If a ragging complaint was found to be concealed or unreported, the guidelines allow action to be taken against the head of the institution. It also sought to establish anti-ragging cells in police stations.
