Tech.title: Arturia adds proper sound design tools to its AstroLab synths
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Arturia’s AstroLab series was already amongst the best stage keyboards out there. They essentially put the company’s AnalogLab suite of vintage synth emulations, sampled pianos, and original instrument plugins into playable hardware. But they were ultimately glorified preset browsers. You could lightly tweak patches using the four macro controls, or dial in some effects, but you couldn’t do any real sound design. That’s all changed now with the AstroLab 2.0 update.

The latest firmware adds a Sound Edit menu that lets you dig into the individual parameters of any instrument. It’s not super intuitive to quickly fire up a blank patch from the instrument of your choosing, and these more advanced sound design tools require some menu diving, but once you get there, creating custom sounds is pretty easy.

The quickest way to build patches from scratch is to make a custom category for templates and save initialized patches for each instrument there. For example, upload a basic Moog bass patch template from the AnalogLab desktop app, then you can tweak it to your heart’s content and save it as a completely new sound directly on the hardware.

Since a firmware update can’t add more knobs and buttons, you still have to make all the changes with the four macro knobs and page through settings four at a time. It can be a bit time-consuming, and you’re not going to do a bunch of on-the-fly tweaking, but it gets the job done.

Arturia has also added a new collection of multisampled instruments, including pianos, strings, and brass sections that offer more realistic acoustic instruments. This is one area where its competition clearly outclassed the AstroLab, but this should help close the gap. In total, there are 67 new patches.

Lastly, Arturia has also made a number of small quality-of-life improvements. The octave LEDs will now show transposition, aftertouch has been tweaked to feel more responsive, and app connectivity has supposedly been made more reliable. While connectivity with the desktop AnalogLab seems rock-solid, the mobile AstroLab Connect app seems as flaky as ever.

AstroLab 2.0 is available now as a free update for all AstroLab keyboards.

Trump Mobile appears to have suffered a data breach that may have exposed the data of 3,615 people, according to reports from PCMag and Straight Arrow News. The breach reportedly included names, home addresses, emails, phone numbers, and order information.

PCMag and Straight Arrow News contacted several individuals in the dataset, who confirmed that the leaked information was accurate. The leaked data may include people who never fully signed up for Trump Mobile, as one person told PCMag that they never managed to set up their account but still gave the company their email address and phone number. A hacking group called BYOD claimed responsibility for the potential breach. One member told PCMag that they breached the phone service by installing a remote access trojan on an employee of Liberty Mobile — the carrier that powers Trump Mobile’s network. The group also claims to have access to the backend of Trump Mobile’s website, according to Straight Arrow News.

The Verge reached out to Trump Mobile with a request for comment but didn’t immediately hear back.

Tech.title: Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery complete $110 billion media megamerger
Tech.content:
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Paramount has completed its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, forming a combined company known as Skydance. The merger officially puts Paramount and WBD’s film studios, along with major networks and brands like HBO, CBS News, and CNN, under one roof.

The road to the media megamerger has been a rocky one for Paramount, which secured an agreement in February after waging a months-long battle against Netflix for WBD. Since then, it has faced criticism from both lawmakers and Hollywood talent about the negative impact of media consolidation.

Paramount cleared its last major hurdle last month, as it settled with 12 states that sued to block the deal over antitrust concerns. Under the settlement, Skydance must release a minimum number of theatrical films over the next five years, starting with 30 in years one and two. It must also spend at least $300 million more on production in the US compared to what the companies spent last year combined.

David Ellison will lead Skydance alongside Ynon Kreiz, the former chairman and CEO of Mattel.

“Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance but for our entire industry,” Ellison said in the announcement. “From the start, our ambition was to bring these two storied studios together and create a stronger competitor, with the talent, resources, and reach to tell great stories in every genre, on every platform, for audiences everywhere. Now that ambition is a reality.”

Tech.title: LibreOffice says ‘no AI’ is now a software feature
Tech.content:
If you’re looking for a document editor that doesn’t use artificial intelligence, LibreOffice may be just the software for you.

The Document Foundation, the nonprofit software maker behind the open source document editor LibreOffice, said in a blog post this week that while it does not reject AI out of hand, it “will not add” AI to its software for the foreseeable future.

The blog post comes weeks after the release of the latest version of LibreOffice in late August, in which the nonprofit reiterated that the software “contains no generative AI features.”

LibreOffice said at the time that this was a “deliberate design position” to ensure that users’ documents are not uploaded to a server for processing and that no part of the software requires a network connection to function. The nonprofit added that its software is used by tens of millions of people and organizations, and that users should retain control over their data.

“Any organisation handling confidential, legally privileged or personal data needs to know where that data goes, and the only assurance that survives an audit is that it does not leave the machine,” the organization said.

LibreOffice says users can still choose to use AI tools by installing software extensions that connect the document editor to local AI models.

The decision to eschew including AI features bucks the trend of many software makers today that try to pack in as much AI as possible, even to the detriment of the user experience. The so-called “enshittification” of modern software by packing in unnecessary and bloated features, like chatbots and AI assistants, prompted some developers to create or include features that block or remove AI features altogether.

AI tools often require the users’ data to be uploaded and processed on a remote server, which the user has no control over how the data is stored or for how long.

LibreOffice said that there is currently “no integration” that meets all of its requirements, such as ensuring that the users’ data stays on their device and that there is no reliance on a single AI provider, among other considerations. The organization’s criteria for including AI into its software is not a “definitive rejection,” but the decision was an assessment of the technology today, rather than a “judgement on the value of the sector.”

“Until then, there will be no AI of any kind in the default installation; extensions will be available for those who wish to integrate AI features, and we will closely monitor where the technology is actually heading,” said LibreOffice’s blog post.

LibreOffice is one of the many kinds of open source and alternative software used to escape the clutches of Silicon Valley tech giants.

Tech.title: Vinod Khosla believes ex-DeepMind engineer’s Wajo will win agent market on trust
Tech.content:
The personal-agent space has become closely competitive in recent weeks, with Meta’s Muse, OpenAI’s Dot, and Instinct taking the lead and more competitors being launched each week. But Vinod Khosla is betting on former Google and DeepMind engineer Shivani Poddar’s Wajo for one simple reason: trust.

“I think the most important thing in an agent, because it’s acting for you, is trust. You have to have trust in the agent, and I think compared to either Muse or Instinct, Wajo is the most trustworthy because it is architected to focus on trust and safety first, and some of the others are not,” Khosla told TechCrunch over a call.

“I mean, who wants to give all their data to Facebook [Meta]? I don’t. And if I give my data to Facebook, I’m the product, not the product I am buying, because they are in the ad business. So trust is important, and most people don’t trust a large company like Facebook,” he added.

In broad strokes, Wajo’s Fo agent works very much like Muse or Instinct. The agent can work across iMessage and WhatsApp, and has a web interface with cards of potential tasks. Errands are organized into categories like “scheduling,” “gifting,” and “life admin.” Its agent can also call businesses or other people on your behalf, booking or canceling services as needed.

In a few early tests, I asked it to call an airline to check for upgrades, and it successfully did so. However, when I asked it to call my partner and remind her to feed the cats, the call didn’t go smoothly, and disclosures were less clear. As rivals like Instinct and Muse are also rolling out calling ability slowly, we might see more discussions around how an AI calling on someone’s behalf should disclose itself. One of the unique things about the tool is that it can hire a human to complete a task when needed.

Apart from this, Fo can create a virtual credit card and pay on your behalf without disclosing your details. The agent also has its own email and can converse with people and businesses. When websites or services block AI agents, Fo can inform the user to take action or create a group with the user and the business for verification.

The startup has also secured backing from Jeff Dean and Gokul Rajaram, but didn’t specify the money raised. Wajo didn’t provide any numbers around users but said that it’s being used in 107 countries and has grown 10x since its launch in late September.

Founder story

Prior to founding Wajo, Poddar worked in various engineering roles at Meta, Google, and DeepMind and was invovled in making the first Facebook assistant. She said that she wanted to build products that were useful to people.

“The whole journey of bringing Gemini to the world and building safety for it made me realize the technological depth that you need to do this. Google is so good in technology that sometimes it can be left behind in product. I thought I needed to do something that is both technology and product at the same time. It has to be something different, which is very grounded in what the user needs,” Poddar told TechCrunch over a call.

Image Credits:Wajo

The former Google engineering lead mirrored Khosla’s thoughts around trust, and emphasized that it was one of the core principles for Wajo.

“Trust is something you have to build from the get-go because one of the technological things that has not been solved yet is teaching agents to unlearn. If they get access to your personal data on day zero, they will always have it for the future. I think trust needs to be built from day zero, not only in your architecture, but in product choices,” she said.

The company is doing work in a few areas in relation to trust and safety. It has applied for a patent for its virtual card system that hides users’ information from sites. For calls, the company said it will include a “trusted contact” list for users whose agents can call them. When you get a call, you can also tell the agent not to call you again, and Wajo records that preference.

In the meantime, wajo’s Fo has a tos complaint solution to agents on Amazon folks. Shop on :) https://t.co/yx2SoknZIy — Shivani Poddar (@shivanipod) October 6, 2026

The startup’s challenge is not to raise privacy concerns like other agents, especially as it is marketing safety as a core value. It also claims that despite tools like Muse being blocked by Amazon, its architecture follows the e-commerce service’s terms of service.

Wajo said that in the coming months it will explore how its Fo agent will work in social settings across multiple users, with the core idea of keeping privacy intact.

Tech.title: Emmys will move from broadcast TV to Prime Video in 2027
Tech.content:
In Brief

Amazon announced on Tuesday that Prime Video will be the new home for the Emmy Awards, marking another major Hollywood awards show’s move from broadcast television to streaming. This will also be the first time that the ceremony has had a dedicated home, as the show rotated across broadcasters like ABC, CBS, Fox, and NBC over the past seven decades.

Prime Video will stream the awards show worldwide for six years for free, starting in 2027, where it will go live in over 240 countries and territories. Non-Amazon Prime subscribers will also be able to watch the awards show on the Prime Video platform.

The terms of the deal were not disclosed.

The move comes as the Emmys face potential viewership declines, as more of its audience moves to streaming services. This year’s ratings for the 78th primetime Emmy Awards on NBC were down nearly 10% from the year prior, after a couple of years of growth, the AP reported. However, the telecast’s 6.87 million viewers this year were higher than its all-time low of 4.3 million in January 2024.

The Emmys aren’t the only major awards show making the shift to streaming. Last year, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences announced a deal giving YouTube the rights to stream the Oscars beginning in 2029, while Netflix has streamed the Screen Actors Guild Awards since 2024.

Tech.title: Mistral’s new 1T model aims to leapfrog closed and open rivals
Tech.content:
The race between open and closed AI is on, and Europe is still in the mix. On Tuesday, French AI lab Mistral AI released Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a new large multimodal model aiming to leapfrog both American and Chinese rivals — following what French president Macron described as “a third way in AI.”

Amid a growing divide between closed models that can be unplugged and open models that are often made in China, Mistral is positioning ML4 as an alternative to both. Nicknamed Le Chonk in reference to its 1 trillion parameters, ML4 is definitely not small; but is not an open-weight model yet. For the time being, it can only be accessed via a public guardrail endpoint, but Mistral plans to make its weights available in just three weeks, after safety testing is complete.

“In the meantime, we’ll work with trusted partners and governments to make sure that the open source weights can be used to defend, but not to [perform] malicious attacks,” Mistral VP Science Pierre Stock told TechCrunch.

Security concerns have been mounting in recent months, particularly among Mistral’s core audience — enterprises and institutions. At the same time, an open-weight model is easier to audit, Stock said.

Another important behind-the-scenes aspect is that ML4 was trained entirely on Mistral’s compute; using only 4,000 Nvidia GPUs “which is two to three times less than our Chinese competitors, and significantly less than the closed source competitors,” Stock said.

With benchmark results still pending, Mistral hopes ML4 will be best in class among open-weight models, especially outside of China, but not only, Stock said. Thanks to focused training, it could also outperform closed models in specific areas that are key to its customers, and where multimodal capabilities can add value.

According to Stock, ML4’s optimized use cases include cybersecurity and finance, but also chip design, which is core to two of Mistral’s main backers — Dutch giant ASML, which led its Series C, and Samsung, which led its Series D last month at a €21 billion valuation (about $24.39 billion).

At the time, the company tried to convey that its decision to host Chinese models wasn’t a pivot into becoming a mere inference provider. With Le Chonk in its corner, the company believes it should still be considered a frontier lab as well.

Tech.title: Pinterest’s AI now turns beauty Pins into action plans
Tech.content:
In Brief

Pinterest on Tuesday showed off a new feature that will leverage AI to take action on your saved inspiration from beauty-related Pins, like hair and nail ideas, and turn them into actionable plans you can take with you to the salon.

“Beauty Guides,” which are powered by the company’s visual intelligence and generative AI technology, Pinterest Intelligence, will translate Pins into terms and phrases used by stylists and nail artists that everyday users may not know, like “balayage,” “root melt,” or “almond nails.”

The feature is a small but practical way to introduce AI into users’ everyday lives, as it slots into something that people are already doing: bringing a photo of their inspiration to the salon. That’s useful to a large extent, but having the right terminology at hand while you discuss what parts of the look you want to edit or change can be useful as well.

Plus, the guides offer the sort of information that can help users plan for their visit, like the time each part of the process may take and the cost. (Balayage goes into the hundreds of dollars, so that’s information you might like to have up front!)

Image Credits:Pinterest

The action guides will show up when you tap on the “Get the Guide” button within the app, and will then offer details about what, specifically, you should ask for to achieve the same look, the time it takes, price range, and maintenance requirements, like how often you’ll need to trim, tone, or touch up, for instance.

At launch, the feature will work across Pins related to hairstyle, color, nail shape, and finish.

Tech.title: Uber is spending $2.3B to get into catering
Tech.content:
In Brief

Uber is buying a catering company called ezCater, as it continues to grow the types of services available through its Uber Eats division. It’s an all-cash transaction valued at $2.3 billion.

Billed as a “leading U.S. platform for catering and workplace meals,” ezCater is a marketplace for businesses that need large meals, like an Expedia for catering. The company was founded in 2007 and has become a business that generated over $2.5 billion in gross bookings over the last 12 months, according to Uber. It’s a huge exit for a company that was bootstrapped for seven years before raising its first $4 million round in 2014.

Dara Khosrowshahi, Uber’s CEO, billed the acquisition as a way for restaurants to find new, larger customers. “Catering is a big business, and can be a huge revenue stream for restaurants,” he said in a statement. “With Uber’s reach, we can bring that experience to millions more customers and help restaurants win more of these valuable orders.”

The acquisition is the latest in a run of moves by Uber to grow its food delivery business. The company is also in the process of buying Delivery Hero for $15 billion, and it’s investing in (and partnering with) drone delivery companies like Zipline and Flytrex.

Tech.title: A New Neurotech Startup Launches to Rival Sam Altman’s Merge Labs
Tech.content:
Sam Altman-backed Merge Labs has a new competitor in the race to build a brain-computer interface powered by ultrasound. Bridge Neurotech is launching with $13.5 million in funding, including from venture firm General Catalyst, which has also backed major tech companies such as Anduril, Anthropic, Airbnb, and Stripe.

The company is the latest in a growing field of startups that aim to translate signals from the brain into useful actions. Elon Musk’s Neuralink, plus Synchron, Paradromics, and Precision Neuroscience are all working on brain-computer interfaces to help people who have lost the ability to move or speak.

These approaches all require surgery of some kind, which is why Bridge founder and CEO Will Biederman says he struck out on his own. “It fundamentally comes down to a difference in vision,” he says.

Biederman developed the chip Neuralink licensed to use in its first devices as part of his PhD work, but his goal with Bridge is to build a wearable device that could be used by far more people than a brain implant. Only 100 or so people around the world have received an implanted brain-computer interface as part of clinical trials, including at least 21 volunteers who have gotten Neuralink’s device.

“The risks of neurosurgery really cannot be minimized or dismissed, and so the level of safety and benefit that these devices must deliver really is quite high,” Biederman says. “Nobody really wants a hole in their head.”

But wearable brain-computer interfaces have suffered from poor signal quality. Bone and skin weaken electrical signals before they reach external sensors, which affects the performance of a device. It’s why most companies are recording electrical impulses directly from neurons in the brain. Neuralink and others have shown that these electrical systems can allow paralyzed people the ability to control electronic devices, move robotic arms, and communicate in real time with just their thoughts.

Bridge Neurotech thinks ultrasound offers an alternative to current implants and external sensors. Ultrasound uses high-frequency sound waves to bounce off moving red blood cells and measure the speed and direction of blood flow. In the brain, fluctuations in blood flow closely follow neural activity.

Both Bridge Neurotech and Merge Labs have ties to Arbor Neuroscience, which was previously known as Forest Neurotech, a nonprofit founded in 2023 by Biederman and fellow researchers Sumner Norman and Tyson Aflalo to pursue “work that is too integrated and long-horizon for a single academic lab, and too early for a company.” The organization built an instrument that uses ultrasound to image brain function that is in trials in the UK.

Tech.title: Mistral Says Its New AI Model ‘Le Chonk’ Is the Best Open-Weight Offering Outside of China
Tech.content:
As tensions mount over who gets access to top-end artificial intelligence, French company Mistral has released a new freely available model that it claims can compete with the very best from the US and China.

The new 1 trillion-parameter model, Mistral Large 4—nicknamed Le Chonk—can be used and customized by anyone. It’s currently available in preview, with a final version to follow by the end of the month. Though Le Chonk is built to compete with leading general-purpose models, it’s optimized specifically for coding and cyberdefense, as well as tasks particular to manufacturing, finance, electrical engineering, and other niches.

“There are a lot of areas where the other labs will not focus that much,” Guillaume Lample, cofounder and chief scientist at Mistral, tells WIRED. “There are so many domains in which you can improve models.”

Mistral presents Le Chonk as by far the most capable open-weight model developed outside of China, and “very, very close” to some proprietary models. Whereas Chinese labs have been accused by the US government of abusing distillation—the training of a smaller model on the outputs of a larger one—to close the performance gap with OpenAI and Anthropic, Mistral claims to have trained its model from scratch.

It’s already considerably cheaper for businesses to run open-weight models, which cost only as much as the compute they consume. By reducing the performance gap on leading proprietary models and providing a competitive alternative to releases from China, Mistral says, Le Chonk will eliminate the few remaining reasons a business might hesitate to choose open source.

Tech.title: A First Ride With Lightfoot, a Solar-Powered Scooter
Tech.content:
Almost everyone who sees it says it looks ridiculous, but in a fun, whimsical sort of way. No doubt that's why its maker dubs it the “smile machine.” No other vehicle I've ever ridden has commanded this much attention. People have commented on the Lightfoot at traffic lights and even mid-ride, where several cyclists precariously pulled out their phones to take photos.

The Lightfoot hails from Otherlab, a research and design company founded by inventor Saul Griffith, who also cofounded Rewiring America, a nonprofit that helps US households switch from fossil fuels to clean energy. Griffith tells WIRED that the project started several years ago after publicly available data showed that 52 percent of all US passenger trips across all modes of transportation were less than three miles. Instead of relying on a car, why not try a simpler vehicle for short trips that can also recharge itself during the day?

“Solar can make a meaningful contribution. There's a nice pathway here for an easy vehicle that people really engage with that's simple and robust,” Griffith says.

Making it a scooter instead of a bike gives it a broader appeal too. “I think for every one person who wants something with pedals, there's nine people who don't give a fuck about pedals,” Griffith says.

Lightfoot Specs Speed: 20 mph

20 mph Power: Dual 750-watt brushless hub motors

Dual 750-watt brushless hub motors Battery: 1.5 kW

1.5 kW Range: 37 miles

37 miles Solar: Dual 120W panels

Dual 120W panels Rider height: 5'2" to 6'2"

5'2" to 6'2" Weight: 137 pounds

137 pounds Max payload: 419 pounds

I've been living with the Lightfoot for a little over two weeks. Unfortunately, for most of that time, New York City has been facing heavy rainfall—with a nor'easter sprinkled in. Not ideal conditions for a solar-powered scooter. That's why Otherlab is initially focusing on selling its $4,495 vehicle in California—it's now officially on sale (in sky blue or solar orange), and you can reserve one for $100.

Eventually, Griffith says, the company plans to expand into more southern states, beelining toward the Sunshine State, Florida, then gauging interest in northern states. Griffith says the company is talking to resorts, campuses, and fleet managers and plans to sell the Lightfoot in countries like Vietnam, where Hanoi will heavily restrict gas-powered scooters starting in 2027. But that's the larger vision—for now, the focus is to produce enough vehicles and get them to initial customers first.

“If you look at the bloodbath that is people who've done micromobility companies, they nearly all raised too much money and tried to be gigantic immediately,” Griffith says. “We just didn't want to do that.” He says that the first couple of production runs should prove that people like the Lightfoot and allow the company to study how people are using it.

Part of that involves servicing, and Griffith says the company wants to establish a service infrastructure as it expands. However, he points out that the Lightfoot uses common off-the-shelf components that should make repairs easy for most mom-and-pop bike shops (after removing the solar panels).

More evidence that the Lightfoot isn't built for New York City? If you're facing a slew of cloudy days, the only other way to charge it is by plugging it directly into an outlet. You cannot remove the battery. Also, the 137-pound vehicle is designed to be parked outside, meaning you'll need access to a power source that can reach the sidewalk or your patio. I'm lucky enough to have a secure backyard space with an outlet, so I was able to top it up despite the cloudy conditions.

Tech.title: Spotify’s New Music Quiz Will Test Your Trivia Knowledge
Tech.content:
How well do you know your music trivia? Music streaming service Spotify has unveiled a new mobile feature called Music Quiz that tests fans’ knowledge of over 2,000 artists. It’s rolling out to the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and a handful of other countries from Tuesday.

The shareable quiz, which follows a BTS quiz earlier in the year, features music trivia, album cover art and audio tracks spanning an artist’s music and milestones. Fans can share their scores for each artist’s quiz with friends, like the popular New York Times puzzle Wordle.

There are quizzes for artists including Bad Bunny, Don Toliver, Bruno Mars and Charli xcx.

More from CNET



How to use the Spotify Music Quiz

To find a music quiz, you have to go to the individual artist’s page.

First, make sure your Spotify app is up to date.

Next, play a track from the artist, and a Music Quiz card will pop up in their profile.

The app will then ask a series of questions about the artist and their music, and once you’ve finished, you can share your score on various social media and messaging apps.

Spotify is the world’s largest music streaming service, with over 300 million paid subscribers. It frequently experiments with new ways of engaging its users, including snapshots of your music streaming history, AI-driven personalization options, a Running Mode for your workouts and the popular Wrapped yearly summary.

Tech.title: I’ve Been Testing Kitchen Gear for Years. Here Are 4 Prime Day Deals I’m Texting to Friends
Tech.content:
Amazon’s October Prime sales are a chance to outfit your kitchen with sought-after items without paying full price. With everything more expensive, you’d be wise to take advantage of discounts if you’re hoping to upgrade your coffee maker, air fryer, blender and other helpful cooking equipment.

There’s a lot to parse, with thousands of deals on Amazon and plenty of knock-offs that look tempting but may not be worth it even at a discount. I’ve been testing kitchen gear for years and know how to spot a great kitchen deal through the smoke and mirrors. Of the hundreds I sifted through, these are the four I’d recommend to friends, family or anyone gift shopping for a home cook — established or aspiring.

Vitamix $295 (save $205) Vitamix Propel Series 510 blender Get it now $295 at Amazon Expert Take All Vitamix blenders pack big power, but the Propel Series has a little extra — at least compared to the VX series (formerly called the Explorian). It has 2.2 peak horsepower, so it can handle just about anything you drop inside. Unlike the manual-only VX, the Propel has three built-in automatic programs for smoothies, frozen desserts and hot soups for hands-off blending. It’s also one of the quietest and lightest Vitamix blenders, which makes it feel user-friendly. These blenders aren’t cheap, but as CNET’s Anna Gragert, who uses a 19-year-old Vitamix without issue, can attest, they really last. Bottom Line This is the cheapest we've ever seen the Vitamix Propel 510 drop on Amazon. The powerful blender retails for $500 with an average tag of $433 on Amazon. It's only been down to $300 twice before during flash sales. It comes with a five-year warranty.

Pamela Vachon/CNET $153 (save $27) Ninja Crispi glass-bowl air fryer Get it now $153 at Amazon $153 at Best Buy Expert Take Simply put, this is the best air fryer we’ve tested, and it’s currently at its lowest price ever on Amazon. The Crispi broke the air fryer mold when it launched, with a modular build that’s easier to store and a glass bowl cooking chamber that’s easy to clean and PFAS-free. If you’ve used a nonstick air fryer basket, you know how quickly it accumulates a layer of gunk that’s hard to remove. Not so with the Crispi. As a bonus, the cooking chamber comes with a tight-fitting lid that makes storing leftover food simple and intuitive. The Crispi has as much power as you’ll ever need from an air fryer and features uncomplicated cooking controls. If there is one ding on this model, it’s that the cooking chamber is lower than some we’ve tested, meaning you might struggle to fit a whole chicken or large cut of meat without breaking it down first. For more cooking capacity, try the Ninja Crispi Pro — also on sale for Prime Day. Bottom Line Our favorite air fryer at its lowest price ever on Amazon — what's not to love? The Ninja Crispi has significant advantages over pod-style nonstick air fryers, and thanks to its outsized popularity, it rarely goes on sale.

Technivorm $270 (save $100) Technivorm Moccamaster KBGV coffee maker Get it now $270 at Crate & Barrel Expert Take The Dutch coffee maker company Technivorm has sold exceptional brewers for decades, earning it cult status among coffee snobs. The KBGV drip coffee machine has clean lines and sharp angles that give off both a vintage and laboratory feel. Retro design aside, in our testing, this brewer consistently delivers perfectly balanced coffee, heating water up to a precise temperature as it hits the grounds. Bottom Line Technivorm's brewers often sell for $400, so snatching up one of its most popular models for $270 is a no-brainer if you were already planning to upgrade your home setup. The KBGV is currently listed for $366 on Amazon and seldom drops below $300.

Ninja/CNET $88 (save $42) Ninja Blendboss personal blender Get it now $88 at Amazon Expert Take The BlendBoss is the latest addition to Ninja’s blender lineup, and it quickly became our top pick. When we tested it against several others, we found it pulverized ice into snow in 15 seconds — as fast as any — and made quick work of turning dense frozen fruit into healthy smoothies. The blender comes in a range of colors — great for gifting — and has a quirky design unlike any other personal blender I’ve seen. Bottom Line This is one of few times the BlendBoss has been discounted since it launched earlier this year. The small and powerful blender typically sells for $130 but it's down to $88 for Prime Day.

What’s the single best kitchen deal?

That largely depends on your kitchen needs. For me, the powerful Vitamix Propel 510 for $295 is simply one of the best prices we’ve seen on any of the brand’s iconic blenders in some time. I fully expect that deal to expire or sell out long before Prime Day ends.



More from CNET

Is Prime Day a good time to buy kitchen gadgets?

Absolutely. The kitchen category really pops off during Prime Day sales, and we’re seeing discounts of 40% to 60% on some of our favorite gear, making them easy to recommend right now. The next opportunity to save big will be Black Friday, but price hikes can happen at any time, so there’s no guarantee we’ll see deals as good as today’s again.

Tech.title: Are the Early Holiday Sales Full of Fake Discounts? What to Know Before Shopping This Week
Tech.content:
Early holiday sales are here, even though the holidays are a couple of months away.

Amazon, Best Buy and Walmart are just a few of the stores offering discounts and limited-time deals on popular gifts like tech, kitchen gadgets and toys. Is now the time to buy your holiday must-haves at a steep discount, or are retailers inflating the original price, tacking on a flashing sale badge and fooling you with a fake discount? Here’s what our shopping expert thinks.

Yes, early holiday sales are worth it

You may seem excited about getting a good deal on a laptop or headphones, but some retailers have a way of making the deal look enticing, even though it’s not. And some US adults are getting hip to that. CNET’s latest holiday shopping survey found that US adults are prepared for holiday shopping frustrations like fake or misleading discounts (43%) and inflated baseline costs (35%). Other shopping pains include deals selling out instantly (39%) and higher prices for outdated tech (33%).

More from CNET

James Bricknell, CNET’s managing editor for deals, broke down how some retailers may try to show a deep discount that isn’t quite true — also known as inflating baseline or original prices.

“Often, retailers will not inflate the price per se, but will inflate the recommended retail price to suggest the product sells for more than it does,” said Bricknell. “This makes the discount feel larger, when it may only be 5% or 10% off.”

But that doesn’t mean you shouldn’t ignore holiday sales. It could be one way to save on a new device you’re considering, like a laptop or headphones — even if it’s not a deep discount. While some savings may be only 10 or 20%, they could still help shave off some of the cost and avoid paying full price.

But with some retailers adjusting prices to falsify savings, how do you really know you’re getting a deal?

How to spot a good deal during holiday sales

Typically, early holiday sales yield savings on tech but you’ll need to create a plan and do some research before the sales start.

Over the years, CNET has done the work to determine if sales are worth it and shared the best deals on popular tech items. We use several data sources to see when a product is truly on sale, compare the new price with a 90-day average, and share them during big sales, along with expert insight on some of the most popular gadgets to help you shop confidently.

You can take some of the same steps as our deals team by comparing prices across retailers to find the biggest savings.

“Don’t assume the first place you see has the best sale; shop around to make sure the sale price seems legit,” Bricknell said.

If you’re worried about secretly higher prices, Bricknell recommends checking the brand’s official website for the base price. Once you find a good deal, use a price tracker like CamelCamelCamel or Keepa to see historical pricing and determine whether it’s worth buying now or waiting.

Chrome’s Shopping Insights browser extension lets you bookmark a page and track a price. Google says that trackable products are saved to your Shopping list folder by default, too. And now Safari’s Notify Me tool is a built-in tool that can track webpage changes, including price drops. CNET also has a price comparison extension, though it’s probably faster to find what you want through our big roundups of deals during sales.

Bricknell added that if a deal seems too good to be true, it probably is. “A deep discount of 50% or 75% on something that normally costs hundreds is something to be wary of.”

Tech.title: I Played Switch Sports Resort: Motion Gaming Is Still Nintendo’s Secret Weapon
Tech.content:
I pulled back my arms to aim and fired arrows into multicolored targets in an archery-meets-darts game, side by side with NPR games editor James Perkins Mastromarino. I played him in thumb wrestling, wiggling my little Joy-Con for leverage. I skateboarded across Wuhu Island by sliding the Joy-Con controller in mouse mode on my leg. I flew a plane around by aiming it in the air like a model airplane. My arms got tired, and I thought: Nintendo needs more of this. So do I.

It was a total throwback to play a bit of Nintendo’s upcoming $50 Switch Sports Resort game again. The Switch 2 exclusive arrives Oct. 22, but I got to check out nine of the 12 games in an early preview in New York. While I knew what to expect, I didn’t think I’d love it all again as much as I did. And, once again, I marveled that Nintendo has a whole doorway to motion gaming that still feels untapped.

Outside of the motion-focused viral phenomenon Nex Playground console, and VR gaming that leans on motion controls nearly constantly, the gaming world doesn’t touch active gaming much. Except, that is, for Nintendo.

More from CNET

Nintendo dips into motion games from time to time, emerging like a phoenix at odd moments. The original Wii Sports Resort came out way back in 2009 (when I was just starting out at CNET, and played it with then-colleague Jeff Bakalar). The game was also the debut of a more advanced motion-sensing add-on to the Wii controllers that allowed gyro-based movement.

Fitness Boxing and Just Dance have been Switch standards for years, and I loved Ring Fit Adventure, a game that CNET’s Bridget Carey reminded me needs a comeback for Switch 2. Mario Party has motion game modes, too. But Switch Sports Resort is Nintendo’s most complete motion party package of them all.

Flying around the island (or skating or jetskiiing) feels like a whole other mode, in a good way. Nintendo

Switch Sports came out for the Switch four years ago, and Resort is the better game. It has more activities (12 compared to eight on Switch Sports), plus it has a large island chain similar to the old game Pilotwings that can be flown through, or jet-skied around, or skateboarded across. In the free-moving modes, there are little extras to collect and secret items to grab. In sports modes, it’s all about competition.

I only got a taste of the surprises in store, but Switch Sports Resort has additions compared to the older Wii game. Skateboarding, which uses the Joy-Con in a mouse-based mode to slide over surfaces similar to the standalone Drag x Drive, tired my arms but was fun to slide around for a while. Thumb wrestling’s also new. It’s sort of absurd that thumb wrestling has been made into a game when it’s so easy to play for real, but the Switch 2 version almost feels like a simple thumb-based Punch-Out with tilting and power increases where you hold your thumb down to make it bigger and slam your opponent better (while hoping they don’t pin you first).

New this time: thumb wrestling! Weird, but fun. Nintendo

Some games are Switch Sports repeats, like Bowling, but this version adds a 100-pin mode that Wii Sports Resort lacked. Archery also has a new darts-like competitive score-based game compared to the Wii Sports Resort version. There’s also a single-player tournament mode where you can take on NPC players in tiered matches. I’m sure there are other secrets afoot, knowing Nintendo.

But the same-room multiplayer is where this game’s clearly meant to shine. And it made me get a little excited about trying this at home soon, too. Switch Sports Resort gives me just enough of that nearly VR-like motion gaming feel that brings me into headsets again and again, but in front of a TV, with others, goofing around, like the old Wii days. I miss the old familiar feeling that suddenly seemed new again.

I’ll have more thoughts when I do a review, but in the meantime, a question for Nintendo: How about some new motion games, too?

Tech.title: What Is ChatGPT? Everything You Need to Know About the AI Assistant
Tech.content:
ChatGPT is the artificial intelligence chatbot that brought generative AI into the mainstream.

Launched in November 2022 by OpenAI, the company co-founded by Sam Altman, ChatGPT quickly became the most popular AI application, and the one everyone tried to emulate and one-up.

Since then, all the big tech players have joined the generative AI race. Perplexity, Meta AI, Google’s Gemini, Microsoft’s Copilot, Grok and Anthropic’s Claude can all do similar things. But ChatGPT’s popularity and early start gave it a strong lead.

More from CNET

ChatGPT became one of the fastest-growing apps in history, amassing over 1 billion users. It often stands out for its versatility and ease of use, but mostly for the sheer scale of its user base.

This AI assistant is now far beyond the familiar prompt-and-answer chatbot. You can ask it to generate images, write and debug code, build a website, help you understand your medical records and even plan your next Starbucks order. It can also research a topic in depth and handle multistep jobs, using apps and browsing the web to get things done.

The tricky part can be figuring out which version does what — and whether you need to pay for it.

Let’s see how exactly ChatGPT works, how to use it and what you get for free or with a subscription.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, CNET’s parent company, in 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

How does ChatGPT work?

ChatGPT is built on a transformer architecture, a type of neural network that identifies relationships between words. Its name comes from GPT, short for generative pre-trained transformer.

OpenAI says its models are developed and trained on massive amounts of data from publicly available internet content alongside partner licensing deals, user interactions and data generated by human trainers and researchers.

ChatGPT’s large language models learn patterns from training data and use those, along with your prompt and the conversation, to generate responses. That’s one reason why it sometimes hallucinates or generates confident-sounding but incorrect information.

Sometimes it does it so convincingly and naturally that you might forget it’s not actually thinking.

ChatGPT/Screenshot by CNET

Afraz Jaffri, a senior director analyst at Gartner, says he thinks ChatGPT’s biggest flaw is that “They’re just unreliable. So even if I ask something and I get a response, I still want to check that that is actually true, which kind of defeats the point of us getting it in the first place.”

Jaffri says those mistakes now happen less often than they did in the early days of ChatGPT, though.

“The advancements in the things put around the model that turn it into an agentic system in ChatGPT, that allow it to take actions, search, verify and try multiple approaches, mean that its utility beyond simple question answering has drastically improved,” Jaffri tells CNET.

ChatGPT can search the web and cite sources, making its answers easier to fact-check. But it doesn’t mean you shouldn’t do it.

Where can you use ChatGPT?

You can easily access ChatGPT through a web browser or via its apps on Android and iOS devices.

It has also been integrated into Apple products via Apple Intelligence and Siri. OpenAI’s Microsoft Office add-in puts ChatGPT inside Word, Excel and PowerPoint, where it can help edit documents, explain formulas and build presentations.

OpenAI also lets you interact with ChatGPT via phone calls and messages. You can call 800-CHATGPT from a US or Canadian number. WhatsApp messaging is available to users with EEA numbers through the verified contact at 800-242-8478. Access is based on your number’s country code.

What can you do with ChatGPT?

There are many use cases for ChatGPT. It can plan your vacations, practice job interview questions with you, help you with your budgeting and translating, write your resume, do your meal planning, draft emails, summarize long documents, develop business strategies and just have a conversation with you. It’ll learn from your inquiries and requests, and tailor itself to what it thinks you like.

To stop OpenAI from using your chats to train its models, turn off Improve the model for everyone under Settings/Data controls. You can still keep those chats in your history.

ChatGPT/Screenshot by CNET

If you want a conversation removed from your history, start a Temporary chat (in the upper-right corner). It won’t add or change memories or be used for training, though OpenAI may keep a copy for up to 30 days for safety.

Temporary chats can still use what ChatGPT already knows about you. Choose Unpersonalized to stop it from using existing memories, custom instructions and plugins. If you save the chat later, your regular account settings apply.

Deep research takes more time to investigate a question and put together a report with citations. You can steer its research toward particular websites, give it your own files and change its plan before it starts.

If you don’t feel like it or can’t type your prompt, you can talk to ChatGPT, too. Live voice lets you verbally interrupt ChatGPT mid-answer and ask it to use connected apps. Eligible subscribers can also share their camera or screen through the separate Advanced voice option on mobile.

On supported paid plans, the MacOS app’s Record feature can transcribe and summarize a meeting. You’ll need the participants’ consent before recording.

You can also generate and edit images with ChatGPT. Image 2.5 is available across plans with different limits. You can generate pictures from descriptions or edit existing ones, like changing selected parts, removing backgrounds or even starting with a sketch.

Created by Barbara Pazur using ChatGPT

It’s a bit unusual for one of the biggest AI players, but ChatGPT can’t generate videos. OpenAI used to have the Sora video generator, but discontinued its consumer app and website in April.

OpenAI also officially shut down its Atlas AI browser in August after a very short run.

ChatGPT Health is another feature that lets eligible US adults connect supported medical records or Apple Health data to help interpret lab results and prepare questions for a doctor. It isn’t intended to diagnose conditions or recommend treatment.

If you’ve used custom GPTs, the tailored assistants people could build and share, another change is coming. OpenAI plans to retire them on Dec. 11, with plugins taking over that role. Plugins supply tools and reusable instructions for particular jobs. A plugin might let ChatGPT retrieve documents from Google Drive or work with your email, once you connect the account and grant permission.

Projects keep related chats, files and instructions together, saving you from explaining the same assignment every time. They’re available across plans and can be shared with others.

Library stores files you can reuse across conversations, including documents and images. Be aware that deleting a conversation doesn’t automatically delete a file saved in Library.

ChatGPT/Screenshot by CNET

In Tasks, you can schedule reminders or recurring requests, like a morning briefing. Eligible paid users can also trigger tasks in Work when something happens in a connected app, like a new email arriving or Slack activity.

What’s different about ChatGPT Work?

ChatGPT Work handles multistep tasks from start to finish. You might ask it to research a topic and build a presentation, then revise the slides together. It can browse websites and use connected apps as it works, then produce an editable file. You can ask for changes without starting the assignment again.

ChatGPT/Screenshot by CNET

Codex handles software development with a more technical interface. Work can also generate interactive visuals, and eligible Plus, Pro and workspace users can build websites or lightweight apps through Sites, which are currently in public beta.

OpenAI also just introduced dots, personal AI agents powered by GPT-6 Astra. You can give one an ongoing job, like keeping tabs on a project, and it can work on its own cloud computer while you’re away. You decide which apps it can use and what actions need your approval. For now, you’ll need Pro or Business Premium in an eligible market or access to the beta through an Enterprise, Edu or Healthcare account.

Dots are OpenAI’s agents. OpenAI

Different models for different functions

ChatGPT started with GPT-3.5, but today it has several GPT-5.6 and 6 models and GPT-6 Astra. Which one is best for you depends on what you’re asking it to do, your subscription and whether you’re using Chat, Work or Codex.

In regular ChatGPT, Free and Go use GPT-5.6 Luna for everyday questions, with a Think option for harder ones. Plus uses GPT-5.6 Sol. Instant thinking level gives quicker answers, while Medium and High allow more time to reason through problems.

In regular ChatGPT, Pro, Business and Enterprise add Extra High thinking level and GPT-5.6 Sol Pro for really hard tasks, along with GPT-6 Pro, powered by Astra. Usage limits apply, and workplace administrators can restrict your access.

To adjust how much time a model spends on reasoning in regular chat on Plus and Pro, you need to change the thinking effort setting yourself.

ChatGPT/Screenshot by CNET

Work and Codex give you more models to choose from than regular Chat.

ChatGPT/Screenshot by CNET

GPT-6 Astra is OpenAI’s most capable model for complex research, coding and tasks across apps. Plus subscribers can use it in Work mode with usage limits.

The newer GPT-6.1 Sol improves on GPT-6 Sol for coding and operating computers. OpenAI says it approaches Astra’s performance on those tasks and professional work. It’s rolling out in Work and Codex to Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu users, but isn’t available in regular Chat.

The next incremental model update for ChatGPT is here. OpenAI

Other choices include GPT-6 Luna for quicker, focused jobs such as summaries and GPT-5.6 Terra for everyday assignments. GPT-6 Luna also remains exclusive to Work and Codex.

Work and Codex offer GPT-6 Sol for complex coding and tasks involving tools, GPT-5.6 Terra for everyday assignments and GPT-6 Luna for quicker tasks. GPT-6 Sol and Luna aren’t available in regular Chat.

Astra and AGI chatter

Astra’s arrival also stirred up talk of artificial general intelligence, or AGI, meaning AI with human-level abilities across intellectual tasks. OpenAI President Greg Brockman suggested it marked an “AGI era.” Whether that stands to be true remains debatable.

Jaffri says Astra is one of the most capable models available, alongside Claude Opus 5.5, with its biggest gains in operating computers and coding, particularly spotting security vulnerabilities.

Jaffri also points to a trade-off in its reduced use of reasoning tokens, which help trace a model’s decisions.

“Reducing the number of tokens means that the price per task of the model can be reduced, but at the cost of reduced explainability,” Jaffri tells CNET. Without understanding what models are doing, he warns, making them safe could prove to be impossible.

ChatGPT pricing

You can do plenty without subscribing. The free plan includes everyday text chats and limited access to tools such as image generation and deep research. Free and Go users also get limited Work access on desktop.

US prices start at $8 a month for Go, which increases allowances for tools and uploads. Plus costs $20 per month and adds more capable models, with Work across desktop, web and mobile.

Pro now comes in $100, $200 and $500 monthly tiers. Yes, that’s $500 per month. The new Pro 500 plan gives you 25 times Plus’s Work and Codex allowance and access to Astra Ultrafast for faster responses, though that speed burns through your allowance faster, too. Work and Codex share usage limits separate from regular Chat.

There’s less welcome news for $200 Pro subscribers — the price stays put, but the allowance is shrinking. The plan has reopened to new subscribers with lower limits. Eligible existing subscribers keep their old limits through Oct. 29, then their Work and Codex allowance drops from 20 times to 10 times Plus’s. Their GPT-6 Pro messages in Chat also fall from 200 to 100 per week.

To soften the blow, OpenAI says affected subscribers will receive a one-time grant of 62,500 usage credits, valued at $2,500. But there’s a catch: those credits expire on Dec. 31.

Business costs $25 per user per month, with a minimum of two users. Enterprise and Edu have custom pricing.

Free and Go plans may show ads in supported regions. Plus and the higher tiers are ad-free. OpenAI says ads don’t influence answers and advertisers can’t read your chats.

Lawsuit after lawsuit, and other controversies

ChatGPT faces ongoing legal challenges related to industry concerns regarding the ethics and the legality of data sourcing for AI training. High-profile lawsuits against OpenAI and other technology companies include those from major publishers like The New York Times, Dow Jones and CNET’s parent company Ziff Davis (see the disclosure above), which allege unauthorized use of their content to train AI tools, as do many individual authors.

In June, Florida sued OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging that the company concealed serious risks, including dangers to minors. The lawsuit cited allegations that ChatGPT helped the gunman plan the 2025 Florida State University shooting.

In another lawsuit, the parents of a 19-year-old allege that ChatGPT’s advice about mixing drugs led to his fatal accidental overdose in May 2025. OpenAI says those conversations involved an older version of ChatGPT that it has since retired, and that it has strengthened its safeguards.

Amid lawsuits alleging ChatGPT contributed to several deaths, OpenAI introduced Trusted Contact in May. The optional feature lets adults choose a consenting friend or family member to be notified (after human review) if their chats raise serious concerns about potential self-harm or suicide.

OpenAI began rolling out ChatGPT for Teens on Aug. 18, giving younger users help with studying, reminders to take breaks and added protection from potentially harmful content. Parents can also opt in to parental controls by linking accounts to manage settings and set quiet hours, though they can’t read their teen’s conversations.

In June, cybersecurity firm Mindgard reported that variations of a viral “restore this photo” prompt tricked ChatGPT into generating sexually explicit and graphically violent images.

OpenAI has also acknowledged breaches involving Hugging Face and Australian government systems during internal testing of experimental models. Jaffri warns that these incidents now show that “the technology itself creates a risk to society.”

“The main fear is that these agents may reach a level where they can improve themselves by updating their own models, without needing human supervision or interaction, known as recursive self-improvement,” Jaffri tells CNET.

That’s why AI labs have adopted “pacing,” Jaffri says. This means slowing development to give themselves more time to find reliable ways to test new models.

ChatGPT is one of the default interfaces for how people interact with AI and even how they get information from the internet.

“The whole kind of technology itself is going to be transformative for a lot of different areas, which will have a direct impact on our lives,” Jaffri says. “Hopefully for the better.”

If you feel like you or someone you know is in immediate danger, call 911 (or your country’s local emergency line) or go to an emergency room to get immediate help. Explain that it is a psychiatric emergency and ask for someone who is trained for these kinds of situations. If you’re struggling with negative thoughts or suicidal feelings, resources are available to help. In the US, call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988.

Tech.title: How to Disable Some Apple Intelligence Features on Your iPhone or Mac and Reclaim Valuable Space
Tech.content:
Apple launched iOS 27 and MacOS 27 in September, and those updates introduced a revamped Siri AI powered by Apple Intelligence to Apple devices. While the new Siri was better at most tasks in my testing, it can still take up a significant amount of on-device storage space. On my iPhone, for example, it takes up about 6.4 GB of data, while it takes up about 17.9 GB of space on my MacBook Neo.

If you aren’t using the new AI features, you can disable some of them, and depending on what system you’re on, you can reclaim some of that valuable storage space. That way you can stave off for a little while the dreaded pop-up that tells you your storage is full – I need that extra storage for photos of my wife, son and dog.

Here’s how to see how much storage Apple Intelligence is taking up on your devices and how to disable – or at least limit – it on different operating systems. And don’t forget, Apple Intelligence is only available on certain devices.

How much space is Apple Intelligence taking up on your device?

How much space Apple Intelligence is taking up on your device is easy to check. If you’re on iPhone, go to Settings > General > iPhone Storage > iOS. From here, look for the Apple Intelligence tab to see how much space it takes up on your iPhone.

On a MacBook, click the Apple logo in the top-left corner of your screen, then go to System Settings > General > Storage, and click the i next to MacOS. A new pop-up will open to show you how much space Apple Intelligence uses on your MacBook.

How to disable Apple Intelligence on your iPhone

Disabling Apple Intelligence on your iPhone that’s running iOS 27 or later is straightforward. Go to Settings > Siri > Turn Off Siri and follow the on-screen prompts. You can then go back and check your storage, and Apple Intelligence should be gone from that menu.

Disabling Siri AI can free up a few gigabytes on iOS 27. CNET

If you’re running iOS 26, you can disable Apple Intelligence by going to Settings > Apple Intelligence & Siri and tapping the toggle next to Apple Intelligence. This should free up some space on your iPhone.

You might also have to disable other Apple Intelligence features across your iPhone. To do this, go to Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy Restrictions and tap the toggle next to Content & Privacy Restrictions. Then, tap Intelligence & Siri. From here, you’ll need to tap into Image Creation, Writing Tools and Intelligence Extensions and tap Don’t Allow in each one.

This should free up a few gigabytes of space on your iPhone.

You can free up a few gigabytes of space in iOS 26 by disabling Apple Intelligence features. CNET

How to disable Apple Intelligence on your Mac

Disabling Apple Intelligence and freeing up storage space on your device can be weird, depending on which operating system you’re using. For instance, if you’re on MacOS 26, it’s easy to disable the feature and free up space. If you’re on MacOS 27, it’s a little more complicated.

We’ll start off with the easy one. To disable Apple Intelligence on MacOS 26, first click the Apple logo in the top left corner of your screen. Then go to System Settings > Apple Intelligence & Siri and click to toggle next to Apple Intelligence. That should free up a few gigabytes of data on your device.

Disabling Apple Intelligence on MacOS 26 frees up a little bit of storage. CNET

There are a couple of potential ways to disable Apple Intelligence on MacOS 27. The easiest way I found to free up a few gigabytes of space is to click the Apple logo in the top-left corner of your screen, then go to System Settings > Siri and change your language to something like English (Irish). Siri AI isn’t available in every region yet, so changing your Siri language to a language from one of those regions could trick your device. Granted, it freed up only about 4 GB for me.

I changed my Siri language, and it freed up a few gigabytes of space. CNET

CNET’s sister site PCMag has a more in-depth way of turning off Apple Intelligence and freeing up some space. However, I couldn’t get this method to work. I’m not sure why I couldn’t get this method to work, other than that my device is running MacOS 27.0.1 and not MacOS 27. Maybe this will work for you, though.

According to PCMag, you have to go to System Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy. Then, toggle Content & Privacy off. Click Siri and change it to Siri Classic. Then go through the list of Capabilities and turn each feature off.

You’re not finished yet. Then, go to System Settings > Siri and select Don’t Allow Siri or Siri Classic.

Finally, you’ll need to go into individual Apple Intelligence settings and disable those features. Some easy ones include going to System Settings > Notifications > Summarize Notifications and turning the toggle off, or going to System Settings > Messages > Settings and turning off Message Summaries.

You could do all that work, or you could just switch your Siri language as I did. The choice is yours.

For more iOS news, here’s what to know about iOS 27 and iOS 27.0.1.

Tech.title: A Surface Laptop Ultra? What to Expect for Microsoft’s Oct. 7 Event
Tech.content:
After a summer full of folding iPhones and Googlebooks, Microsoft is getting ready for a new laptop-centered event this week. The company is hosting a Windows and Surface event on Wednesday in San Francisco, its first laptop event in two years. This is everything we’re expecting to see — and no, sorry, Windows 12 is not on the list.

The event will be a “conversation on how local AI will shape the next chapter of the PC,” according to Microsoft. That makes sense as Microsoft has been all-in on AI by incorporating Copilot everywhere and partnering with chip makers like Qualcomm to bring enough firepower to its devices to handle the computational load of generative and agentic AI tasks. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and the head of Windows and Devices, Pavan Davuluri, are slated to speak.

This event could be when Microsoft actually drops the Surface Laptop Ultra, a 15-inch high-end variant first announced this spring at Computex. The Ultra is powered by Nvidia’s new RTX Spark chip, so Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s slated appearance at the event is another sign toward the Ultra.

More from CNET

We already got two new Surface laptops this month, previewed at Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Summit. At the Hawaii event, Microsoft upgraded its Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface 13-inch laptops, running on Snapdragon Elite X2 chips, and introduced a new Surface mouse to go along with them. The new laptops have better cameras and “embody the PC-phone marriage Qualcomm promised years ago,” CNET’s David Lumb reports.

A big question will be prices. Computer hardware companies have raised their prices across the board, from Apple to Asus and Acer, over the last year to keep up with rising manufacturing costs. AI is at least partially to blame, with advanced chips in hot demand for data centers as well as laptops and phones. Other costs, like price increases in Windows licenses during the manufacturing process, may also be contributing to higher price tags. The result, sometimes called RAMageddon, is that it’s more expensive to buy new devices.

How to watch Microsoft’s Windows and Surface event

The keynote begins at 10 a.m. PT / 1 p.m. ET on Wednesday, Oct. 7., and it’s expected to last about one hour. The event is being held in San Francisco and will be livestreamed on Window’s YouTube channel. CNET will be on the ground to bring you all the latest Microsoft news.

Tech.title: Hunt Demons All October Long in These Free PlayStation Plus Games
Tech.content:
October is a month filled with longer nights, spooky ghost stories and plenty of ghouls and monsters. If you subscribe to any PlayStation Plus plan, you can enjoy those things from the comfort of your cozy home by playing Hunt: Showdown 1896 from now until Nov. 2.

PlayStation Plus, which is Sony’s version of Xbox Game Pass, offers a large, constantly expanding library of games. Subscribers can choose from the Essential, Extra and Premium tiers, each with unique perks and benefits. Starting at $11 per month, the plans give subscribers access to monthly games and rewards, and each month, all subscribers can access a handful of games at no additional charge.

Here are the games all PlayStation Plus subscribers can play this month.

Hunt: Showdown 1896

Danger lurks around every corner in this player-versus-player extraction shooter set in an alternate 19th century. You can play as a bounty hunter with up to two others searching for one of six demons across four open-world maps, or you can fight against other players for loot. No matter what, you should have a wicked good time.

F1 25

The officially licensed video game of the 2025 FIA Formula One Championship is coming to PlayStation Plus. Two new teams joined the F1 franchise in this series installment: Audi and Cadillac, the first major US car manufacturer in F1. You’ll also experience lighter, smaller cars in this installment, which presents all-new driving mechanics you’ll have to learn. Do you have what it takes to beat Lando Norris to the Drivers’ Championship?

Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2

The square Earth is in pieces… again! Giant ants, spiders, bees and other gargantuan enemies are wreaking havoc, and it’s up to you and your team to stop them. You’ll construct a team that complements your play style, build your arsenal and defend the planet. Whether you’re on a round or square planet, you’ll defend it from all threats.

For more on PlayStation Plus, here’s what to know about the gaming service. You can also check out the latest and upcoming games on Xbox Game Pass.
